title: fix(vta): rooms/owner/register signs rooms/create as the owner, so a VTC host accepts it
body:
`rooms/owner/register/0.1` had the VTA send `rooms/create` signed with its own
DID (`{vta_did}#key-0`) while naming the caller as `ownerDid`. `rooms/create`
is issued by its Owner, and every host — the VTC and room-host alike, through
`vti_rooms::authz::authorize_create` — records as owner only the party whose
proof is on the request. So every registration through the VTA was refused
unless the owner was the VTA itself, and a VTC's rooms policy then judges
creation against that signer, who must be a member of the community.

The register specification says the key holder "speaks to the host as its
principal" (actsAsSubject). It now does: the outbound `rooms/create` is
issued and signed by the owner — `ownerDid`, or the caller when absent —
through the gated key oracle as before.

The owner must be a DID this agent holds the signing key for, in a context
the caller acts in (`room_host::owner_signing_key`):

- this agent's own DID: its `#key-0`, as before;
- a did:webvh it minted: the caller must act in the DID's context; the
  method is the first `assertionMethod` entry of the DID's own stored log
  (no resolution) whose public key is an active Ed25519 record of that same
  context — matched by key bytes, so template DIDs that number their
  methods from #key-1 over records named #key-0 sign under the published id;
- a did:key: an active record with that key in a context the caller acts in.

Anything else is `permissionDenied`, worded the same whether the DID is
unknown or held for another context, and saying to name an `ownerDid` this
agent holds (a `pnm` session's did:key, held client-side, is not one). The
oracle still re-checks the key when signing. A VTA with no DID of its own can
now register rooms for owners it holds keys for.

Tests: the outbound document's issuer and proof VM are the owner's, the
proof verifies against the owner's published key, and `authorize_create`
(the rule every host applies) accepts it; an owner in another context, an
unknown DID and a client-held caller key are refused; a held did:key and the
agent's own DID sign as themselves. docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md §5.2 and the
task table say registration through the VTA signs as the owner, who must be
a member of a VTC host.

## Tests
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 5747 passed
- clippy `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and fmt clean
- vtc-service not touched. No in-process VTC test: vta-service cannot depend on vtc-service, so the test applies the host rule itself (`vti_rooms::authz::authorize_create`) to a proof verified against the owner's published key.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.31.2
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: Community-owned rooms and member offers — vtc/rooms/community/* and vtc/rooms/offers/* ([#768](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/768))

A community hosts rooms its members own, and can now own rooms itself — the
  board's papers, a working group's drafts, a members' library — run from its
  console. Design: verifiable-trust-infrastructure docs/05-design-notes/
  data-rooms-files.md §8.4.

  The community is the owner, and its own VTA is the key holder: the VTA mints
  the room's DID, signs its credentials and holds the community's place in a
  sealed room's group, through the same rooms/owner/* and rooms/keys/* tasks any
  owner's key holder serves. The community holds no room key and no group
  secret.

  Administrators, holding the new vtc.rooms.manage (the owner's authority,
  distinct from hosting's vtc.rooms.admin):
  - vtc/rooms/community/create — the VTA mints, founds the group, issues the
    community's own admin authority; the room is stored only after every
    remote step, so a failure leaves no room behind.
  - vtc/rooms/community/{list,get} — the owner's view, with counts and when the
    community's own authority lapses.
  - vtc/rooms/community/members/{add,remove,list} — add has the VTA issue the
    invitation, membership and authority credentials (never admin) and keeps
    them as an offer; remove advances a sealed room's epoch through the owner's
    group removal and says what removal does not do (no recall; an authority
    credential is honoured until it expires, so open rooms want short expiries).
    members/list is paged and separate from get, because a community library
    can admit the whole community.

  Members, on their own DID (pull-shaped admission: a member's VTA has no
  inbound address):
  - vtc/rooms/offers/list — the caller's offers and the credentials to store with
    their own key holder; never anyone else's.
  - vtc/rooms/offers/accept — on a sealed tier, a KeyPackage in and the Welcome
    out, after the VTA adds the member. A repeat with the same KeyPackage gets the
    same Welcome; an unknown outcome is admissionPending, retried safely because
    the VTA settles a pending admission first.

  Only active members of the community are admitted to its rooms. Step-up and
  consent are described as the intended model, not declared (SPEC §7.3 item 13).
  The owner's record of whom it admitted lives apart from anything the host path
  reads, so invariant I5 and portability hold.

  New shared schema vtc/_shared/0.1/community-room.schema.json. Additive for the
  generated types: new modules only.



### Specifications

- **rooms,vtc**: Rooms/owner/group/remove, and a `rooms` topic on the console's live events (vtc/admin/events 0.2) ([#767](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/767))

rooms/owner/group/remove/0.1 — the last of the owner's group tasks
  (data-rooms-files.md §11). Removal is an epoch advance and nothing else is:
  the key holder drops the member's leaf and advances the room at its host
  with the link and commit, under the caller's `admin` authority. Same
  remote-first rules as group/add as corrected in #766: the advanced state is
  kept durably before the host is contacted, applied only once the host
  accepts, discarded only on a refusal, kept on an unknown outcome and settled
  by the next request through rooms/info. At most one pending advance per room,
  admission or removal. Refuses `ownLeaf` (an owner leaving hands the room on
  with rooms/owner/transfer). States what removal does not do: no recall of
  what was read, and the authority credential is a separate thing.

  vtc/admin/events {_shared,subscribe,event} 0.2 — the topic set is closed per
  version ("a topic not listed here is a new MINOR version of this
  component"), so the `rooms` topic is a new version rather than an `ext`
  member. `rooms` prompts vtc/rooms/list, vtc/rooms/usage and
  vtc/storage/configs/list, goes to holders of vtc.rooms.admin, carries no
  count, and is hinted when a room is registered or removed or changes
  lifecycle state, when a room's usage or a storage config's held bytes
  crosses 80, 95 or 100 percent of a limit or capacity in either direction,
  and when a storage config is created, changed or changes state — naming
  none of them (data-rooms-files.md §6.3 alerts). subscribe 0.2 allows up to
  seven topics. 0.1 is unchanged; a community serving both answers each at its
  own version.

  Additive for the generated types: new modules; the TypeScript 0.1 modules
  keep exporting `Topic` (the generator now disambiguates the two shared
  definitions internally).

- **rooms**: Group/add keeps a pending admission on an unknown outcome; details schemas for group codes ([#766](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/766))

Corrections to rooms/owner/group/{create,add}/0.1 (drafts, #763), found
  implementing them in the VTA:

  - add, item 5: discard the pending admission only on a refusal. An
    unreachable or silent host is an unknown outcome — it may have accepted —
    and discarding then would leave the owner an epoch behind their own room.
    The pending admission is kept for item 6; hostUnreachable's meaning says so
    instead of "nothing was changed".
  - add, items 2-3: what is kept is the advanced group state with the link,
    commit and Welcome, beside the group the recipient holds, since a
    committer cannot process its own commit later.
  - add, item 6: the host's epoch is read with rooms/info under the caller's
    read authority, from the host the admission was sent to; a host at neither
    epoch has moved on, so discard and refuse epochConflict.
  - detailsSchema for create's alreadyExists (epoch) and add's epochConflict
    (hostEpoch), which the text already promised.
  - create, item 1: the gates on naming the key are issue-membership's, but
    nothing is signed, so a signing quota is not consumed or consulted.

- **rooms**: Rooms/owner/group/{create,add} — the owner's agent founds and grows a sealed room's group; register signs as the owner ([#763](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/763))

* spec(rooms): rooms/owner/group/{create,add} — the owner's agent founds and grows a sealed room's group; register signs as the owner

  A sealed room (`attributed`, `private`) cannot be written to until its MLS
  group exists, and every member reaches the group by a Welcome — except the
  owner, whom nobody can welcome. The member half is specified
  (`rooms/keys/{key-package,welcome,commit}`); the owner half was not, so no
  surface could found a sealed room or admit anyone to one.

  - `rooms/owner/group/create/0.1`: the owner's key holder forms the room's
    group with the owner as its only leaf, at room epoch 1 (the epoch a host
    records at registration). Entitlement: control of the room's signing key,
    as for issuing its credentials. Refuses `alreadyExists` rather than
    replacing a group whose key schedule sealed records depend on.
  - `rooms/owner/group/add/0.1`: the key holder admits a member's KeyPackage,
    advances the room at its host with `rooms/epoch/mint` (link and commit
    included, the caller's `admin` authority presented), and returns the
    Welcome for the caller to deliver with `rooms/keys/welcome` — never
    through the host. Remote first: the pending commit is kept durably, sent,
    and applied only once the host accepts, and reconciled against the host's
    epoch after a crash, since a key holder cannot process its own commit
    from the wire.
  - `rooms/owner/register/0.1` (draft, clarified in place): the key holder
    sends `rooms/create` with `ownerDid` as its issuer, signed with a key of
    that DID it holds, and never as itself; it refuses with `permissionDenied`
    before contacting the host when it holds none. `rooms/create` names the
    Owner as issuer, and a host running a creation policy (a community
    admitting rooms for its members) checks the party asking is the owner it
    names — a registration issued by the agent in another party's name is one
    no host can tell from registering rooms in a stranger's name. No schema
    change beyond the `ownerDid` description.

  Additive for the generated types: two new modules, no change to an
  existing type.

body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.31.1` → `0.31.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.31.1` → `0.31.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.31.1` → `0.31.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.31.1` → `0.31.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.31.1` → `0.31.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.31.1` → `0.31.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.31.1` → `0.31.2` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.31.1` → `0.31.2` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.26.1` → `0.26.2` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.8.2`) | `0.8.1` → `0.8.2` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.8.1` → `0.8.2` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

## `vta-sdk`

## [0.69.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-sdk-v0.68.0...vta-sdk-v0.69.0) — 2026-10-14 ### Added - **vtc**: Console Storage page, moving a room's storage, and the rooms' defaults ([#2081](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2081)) P9 part 3b (docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md §7, §8.1). - Storage (/storage, vtc.rooms.admin): every storage config with what it holds against its capacity, its credential state (never a credential) and its health; configs whose credential is `required` — as after a restore — are listed first. A config's own page probes it (optionally writing, reading back and deleting a canary) and shows each step, changes its label, capacity or default, and retires it. "New storage" creates a `local` config or an `s3` config through an external account at the community's VTA, named by its context and identifier: the form asks for nothing secret. Kinds and auth modes this build does not serve (ambient, sealed, gcs, walrus) are not offered. - A room's page gains "Send new uploads to other storage" (vtc/rooms/storage/assign/0.1). Its existing files stay where they are. - Create, update, retire and assign take the requester's operation-bound step-up and are parked for another holder of vtc.rooms.admin (§7.4); the screens say "Sent for approval" and link the action, never "Saved". Retiring the default or a config with rooms is not offered, as the VTC refuses both. - Data rooms gains a Defaults card (the design's Settings ▸ Rooms; the console has no Settings area): each room's and each member's limits, the host-wide largest file, capacity and how long a deleted file is kept, read-only, with the configuration sections that change them. To carry those defaults, vtc/rooms/list's ext["org.openvtc"].roomFiles now holds, when files are on, `defaults.{room,member}` (each byte measure capped at the host ceiling, as reported limits are), `maxFileBytes`, `orphanGraceHours` and `storageCapacityBytes` when set. Files off still answers `{ enabled: false }` and nothing else. vti-rooms gains a read-only BlobHost::host_limits() accessor. The storage response shapes are rendered from the specification (vta_sdk::openapi wrappers → admin-ui/openapi.json → wire.ts). Census updates: the list-limit census and its Rust counterpart gain vtc/storage/configs/list (100), the sidebar census gains Storage, and the console document-type manifest gains the seven storage tasks. - **vtc**: Console room detail and Room usage pages — limits, per-member usage, activity and CSV ([#2079](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2079)) P9 part 3a (docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md §8.1): the admin console's view of what the community stores for its rooms, over the vtc/rooms/{get,usage,limits/set}/0.1 tasks #2077 serves. - Room detail (/rooms/, linked from each row of Data rooms): the room's facts; its storage, files still on earlier configs and files awaiting deletion; its ten largest files by size only; its limits with where each came from (override, rooms policy, community default); per-member usage on rooms that are not private (members who added nothing are not listed — the host never saw them, so it is no roster); daily activity over 30, 90 or 365 days. From it an administrator overrides the room's limits, its members' default or one member's, clears an override, or pauses and resumes uploads (filesEnabled alone, leaving every limit as it is). Each change takes a reason, which the audit trail records. - Room usage (/room-usage): the figures grouped by room, member, storage config or day; rooms and configs past 80, 95 or 100 percent of a limit or of capacity, listed first; CSV export of what is shown, with cells a spreadsheet would run as a formula prefixed (OWASP CSV injection). - Both pages need vtc.rooms.admin, as the room list now does. Neither shows a record title, a file name or a file's contents: the host has none. The response shapes are rendered from the specification (vta_sdk::openapi wrappers → admin-ui/openapi.json → wire.ts), not written by hand. Charts are hand-drawn SVG; the console has no chart library. A size field is pre-filled in the largest unit that states it exactly ("1 GiB", "1536 KB"), so re-saving a form changes nothing it was not asked to. The room identifier is taken from the route as the router decoded it: decoding it again would turn a did:web port's %3A into ':' and ask for a different room. Census updates: the list-limit census and its Rust counterpart gain vtc/rooms/usage (100), the sidebar census gains Room usage, and the console document-type manifest gains the three tasks. - **vtc**: DCQL trusted_authorities held at the response, not only published ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2067](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2067)) A criterion's credential query may carry `trusted_authorities` (OpenID4VP 1.0 §6.1.1). The wallet uses it to choose a credential; the verifier still has to check it, and the DCQL matcher does not read it. Until now the VTC published it and ignored it. - `vta_sdk::x509_issuer::x5c_issuer` returns, beside the issuer key, the key identifiers of the authorities certifying it: each certificate's AKI, the SKI of every certificate above the leaf, and that of the anchor reached. - `aki` is held on both paths: a wallet response whose credential no named authority certifies is refused `issuerNotTrusted`, and the join criterion match rewrites a gated query to keys only such a credential offers. A DID issuer has no chain and meets no such query. The anchors still decide trust; `trusted_authorities` only narrows them. - Registration refuses what cannot be held: `etsi_tl`, `openid_federation`, `trusted_authorities` on a non-`dc+sd-jwt` query, an empty list, or an `aki` value that is not base64url. - **vta**: Gate the TEE first-boot admin claim on a pre-registered c… ([#1987](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1987)) * feat(vta)!: gate the TEE first-boot admin claim on a pre-registered claim DID POST /bootstrap/request (Mode B) accepted an anonymous caller: whoever reached a fresh TEE VTA first claimed admin, gated only by the carve-out sentinel, which a hostile host can make vanish by forging its absence or dropping its write. - pnm: `bootstrap claim-did create|show|discard` mints an Ed25519 claim DID before the VTA exists; the private key lives only in the OS keyring (file store refused). `bootstrap connect --slug` signs the request with it and drops the key once attestation verifies. - vta-sdk: optional `claim_signature` on the sealed BootstrapRequest, over a domain tag || client pubkey || nonce. - vta-config: `tee.bootstrap_claim_did`, settable only via the tenant overlay (deny_unknown_fields kept; admin_did still forbidden), validated at boot and covered by the attested config digest. - vta-service: verify the signature, require client_did == the configured claim DID (403, nothing written), then the carve-out; burn the claim DID with the sentinel on success.
## `vti-common`
## [0.44.1](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-common-v0.44.0...vti-common-v0.44.1) — 2026-10-14 ### Added - **vtc**: Room usage, room detail and limit overrides — vtc/rooms/{get,usage,limits/set} and rooms/usage ([#2077](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2077)) P9 part 2 (docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md §6.2–6.3, §8.1): the host tasks the console's room detail and Usage pages read, over the history and overrides #2073 put in vti-rooms. vtc/rooms/get (vtc.rooms.admin): one room's host record, assigned config and every earlier config still holding its blobs, effective limits with each scope's source and the host ceiling, usage and orphans, the ten largest blobs by size only, and on rooms that are not private a count of members with files — never their DIDs (item 5). vtc/rooms/usage (vtc.rooms.admin): rows grouped by room, member, storage config or day, filtered by room, member, config and an inclusive date range (default the last 30 days; invalidRange past 400 days, inverted, or before the oldest kept day), sorted, and paged by a cursor bound to its query (invalidCursor otherwise). Member figures only on rooms that are not private (memberUsageUnavailable when one is named). Activity by config is attributed to each room's current assignment. vtc/rooms/limits/set (vtc.rooms.admin): an override for the room, its members by default, or one member; refuses aboveCeiling, memberLimitsUnavailable and invalidCombination as declared, answers the effective limits, the target scope's usage and overLimit, and is audited (new RoomLimitsChanged event: room, target, previous, current, reason). Not parked, as the specification says: an allowance is reversible and loses nothing. rooms/usage (the room owner's read, an admin chain) on both hosts, through vti_rooms::blob_tasks::usage: one entry per member holding storage or an override, paged; notAvailable on a private room. vtc/rooms/list moves to vtc.rooms.admin, as §6.2 says it should: a community can hand room hosting to someone who is not a full administrator. Both censuses carry the new tasks: conformance witnesses for the three, and error-code witnesses for every code they declare. - **vtc**: Room files in S3 through the community's VTA — one presigned request per object, no storage credential held ([#2063](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2063)) A storage config of kind `s3` with `auth: {mode: vta-account, context, account}` (vtc/_shared/0.1 room-storage, dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#758) keeps room files in a bucket whose credential only the community's VTA holds. For each object operation the VTC asks its VTA for one presigned request (`external/credentials/issue/0.1` against an `s3-static-presign` account): one action on one object, prefix `rooms//`, for 300 seconds. The VTA checks the binding, `external-auth-use`, the account's state, the scope against its ceiling, the TTL and the rate, audits the issuance, and seals the request to this community's X25519 key inside a `#response` whose proof is verified as the VTA's before it is read. The VTA is reached over the VTC's existing messaging socket (TSP > DIDComm, by the VTA's advertised services), so the VTA needs no inbound address for this, and the community holds no storage secret at rest. - vti-common: `blob_store::presigned` (feature `blob-presigned`) — a `BlobStore` over a `Presigner`. Each request is checked before use (https, the asked method, a path ending in the object's key); no redirects; GETs are reused until shortly before they expire; a put streams with Content-Length; a ranged get checks the length returned. - vtc-service: one link to the VTA. `vta_link::VtaLink` (#2060's `keys/sign-jws` link) now runs on `outbound::PeerTasks`, the sign/send/await-verified-reply exchange the git bridge also uses, and `rooms::vta_storage::VtaStorage` issues storage credentials over it. - storage configs: create/update ask the VTA about the account (a canary read under `probe/`) and refuse `unknownAccount`, or name the member at fault for a scope or TTL the binding cannot cover; the probe authenticates through the store's own health check; `credentialState` carries the context. - Docs: `docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md` setup at the VTA; `data-rooms-files.md` P4b.

title: chore(pnm): mediator-admin and mediator-tui 0.42 from affinidi-messaging-mediator
body:
`pnm messaging console` moves from `affinidi-messaging-mediator-admin` / `-tui` 0.11 to 0.42.

The mediator crates moved out of affinidi-tdk-rs into [affinidi/affinidi-messaging-mediator](https://github.com/affinidi/affinidi-messaging-mediator), which versions them in lockstep with the mediator; 0.42.0 is the first release from the new repo. The lockfile also picks up `affinidi-messaging-sdk` 0.36.1 and the new `affinidi-messaging-mediator-types` 0.1.0 (the SDK's shared types now come from there).

No source changes were needed. Locally: `cargo build`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test -p pnm-cli` (118 passed) are clean.

title: feat(vtc): community-owned rooms and member offers — vtc/rooms/community/* and vtc/rooms/offers/*
body:
A community hosts rooms its members own, and can now own rooms itself — the
board's papers, a working group's drafts, a members' library — run from its
console. Design: verifiable-trust-infrastructure docs/05-design-notes/
data-rooms-files.md §8.4.

The community is the owner, and its own VTA is the key holder: the VTA mints
the room's DID, signs its credentials and holds the community's place in a
sealed room's group, through the same rooms/owner/* and rooms/keys/* tasks any
owner's key holder serves. The community holds no room key and no group
secret.

Administrators, holding the new vtc.rooms.manage (the owner's authority,
distinct from hosting's vtc.rooms.admin):
- vtc/rooms/community/create — the VTA mints, founds the group, issues the
  community's own admin authority; the room is stored only after every
  remote step, so a failure leaves no room behind.
- vtc/rooms/community/{list,get} — the owner's view, with counts and when the
  community's own authority lapses.
- vtc/rooms/community/members/{add,remove,list} — add has the VTA issue the
  invitation, membership and authority credentials (never admin) and keeps
  them as an offer; remove advances a sealed room's epoch through the owner's
  group removal and says what removal does not do (no recall; an authority
  credential is honoured until it expires, so open rooms want short expiries).
  members/list is paged and separate from get, because a community library
  can admit the whole community.

Members, on their own DID (pull-shaped admission: a member's VTA has no
inbound address):
- vtc/rooms/offers/list — the caller's offers and the credentials to store with
  their own key holder; never anyone else's.
- vtc/rooms/offers/accept — on a sealed tier, a KeyPackage in and the Welcome
  out, after the VTA adds the member. A repeat with the same KeyPackage gets the
  same Welcome; an unknown outcome is admissionPending, retried safely because
  the VTA settles a pending admission first.

Only active members of the community are admitted to its rooms. Step-up and
consent are described as the intended model, not declared (SPEC §7.3 item 13).
The owner's record of whom it admitted lives apart from anything the host path
reads, so invariant I5 and portability hold.

generated types: new modules only.

title: feat(vtc): community-owned rooms and member offers — vtc/rooms/community/* and vtc/rooms/offers/* (#768)
body:
feat(vtc): community-owned rooms and member offers — vtc/rooms/community/* and vtc/rooms/offers/* (#768)

A community hosts rooms its members own, and can now own rooms itself — the
board's papers, a working group's drafts, a members' library — run from its
console. Design: verifiable-trust-infrastructure docs/05-design-notes/
data-rooms-files.md §8.4.

The community is the owner, and its own VTA is the key holder: the VTA mints
the room's DID, signs its credentials and holds the community's place in a
sealed room's group, through the same rooms/owner/* and rooms/keys/* tasks any
owner's key holder serves. The community holds no room key and no group
secret.

Administrators, holding the new vtc.rooms.manage (the owner's authority,
distinct from hosting's vtc.rooms.admin):
- vtc/rooms/community/create — the VTA mints, founds the group, issues the
  community's own admin authority; the room is stored only after every
  remote step, so a failure leaves no room behind.
- vtc/rooms/community/{list,get} — the owner's view, with counts and when the
  community's own authority lapses.
- vtc/rooms/community/members/{add,remove,list} — add has the VTA issue the
  invitation, membership and authority credentials (never admin) and keeps
  them as an offer; remove advances a sealed room's epoch through the owner's
  group removal and says what removal does not do (no recall; an authority
  credential is honoured until it expires, so open rooms want short expiries).
  members/list is paged and separate from get, because a community library
  can admit the whole community.

Members, on their own DID (pull-shaped admission: a member's VTA has no
inbound address):
- vtc/rooms/offers/list — the caller's offers and the credentials to store with
  their own key holder; never anyone else's.
- vtc/rooms/offers/accept — on a sealed tier, a KeyPackage in and the Welcome
  out, after the VTA adds the member. A repeat with the same KeyPackage gets the
  same Welcome; an unknown outcome is admissionPending, retried safely because
  the VTA settles a pending admission first.

Only active members of the community are admitted to its rooms. Step-up and
consent are described as the intended model, not declared (SPEC §7.3 item 13).
The owner's record of whom it admitted lives apart from anything the host path
reads, so invariant I5 and portability hold.

New shared schema vtc/_shared/0.1/community-room.schema.json. Additive for the
generated types: new modules only.

title: fix(vtc): status lists follow a changed public_url
body:
A VTC whose `public_url` changed after first boot kept minting credentials against the old status-list URL, because `ensure_initial` never touched an existing row. Holders then can't establish revocation status: the old host is gone, and the served list's `id` isn't the URL it was fetched from. Seen on test-vtc (list `id` still `https://test-vtc.storm.ws/...`, served at `test-vtc.openvtc.net`): openvtc refuses every VMC with "revocation status could not be checked".

`ensure_initial` now re-points an existing row at the configured URL under the status-list lock, keeping bits and assignments, and warns. Credentials already issued under the old URL need re-issuing.

Test: `ensure_initial_follows_a_changed_public_url`.

title: fix(vtc): status lists follow a changed public_url (#2087)
body:
fix(vtc): status lists follow a changed public_url (#2087)

* fix(vtc): status lists follow a changed public_url

ensure_initial returned an existing status-list row untouched, so the
list URL minted on first boot stayed in force after public_url changed.
Every credential issued afterwards named a URL the VTC no longer served,
and the served list carried an id that was not the URL it was fetched
from, so no holder could establish its status (openvtc refuses the VMC
with StatusUnknown).

An existing row whose list_credential_id differs from the configured URL
is now re-pointed under the status-list lock, keeping its bits and
assignments. Credentials issued under the old URL need re-issuing.

title: spec(rooms,vtc): rooms/owner/group/remove, and a `rooms` topic on the console's live events (vtc/admin/events 0.2)
body:
rooms/owner/group/remove/0.1 — the last of the owner's group tasks
(data-rooms-files.md §11). Removal is an epoch advance and nothing else is:
the key holder drops the member's leaf and advances the room at its host
with the link and commit, under the caller's `admin` authority. Same
remote-first rules as group/add as corrected in #766: the advanced state is
kept durably before the host is contacted, applied only once the host
accepts, discarded only on a refusal, kept on an unknown outcome and settled
by the next request through rooms/info. At most one pending advance per room,
admission or removal. Refuses `ownLeaf` (an owner leaving hands the room on
with rooms/owner/transfer). States what removal does not do: no recall of
what was read, and the authority credential is a separate thing.

vtc/admin/events {_shared,subscribe,event} 0.2 — the topic set is closed per
version ("a topic not listed here is a new MINOR version of this
component"), so the `rooms` topic is a new version rather than an `ext`
member. `rooms` prompts vtc/rooms/list, vtc/rooms/usage and
vtc/storage/configs/list, goes to holders of vtc.rooms.admin, carries no
count, and is hinted when a room is registered or removed or changes
lifecycle state, when a room's usage or a storage config's held bytes
crosses 80, 95 or 100 percent of a limit or capacity in either direction,
and when a storage config is created, changed or changes state — naming
none of them (data-rooms-files.md §6.3 alerts). subscribe 0.2 allows up to
seven topics. 0.1 is unchanged; a community serving both answers each at its
own version.

Additive for the generated types: new modules; the TypeScript 0.1 modules
keep exporting `Topic` (the generator now disambiguates the two shared
definitions internally).

## Checks (local, as CI runs them)
- `npm run build`: 763 specs validated; `check-bindings` and `check-dart-packages` agree
- codegen regenerated and formatted; clippy --all-features --all-targets -D warnings, `cargo test --workspace --all-features`, `cargo deny check`: green

title: spec(git-ns): nested repository paths for forges with subgroups
body:
Lets git-ns govern repositories under GitLab subgroups: a repository resource becomes `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo-path>` (1–21 path segments, e.g. `gitlab.com/acme/platform/tools/cli`). The namespace stays the top-level owner; a subgroup is not a resource. Segments up to 255 characters.

**Reviewing:** four commits. The first copies each affected version unchanged and the third regenerates bindings — skip both. The second is the change (key hunks below); the fourth adds nested-path examples and invalid examples.

Open: Go and Dart bindings not yet regenerated. Question: may a draft shared schema be widened in place instead of re-versioning 24 tasks?

### The rule — `_shared/0.6` vs `0.5`
```diff
--- a/specs/git-ns/_shared/0.5/git-ns.schema.json
+++ b/specs/git-ns/_shared/0.6/git-ns.schema.json
@@ -3 +3 @@
-  "$id": "https://trusttasks.org/spec/git-ns/_shared/0.5/git-ns",
+  "$id": "https://trusttasks.org/spec/git-ns/_shared/0.6/git-ns",
@@ -5 +5 @@
-  "description": "Shapes used by more than one git-ns/* task: forge-qualified resources, the five git rights, namespaces, repositories, rights records, forge accounts and drift. 0.5 adds `AdminRightRow` and `RightOrigin`: the row shape the administrator's rights console shows, which is either a `RightRecord` restated with membership facts (`recorded`) or a v0.1 `[hooks.git-trust] grant_on_role` grant that is not a record at all (`roleDerived`) — used by git-ns/right/list and git-ns/right/issued-by-departed. Every other definition is unchanged from 0.4. Not itself a Trust Task specification. A VTC is the source of truth for all of these; the Trust Registry and the forge are projections of them.",
+  "description": "Shapes used by more than one git-ns/* task: forge-qualified resources, the five git rights, namespaces, repositories, rights records, forge accounts and drift. 0.6 admits repositories on forges with nested groups, such as GitLab: a repository resource is `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo-path>`, where the repository path holds the subgroups between the top-level owner and the project (`gitlab.com/acme/platform/tools/cli`), up to 21 segments; and a segment may be up to 255 characters. The namespace is still the top-level owner alone, so a resource of two segments is a namespace and one of three or more a repository. Every 0.5 document remains valid. Every other definition is unchanged from 0.5. Not itself a Trust Task specification. A VTC is the source of truth for all of these; the Trust Registry and the forge are projections of them.",
@@ -9 +9 @@
-      "description": "The lowercased DNS host of a forge: `github.com`, a GitHub Enterprise Server host, `codeberg.org`, or a self-hosted Forgejo instance such as `git.example.org`. No scheme, no port, no path. The host is a segment of every resource, so a right never crosses forges.",
+      "description": "The lowercased DNS host of a forge: `github.com`, a GitHub Enterprise Server host, `codeberg.org`, `gitlab.com`, or a self-hosted Forgejo or GitLab instance such as `git.example.org`. No scheme, no port, no path. The host is a segment of every resource, so a right never crosses forges.",
@@ -17 +17 @@
-      "description": "One lowercased owner or repository name. Forges compare these case-insensitively, so the wire form is always lowercase and a producer lowercases before sending. A leading `.` is refused, which rules out `.` and `..`.",
+      "description": "One lowercased owner, group or repository name. Forges compare these case-insensitively, so the wire form is always lowercase and a producer lowercases before sending. A leading `.` is refused, which rules out `.` and `..`. Up to 255 characters, the longest name GitLab allows; GitHub and Forgejo names are shorter.",
@@ -20 +20 @@
-      "maxLength": 100,
+      "maxLength": 255,
@@ -25 +25 @@
-      "description": "A forge-qualified resource: `<forge-host>/<owner>` for a namespace, or `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo>` for one repository, all lowercase — `github.com/acme`, `github.com/acme/widgets`, `codeberg.org/acme`. The forge is never implied: `acme/widgets` alone is not a resource. Containment is by whole segment: `github.com/acme` contains `github.com/acme/widgets` and does not contain `github.com/acme-labs/x` or `codeberg.org/acme/widgets`.",
+      "description": "A forge-qualified resource, all lowercase: `<forge-host>/<owner>` for a namespace, or `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo-path>` for one repository — `github.com/acme`, `github.com/acme/widgets`, `codeberg.org/acme`. On a forge with nested groups (GitLab) the repository path holds the subgroups between the top-level owner and the project: `gitlab.com/acme/platform/tools/cli` is one repository of the namespace `gitlab.com/acme`, and a subgroup such as `gitlab.com/acme/platform` is not a resource. A repository path has 1 to 21 segments (GitLab: 20 levels of subgroup and the project); GitHub and Forgejo repository paths are always one. The forge is never implied: `acme/widgets` alone is not a resource. Containment is by whole segment: `github.com/acme` contains `github.com/acme/widgets` and does not contain `github.com/acme-labs/x` or `codeberg.org/acme/widgets`.",
@@ -27,2 +27,2 @@

+      "description": "A forge-qualified resource naming exactly one repository: `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo-path>`, lowercase, where the repository path has 1 to 21 segments (see `Resource`).",

@@ -84 +84 @@
-      "description": "An identifier the forge itself assigns — a repository id, a user or organisation id — carried as a string so a forge whose ids are not numbers needs no new version. GitHub and Forgejo ids are decimal integers written as strings (`\"812736451\"`). Unlike a name, it survives renames and transfers, which is why rights and bindings are keyed by it.",
+      "description": "An identifier the forge itself assigns — a repository id, a user or organisation id — carried as a string so a forge whose ids are not numbers needs no new version. GitHub, Forgejo and GitLab ids are decimal integers written as strings (`\"812736451\"`). Unlike a name, it survives renames and transfers, which is why rights and bindings are keyed by it.",
@@ -143 +143 @@
-          "description": "Whether the owner is an organisation or a personal account, as the forge reports it. Present once known: a bridge-mode namespace learns it when binding completes, and a manual-mode namespace MAY never learn it."
+          "description": "Whether the owner is an organisation or a personal account, as the forge reports it; a GitLab top-level group is an `organization`. Present once known: a bridge-mode namespace learns it when binding completes, and a manual-mode namespace MAY never learn it."
```

### The meaning — `right/grant/0.4`, *Resources*
```diff
--- a/specs/git-ns/right/grant/0.3/spec.md
+++ b/specs/git-ns/right/grant/0.4/spec.md
@@ ### Resources @@
-Resources are forge-qualified and lowercase — `<forge-host>/<owner>` or `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo>` — and are never accepted without their forge. A producer lowercases before sending, because forges compare owner and repository names case-insensitively and the registry compares by exact string. Rights on a repository are keyed internally by the forge's repository id, so that when the forge renames a repository the VTC moves its rights to the new resource, and a new repository later created at the old name inherits nothing.
+Resources are forge-qualified and lowercase — `<forge-host>/<owner>` for a namespace, or `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo-path>` for one repository — and are never accepted without their forge. The owner is always one segment: the organisation or user, or on a forge with nested groups the top-level group. The repository path is the rest of the repository's path on the forge: one segment on GitHub and Forgejo, and on GitLab the subgroups between the top-level group and the project followed by the project, 1 to 21 segments (`gitlab.com/acme/platform/tools/cli`). A resource with one segment after its forge host is therefore a namespace, and one with two or more a repository; a subgroup (`gitlab.com/acme/platform`) is neither, and no right is held on one. Each segment is 1 to 255 characters. A producer lowercases before sending, because forges compare owner and repository names case-insensitively and the registry compares by exact string. Rights on a repository are keyed internally by the forge's repository id, so that when the forge renames a repository the VTC moves its rights to the new resource, and a new repository later created at the old name inherits nothing.
```

### Old consumers — each new version's *Changes from*
```diff
+++ b/specs/git-ns/repo/adopt/0.3/spec.md   (same section, version numbers aside, in all 24 new versions)
+## Changes from 0.2
+
+- **Nested repository paths.** A repository resource is `<forge-host>/<owner>/<repo-path>`. On a forge with nested groups (GitLab) the repository path holds the subgroups between the top-level owner and the project, up to 21 segments: `gitlab.com/acme/platform/tools/cli` is one repository of the namespace `gitlab.com/acme`. The namespace is still the top-level owner alone, and a subgroup is not a resource, so no right is held on one. A segment may be up to 255 characters.
+- The schema pins [`git-ns/_shared/0.6`](../../../_shared/0.6/git-ns.schema.json) (was `0.3`).
+
+Accepting what `0.2` refused is a backwards-compatible change, released as a `MINOR` increment ([SPEC §5.2](/SPEC.md#52-compatibility-rules)); a `0.2` document is a valid `0.3` document. A producer that also serves `0.2` **MUST NOT** put a resource `0.2` cannot carry — a repository path of more than one segment, or a segment longer than 100 characters — into a `0.2` document: a `0.2` consumer validates against the `0.2` schema and would refuse the whole document. It leaves such repositories, and the rights on them, out of a `0.2` answer instead. Everything else is unchanged from `0.2` and restated below, so that this version stands on its own.
```

### Deliberate limits
```diff
+++ b/specs/git-ns/namespace/bind/0.2/spec.md
+- **`owner` is still one segment**, now up to 255 characters: an organisation or user, or a GitLab top-level group. A subgroup cannot be bound; its repositories belong to the namespace of its top-level group.
+++ b/specs/git-ns/repo/create/0.4/spec.md
+- **`name` is still one segment.** This task creates a repository directly under the namespace's owner. A repository inside a subgroup is created on the forge and brought under the VTC with [`git-ns/repo/adopt`](../../adopt/0.3/spec.md).
```

title: fix(join): say why an issued credential was refused, not that it never came
body:
Seen joining test-vtc: the VTC delivered the VMC (two `credential-exchange/issue` arrived), openvtc refused it because its status list was unreachable, and the row said **"membership credential not received yet"**. The activity log said only "unreachable or did not verify". The real cause was a stale status-list URL on the VTC (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#2087), and nothing on screen pointed there.

- `IssuedCredentialError::StatusUnknown(String)` carries the reason from the status check, e.g. `could not reach test-vtc.storm.ws: …`. It may name the list's host; it never names a DID.
- A refused issue or renewal reply is recorded on the approved-awaiting membership (`credential_refused`, serde default, so existing configs load). It is cleared when a credential is stored.
- The Communities row now reads "✓ approved — the membership credential arrived but was refused: <reason>."

Tests: refusal is noted only on an awaiting join and cleared on store; the panel renders refused rather than missing; the StatusUnknown reason is non-empty and DID-free. Workspace tests pass and clippy is clean.

title: ci(validation): run corpus, review and build checks with preserved evidence
body:
## Behavior

Addresses the repository validation gap identified in #9.

Install an active `.github/workflows/validate.yml` that runs corpus integrity, repository and review regressions, the minimal review validator, and a temporary-output build on pull requests and pushes to `main`. Preserve execution provenance, full corpus errors and warnings, logs, generated files, and SHA-256 manifests in a 14-day artifact. Failures and missing evidence remain explicit; independent checks continue when possible without changing a failed check's conclusion.

## Reconciliation and merge boundary

Reconciled onto current `main` after #16 restored the documented `method/`, `data/`, `tools/`, and `context/` layout. Workflow and reproduction commands now invoke `tools/validate.py` and `tools/build.py`; the validation documentation describes the restored paths. The inactive root `validate.yml` template is removed.

This PR no longer depends on #13. It is ready for maintainer review; no automatic merge is enabled. Contributor self-merge and auto-merge remain excluded.

## Scope

Five paths: the installed workflow, removal of the inactive template, validation documentation, and README/CONTRIBUTING references. No corpus/schema semantics, warning thresholds, branch protections, releases, or publication/deployment behavior changes. The workflow uses read-only repository permissions, pinned actions, and checkout without persisted credentials. Maintainers decide whether the check becomes required.

## Validation

Current head `2457428547b95d5511b49bae8978235ffa14fc24` passed [GitHub Actions run 37608374261](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/actions/runs/37608374261): corpus validation, all 12 repository/review regression tests, minimal review-record validation, temporary build (6 site pages and 12 JSON-LD records), generated-file digest capture, and evidence upload all succeeded.

Artifact `rahp-validation-37608374261-1` (ID 11476425393) has digest `sha256:027dbe89233d4ca17e2d92904f67f062462b4b07e81dc3d9b32abd8f05395250` and 14-day retention. The check demonstrates repository integrity and reproducibility; it does not establish target assurance or independent human review. The DCO sign-off was corrected to match the commit author; verify its latest result on the [PR checks page](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/pull/14/checks).

## Provenance

The layout decision is implemented in #16. This contribution adds bounded repository-level validation and reproducibility evidence and remains subject to upstream maintainer review and merge decision.

title: spec(rooms): group/add keeps a pending admission on an unknown outcome; details schemas for group codes
body:
Corrections to rooms/owner/group/{create,add}/0.1 (drafts, #763), found
implementing them in the VTA:

- add, item 5: discard the pending admission only on a refusal. An
  unreachable or silent host is an unknown outcome — it may have accepted —
  and discarding then would leave the owner an epoch behind their own room.
  The pending admission is kept for item 6; hostUnreachable's meaning says so
  instead of "nothing was changed".
- add, items 2-3: what is kept is the advanced group state with the link,
  commit and Welcome, beside the group the recipient holds, since a
  committer cannot process its own commit later.
- add, item 6: the host's epoch is read with rooms/info under the caller's
  read authority, from the host the admission was sent to; a host at neither
  epoch has moved on, so discard and refuse epochConflict.
- detailsSchema for create's alreadyExists (epoch) and add's epochConflict
  (hostEpoch), which the text already promised.
- create, item 1: the gates on naming the key are issue-membership's, but
  nothing is signed, so a signing quota is not consumed or consulted.

## Checks (local, as CI runs them)
- `npm run build`, `npm run check-bindings`: green (TS, Rust, Go, Dart agree; 202 codes with a detailsSchema match)
- codegen regenerated and formatted; clippy --all-features --all-targets -D warnings, `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features`, `cargo deny check`: green

title: feat(vta): rooms/owner/group/{create,add} — found a sealed room's group and admit members from the owner's agent
body:
A sealed room (`attributed`, `private`) cannot be written to until its MLS
group exists, and the owner's half of a group — founding it, admitting a
member — was library code only. The VTA now serves both owner tasks
(trust-tasks-tf #763):

- `rooms/owner/group/create/0.1` founds the group with the owner as its only
  leaf, at room epoch 1, the epoch a host records at registration. The gate
  is the one issuing the room's credentials uses — control of its signing
  key — checked by a new `keys::require_key_nameable` that applies
  `sign_payload`'s scope, status, context and caller-key-filter gates
  without signing anything. A room this VTA already holds a group for is
  refused `alreadyExists`, never replaced.
- `rooms/owner/group/add/0.1` admits a member's KeyPackage, remote first:
  the add is built on a copy and kept as a pending admission
  (`room-add:<room>` in `room_groups`, the advanced group snapshot with its
  link, commit and Welcome) beside the untouched live group; the room is
  advanced at its host with `rooms/epoch/mint` (link, commit, the owner's
  `admin` presentation); only an accepted advance replaces the live group.
  A refusal (`hostRefused`, or `epochConflict` on `nonSequential`) discards
  it. An unknown outcome (`hostUnreachable`) KEEPS it, and the next admission
  asks the host its epoch (`rooms/info`) and applies or discards it first —
  a key holder cannot process its own commit from the wire, so the pending
  group is the only way to follow a host that did advance. The Welcome is
  returned for delivery to the newcomer's key holder, never sent to the host.
  The KeyPackage must identify `member` (`keyPackageInvalid` otherwise); a
  member already in the group is `alreadyMember`; no `admin` grant in the
  vault is `noAuthority`, before anything is built.

`room_host::send_room_task_typed` keeps a host's refusal apart from an
unknown outcome (`RoomTaskError`); `send_room_task` maps it back exactly as
before for every existing caller.

SDK: `TASK_ROOMS_OWNER_GROUP_{CREATE,ADD}_0_1`, `VtaClient::room_group_create`
/ `room_group_add`. Retry safety: create `RetrySafe` (a repeat is refused
`alreadyExists`, changing nothing); add `Keyed` — the response is the only
copy of the Welcome, so a lost reply retried without a key would be refused
`alreadyMember` with the Welcome gone. Outbound budget lists add; vta-mcp's
guard classes both `Sensitive` beside the issuance verbs.

`pnm rooms owner group-create --room --signing-key [--member]` and
`pnm rooms owner group-add --room --host-did --member --key-package <file|->
[--reason] --out <welcome.json>` (inside `VtaClient::idempotent`).

Tests (vta-service `room_owner_group`): against a stub host on loopback whose
replies are signed as its DID — create at epoch 1 and never twice; a key the
caller cannot name; a full admission after which the newcomer's VTA joins
from the Welcome and each opens what the other sealed; a KeyPackage for
someone else; a refusal leaves the group unchanged; an advance made
elsewhere is `epochConflict` with `hostEpoch`; an advance whose answer was
lost is applied by the next request; a pending admission the host never took
is discarded; no `admin` grant; no group.

docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md §2, §5.4 and §6 use the new tasks and verbs.

## Before merge
- **Depends on trust-tasks-tf #763** (the two specs) and a `trust-tasks-rs` release carrying it.
- Commit `3d0f3e27` (**TEMPORARY**) patches `trust-tasks-rs` to the spec worktree's path so this builds. Drop it and take the released version (a workspace `trust-tasks-rs` floor bump) instead. CI cannot build this branch until then.

## Checks (local, against the patched crate)
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 5752 passed
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3097 passed
- `cargo test -p vta-sdk --doc`: green
- clippy `--workspace --all-targets` and the three reduced-feature `vta-service` runs, `-D warnings`: clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean

title: docs(rooms): community-owned rooms — the community's VTA as key holder, pull-shaped admission, vtc.rooms.manage
body:
Design note data-rooms-files.md §8.4, settled with the product owner on
2026-10-14: rooms are run from where their owner is — a member's from their
VTA (§8.2), the community's from the VTC console.

A community-owned room is owned by the community's DID and its keys are held
by the community's VTA, reached over the VTC's existing vta_link: the same
rooms/owner/* and rooms/keys/* tasks a member's VTA serves for them. The VTC
holds no room key and no group secret. Admission is pull-shaped (the member's
VTA has no inbound address): an administrator adds a member and the VTC keeps
the issued credentials as an offer; the member lists and accepts it from the
portal or the extension, sending a KeyPackage on a sealed room, and the VTC
answers with the Welcome after rooms/owner/group/add. The offer list is the
owner's record in its own keyspace, never read on the host path, so invariant
I5 and portability hold. Creating rooms and managing their members take a new
capability, vtc.rooms.manage, separate from hosting's vtc.rooms.admin; step-up
bound and audited, not parked by default.

Adds the specs this needs to §10 and phase P13, and marks P0 in progress.

title: feat(vtc): console Storage page, moving a room's storage, and the rooms' defaults
body:
P9 part 3b (docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md §7, §8.1).

- Storage (/storage, vtc.rooms.admin): every storage config with what it
  holds against its capacity, its credential state (never a credential) and
  its health; configs whose credential is `required` — as after a restore —
  are listed first. A config's own page probes it (optionally writing,
  reading back and deleting a canary) and shows each step, changes its
  label, capacity or default, and retires it. "New storage" creates a
  `local` config or an `s3` config through an external account at the
  community's VTA, named by its context and identifier: the form asks for
  nothing secret. Kinds and auth modes this build does not serve (ambient,
  sealed, gcs, walrus) are not offered.
- A room's page gains "Send new uploads to other storage"
  (vtc/rooms/storage/assign/0.1). Its existing files stay where they are.
- Create, update, retire and assign take the requester's operation-bound
  step-up and are parked for another holder of vtc.rooms.admin (§7.4); the
  screens say "Sent for approval" and link the action, never "Saved".
  Retiring the default or a config with rooms is not offered, as the VTC
  refuses both.
- Data rooms gains a Defaults card (the design's Settings ▸ Rooms; the
  console has no Settings area): each room's and each member's limits, the
  host-wide largest file, capacity and how long a deleted file is kept,
  read-only, with the configuration sections that change them.

To carry those defaults, vtc/rooms/list's ext["org.openvtc"].roomFiles now
holds, when files are on, `defaults.{room,member}` (each byte measure capped
at the host ceiling, as reported limits are), `maxFileBytes`,
`orphanGraceHours` and `storageCapacityBytes` when set. Files off still
answers `{ enabled: false }` and nothing else. vti-rooms gains a read-only
BlobHost::host_limits() accessor.

The storage response shapes are rendered from the specification
(vta_sdk::openapi wrappers → admin-ui/openapi.json → wire.ts). Census
updates: the list-limit census and its Rust counterpart gain
vtc/storage/configs/list (100), the sidebar census gains Storage, and the
console document-type manifest gains the seven storage tasks.

## Tests
- admin UI: lint (wire:check + tsc) clean; 1029 passed, including 11 new (`plugins/Storage.test.tsx`)
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3097 passed (`the_room_list_says_whether_room_files_are_on` now also holds the defaults)
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 5742 passed
- clippy `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and fmt clean

Not yet viewed in a browser against a running VTC.

body:
Four rustls advisories published 2026-10-14 fail cargo-deny on main and on
every open PR:

- 0346: Debug impls for client session values expose TLS secrets
- 0347: buffered application data sent to the outer server after ECH rejection
- 0348: Brotli certificate decompression can allocate up to 1 GiB before
  authentication
- 0349: an unauthenticated ServerHello can downgrade later connections to
  classical key exchange

All are fixed in 0.23.46. Lockfile only: `cargo update -p rustls`, a
semver-compatible patch, no manifest change. cargo deny check advisories
bans sources licenses passes locally.

Once this merges, #2081, #2082 and #2083 need main merged in (or a re-run after an update) to pick it up.

title: spec(rooms): rooms/owner/group/{create,add} — the owner's agent founds and grows a sealed room's group; register signs as the owner
body:
A sealed room (`attributed`, `private`) cannot be written to until its MLS
group exists, and every member reaches the group by a Welcome — except the
owner, whom nobody can welcome. The member half is specified
(`rooms/keys/{key-package,welcome,commit}`); the owner half was not, so no
surface could found a sealed room or admit anyone to one.

- `rooms/owner/group/create/0.1`: the owner's key holder forms the room's
  group with the owner as its only leaf, at room epoch 1 (the epoch a host
  records at registration). Entitlement: control of the room's signing key,
  as for issuing its credentials. Refuses `alreadyExists` rather than
  replacing a group whose key schedule sealed records depend on.
- `rooms/owner/group/add/0.1`: the key holder admits a member's KeyPackage,
  advances the room at its host with `rooms/epoch/mint` (link and commit
  included, the caller's `admin` authority presented), and returns the
  Welcome for the caller to deliver with `rooms/keys/welcome` — never
  through the host. Remote first: the pending commit is kept durably, sent,
  and applied only once the host accepts, and reconciled against the host's
  epoch after a crash, since a key holder cannot process its own commit
  from the wire.
- `rooms/owner/register/0.1` (draft, clarified in place): the key holder
  sends `rooms/create` with `ownerDid` as its issuer, signed with a key of
  that DID it holds, and never as itself; it refuses with `permissionDenied`
  before contacting the host when it holds none. `rooms/create` names the
  Owner as issuer, and a host running a creation policy (a community
  admitting rooms for its members) checks the party asking is the owner it
  names — a registration issued by the agent in another party's name is one
  no host can tell from registering rooms in a stranger's name. No schema
  change beyond the `ownerDid` description.

Additive for the generated types: two new modules, no change to an
existing type.

## Checks
- `npm run build`: 760 specs validated
- `npm run check-bindings`: TypeScript, Rust, Go and Dart all agree
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features`: green

Implementation follows in verifiable-trust-infrastructure (the VTA serves both tasks; the register fix is in progress there now).

title: feat(vtc): console verifier-identity status — vtc/oid4vp/identities/list (#1988)
body:
A verifier identity is assembled out of band — a key cached here or kept by
the VTA, an EUDI access certificate, swiyu trust statements — and each part
expires or breaks on its own schedule, while a wallet that refuses a request
object tells the community nothing. The console's new Community → Wallet
verifier page shows, per identity, the client_id wallets see, the DID and
signing method, where the key is held, the access certificate's subject,
issuer and validity, each verifier_info attestation with its expiry, whether
it is the default, and whether a session could be opened on it now.

vtc/oid4vp/identities/list/0.1 (trust-tasks-tf #761, trust-tasks-rs 0.31.1
floor), for holders of vtc.config.admin. Problems use the specification's
vocabulary with error/warning severity, each with the vtc oid4vp command that
fixes it: keyCustodyInvalid, signerNotLoaded (installed after start),
agentLinkMissing (VtaHeldSigner with no link — VerifierSigner::can_sign),
certificateMissing / NotYetValid / Expired / ExpiresSoon (30 days),
identityStatementMissing, statementExpired / ExpiresSoon; and community-wide
noPublicUrl and defaultIdentityNotInstalled. isDefault mirrors wallet::start's
choice. Never a private key, nor the key's id at the VTA.

Code: oid4vp::status (the report), trust_tasks::oid4vp_tasks, conformance
witness; admin-ui plugins/walletVerifier.tsx + lib/verifier-identities.ts.
Docs: oid4vp-verifier.md "Checking them from the console".

title: fix(auth)!: logins complete behind a shared IP per-step auth bucket s, serialized challenge cap that evicts instead of refusing
body:
## What and why

Behind one address — a NAT gateway, an app host running many agents — logins
could stop completing altogether.

A login is two requests, a challenge then an authenticate, and both were
charged to one per-IP bucket. Once the burst was spent, every token that
refilled went to whichever request came first; new challenges took them, each
authenticate was refused, and the SDK could only start over with another
challenge while the old one stayed pending. At ten pending challenges the DID
itself was refused — with a 400 a caller could not tell from a validation
error — until the cleanup sweep removed the rows, up to
`challenge_ttl + session_cleanup_interval` (about 15 minutes at the defaults).
Expired challenges kept counting until then.

### Server — per-step buckets (vta-service)

- Anonymous `POST /trust-tasks` requests are charged per step:
  `auth/authenticate/{0.2,0.3}` → `auth-authenticate`, `auth/refresh/0.2` →
  `auth-refresh`, everything else (challenge, public documents) → `auth`.
  Same quota as `auth`, separate buckets.
- The step is read from the document's `type`, not from the client-chosen
  `Trust-Task` header, so labelling challenges as authenticates buys nothing.
  To read it, the limiter buffers an anonymous body up to the existing 64 KiB
  anonymous ceiling before charging it; larger ones are charged to `auth` and
  refused there.
- Authenticate is not exempted from the limiter: it verifies the proof
  (including resolving the signer) before it looks up the session, so an
  exemption would meter none of that.

### Server — per-DID challenge cap (vti-common)

- Only unexpired challenges count (VTI-SES-003, VTI-SES-005).
- At the cap, the oldest outstanding challenge is evicted and the new one
  issued — no refusal. The refusal only ever reached enrolled subjects (an
  unenrolled one persists nothing), so asking for one challenge too many
  disclosed enrolment (VTI-SES-007). Eviction can at worst cancel a login in
  flight, and only by spending the caller's own rate-limit budget — where the
  refusal let anyone lock a DID out for minutes with ten requests.
- Listing, evicting and storing are serialized per DID (striped in-process
  locks), so concurrent requests cannot overshoot the cap. Exact for a store
  one process owns, as the VTA's and VTC's are; documented on the trait.
- Pending challenges are indexed per DID (`pending-challenge:{sha256(did)}:…`)
  instead of scanning every session. The index is written before the row, so
  an interrupted write leaves an entry that listing drops rather than a row the
  cap cannot see; the cleanup sweep also indexes any live challenge without
  one.
- New `SessionStore::pending_challenges`, default `None`. A store that does
  not implement it keeps the previous count-and-refuse behaviour.

### SDK (vta-sdk)

- `auth_light` retries a rate-limited authenticate with the challenge it
  already holds, re-signed each time, for as long as that challenge is valid
  (capped at 10 minutes), with up to 1 s of jitter. Only a 429 the VTA or VTC
  attributes to itself is retried; a proxy's is returned at once. Each wait is
  logged.

### Behaviour changes to know about

- **Breaking:** `vta_service::routes::rate_limit::Limiter` gains two variants
  and becomes `#[non_exhaustive]`.
- New `x-rate-limit-scope` values: `auth-authenticate`, `auth-refresh`.
- One address's anonymous burst on these steps is now 30 at the defaults
  (10 each) instead of 10 across all of them — documented in
  `docs/02-vta/rate-limiting.md`.
- An SDK login now waits out an authenticate rate limit instead of failing at
  once.
- After an upgrade, challenges issued before it are not in the index until the
  sweep indexes them, so a subject can briefly hold up to twice the cap — for
  at most one `challenge_ttl`.

### Not in this change

- A `SessionStore` implemented outside vti-common keeps the previous
  count-and-refuse behaviour until it implements `pending_challenges`; the
  default is unchanged, so no implementor breaks. vti-common's
  `session::list_pending_challenges` implements it for any store whose rows
  are written through `vti_common::auth::session`.
- The VTC's limiter is not split per step. The VTC gets the cap, expiry and
  index changes and the SDK retry, which on its own removes the livelock.
- Refresh capacity per address is unchanged: the separate bucket isolates it
  from logins but keeps the auth quota, so one address still sustains about
  174 refreshing SDK clients at the default token lifetime.

### Evidence

- `agents_behind_one_address_all_log_in_under_a_tight_auth_limit`: four SDK
  logins over real TCP from one address, 1 token/s, while other traffic floods
  challenges. Passes in 3–6 s. With the previous behaviour no login completes
  (fails at the timeout); with the SDK retry alone on one shared bucket it
  takes about 58 s — the 20 s timeout tells the two apart.
- `concurrent_requests_cannot_overshoot_the_cap`: eight concurrent challenges
  one below the cap. Without the per-DID lock, 17 remain against a cap of 10.
- Unit tests for eviction order, expiry, index upkeep and backfill, per-step
  buckets and header spoofing, and the SDK retry decision.
- Full run: workspace and VTC suites (8,832 tests) and doctests, `cargo fmt`,
  and `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` for the workspace plus the three
  reduced-feature vta-service builds.

## Requirements

VTI-SES-003, VTI-SES-005, VTI-SES-007.

## Backport

none — breaking change to `vta-service`.

title: feat(vtc): console room detail and Room usage pages — limits, per-member usage, activity and CSV
body:
P9 part 3a (docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md §8.1): the admin
console's view of what the community stores for its rooms, over the
vtc/rooms/{get,usage,limits/set}/0.1 tasks #2077 serves.

- Room detail (/rooms/<roomId>, linked from each row of Data rooms): the
  room's facts; its storage, files still on earlier configs and files
  awaiting deletion; its ten largest files by size only; its limits with
  where each came from (override, rooms policy, community default);
  per-member usage on rooms that are not private (members who added nothing
  are not listed — the host never saw them, so it is no roster); daily
  activity over 30, 90 or 365 days. From it an administrator overrides the
  room's limits, its members' default or one member's, clears an override,
  or pauses and resumes uploads (filesEnabled alone, leaving every limit as
  it is). Each change takes a reason, which the audit trail records.
- Room usage (/room-usage): the figures grouped by room, member, storage
  config or day; rooms and configs past 80, 95 or 100 percent of a limit or
  of capacity, listed first; CSV export of what is shown, with cells a
  spreadsheet would run as a formula prefixed (OWASP CSV injection).
- Both pages need vtc.rooms.admin, as the room list now does. Neither shows
  a record title, a file name or a file's contents: the host has none.

The response shapes are rendered from the specification
(vta_sdk::openapi wrappers → admin-ui/openapi.json → wire.ts), not written
by hand. Charts are hand-drawn SVG; the console has no chart library.

A size field is pre-filled in the largest unit that states it exactly
("1 GiB", "1536 KB"), so re-saving a form changes nothing it was not asked
to. The room identifier is taken from the route as the router decoded it:
decoding it again would turn a did:web port's %3A into ':' and ask for a
different room.

Census updates: the list-limit census and its Rust counterpart gain
vtc/rooms/usage (100), the sidebar census gains Room usage, and the console
document-type manifest gains the three tasks.

## Tests
- admin UI: lint (wire:check + tsc) clean; 1017 passed, including 12 page tests (`plugins/Rooms.test.tsx`) and 16 helper tests (`lib/rooms-api.test.ts`)
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3097 passed
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 5742 passed
- clippy `--workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and fmt clean

Not yet viewed in a browser against a running VTC.

Next (3b): the Storage page and Settings ▸ Rooms.

Updates `libc` from 0.2.189 to 0.2.190
Release notes

Sourced from libc's releases.

0.2.190

There is now a single config for enabling 64-bit time_t: libc_unstable_time64. This can be set unconditionally; it opts in to 64-bit time_t on the following platforms that use 32-bit by default:

  • 32-bit Linux-GNU
  • 32-bit Linux-uClibc
  • 32-bit Linux-musl. Note that setting this flag also enables some other changes that happend in musl v1.2.
  • 32-bit Windows-GNU
  • ESP-IDF (all targets with this environment are 32-bit)

Most other 32-bit platforms are either already using 64-bit time_t, or are considered legacy and will not be gaining support from their upstream maintainers.

You can enable this using RUSTFLAGS:

RUSTFLAGS='--cfg=libc_unstable_time64' cargo ...

Note that there may still be some changes to features gated by this config option, hence "unstable" in its name. In the near future we will rename it to just libc_time64. Until then, please test it out and report any bugs you find!

Support

  • Add initial support for HelenOS (#4355)

Added

We are slowly filling out the Default implementations, to reduce the need for mem::zeroed() in user code:

  • Unix: Implement Default for a number of structs, especially on Apple platforms (#5576)
  • Linux, NetBSD: Give statvfs a Default impl (#5583)
  • Linux: Add Default to a linux/can.rs structs (#5257)

Other additions:

  • Expose the libc_unstable_time64 cfg (#5411)
  • Android, Glibc: Add pthread_gettid_np (#5359)
  • Android: Add RTLD_NEXT (#5323)
  • Android: Add reuseport BPF socket options (#5366)
  • Apple: Add TCP header flags, options and SACK limits (#5358)
  • Apple: Add NET_RT_DUMP2 (#5442)
  • Apple: Add posix_spawn_file_actions_add(f)chdir(_np) (#5558)
  • BSD: Add BPF_WORDALIGN (#5320)
  • BSD: Add lchmod and lchflags where supported (#5400)
  • BSD: Add minherit and related constants (#4849)
  • Docs: Add more links to public headers and manual pages (#5407), (#5485)

... (truncated)

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.31.1
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: Verifier identities list — the OpenID4VP verifier's state for administrators ([#761](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/761))

vtc/oid4vp/identities/list/0.1 lets a community's configuration
  administrator read the OpenID4VP verifier identities the community presents
  to swiyu and EUDI wallets, and what stops each from serving one.

  A verifier identity is installed out of band — a DID registered with an
  ecosystem, an access certificate from a registrar, trust statements from a
  registry — and each part expires on its own schedule. A wallet that refuses
  a request object tells the community nothing. Per identity the response
  gives the client identifier wallets see, the DID and signing method, where
  the key is held (cached, or kept by the community's agent), the access
  certificate's subject, issuer and validity, each verifier_info attestation
  with its expiry, whether it is the default, and whether a session could be
  opened on it now. Problems use a fixed vocabulary with error/warning
  severity: invalid key custody, no loaded signer, no link to the agent, a
  missing, not-yet-valid, expired or expiring certificate, a missing identity
  trust statement, an expired or expiring statement; and, community-wide, a
  default identity that is not installed, or no https public URL.

  The response never carries key material, nor the identifier under which the
  agent holds a key.

| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.31.0` → `0.31.1` | patch |

| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.26.0` → `0.26.1` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.8.1`) | `0.8.0` → `0.8.1` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.8.0` → `0.8.1` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(vtc): verifier identities list — the OpenID4VP verifier's state for administrators (#761)
body:
feat(vtc): verifier identities list — the OpenID4VP verifier's state for administrators (#761)

vtc/oid4vp/identities/list/0.1 lets a community's configuration
administrator read the OpenID4VP verifier identities the community presents
to swiyu and EUDI wallets, and what stops each from serving one.

A verifier identity is installed out of band — a DID registered with an
ecosystem, an access certificate from a registrar, trust statements from a
registry — and each part expires on its own schedule. A wallet that refuses
a request object tells the community nothing. Per identity the response
gives the client identifier wallets see, the DID and signing method, where
the key is held (cached, or kept by the community's agent), the access
certificate's subject, issuer and validity, each verifier_info attestation
with its expiry, whether it is the default, and whether a session could be
opened on it now. Problems use a fixed vocabulary with error/warning
severity: invalid key custody, no loaded signer, no link to the agent, a
missing, not-yet-valid, expired or expiring certificate, a missing identity
trust statement, an expired or expiring statement; and, community-wide, a
default identity that is not installed, or no https public URL.

The response never carries key material, nor the identifier under which the
agent holds a key.

Tracking: OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1988.

title: fix(vtc): a VTC with no [rooms.files] section starts with room files off
body:
## Problem
Updating an existing VTC, one configured before room files existed, could stop it from starting. Startup always opened room storage:
- it created the `local_storage_bases` directories;
- it seeded a `local` storage config under `<data_dir>/room-blobs`.

Any failure in either stopped the VTC, for a feature its operator never turned on. #2074 fixed one such failure (a relative `data_dir`). This change removes the whole class.

## Change
- **`[rooms.files]` is optional** (`RoomsConfig.files: Option<RoomFilesConfig>`).
- **With no section**:
  - no directory is created and nothing is seeded;
  - the storage registry opens over whatever configs are already stored;
  - uploads answer `filesDisabled`;
  - stored files and records are still served.
- **Writing the section turns files on**: `enabled` now defaults to `true` inside it, and `enabled = false` keeps the settings but refuses uploads.
- **Configs written by setup since P5** carry an explicit `enabled = false`, so they stay off.
- **Console:** `vtc/rooms/list` reports the state in `ext["org.openvtc"].roomFiles.enabled`. When files are off, the Data rooms page says so and shows the section to add, with absolute paths:
  ```toml
  [rooms.files]
  local_storage_bases = ["/var/lib/vtc/room-storage"]
  blob_dir = "/var/lib/vtc/room-blobs"
  ```
  An older VTC that doesn't send the flag shows no notice.
- **Docs:** `docs/02-vta/data-rooms.md` is updated.

## Tests
- `without_the_section_nothing_is_created_and_files_are_off`: it opens over a data directory that cannot be created, and checks that nothing is seeded and uploads are off.
- `room_files_are_off_without_the_section_and_on_with_it`: the config shapes, including the suggested section and `enabled = false`. A saved config doesn't grow a section.
- `the_room_list_says_whether_room_files_are_on`: the ext flag both ways. With files off, no storage config is seeded. `TestVtc::without_room_files()` builds that case.
- Full results:
  - `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 3083 passed.
  - `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings` and fmt: clean.
  - Admin UI: `npm run lint` and `vitest`: 988 passed.

Every configuration written before room files existed has no [rooms.files]

The console learns the state from vtc/rooms/list
(ext["org.openvtc"].roomFiles.enabled) and, when files are off, the Data rooms
page shows the section to add:
