title: security(sync): never sync an applicant's hidden-vetting key to the VTA
body:
The vetting book synced to VTA app state stripped only the hidden vetter's
engine. Each application's applicant engine (`hidden_state`, an
`ApplicantSnapshot`) went with it, `usk` included — the key every tag and
proof of that application derives from — contradicting the module's own
rule that the hidden-vetting engine stays local and that app state is not
for secrets.

`vetting_json` now strips `hidden_state` from every application. On apply,
each application keeps this install's engine (matched by id) and an engine
that arrives from a build that synced one is dropped, never adopted. The
apply also decodes before taking the local engines, so a record that fails
to decode no longer discards them.

A key already at the VTA is overwritten the next time the upgraded install
exchanges: its projected book no longer matches the stored record. Backups
of the VTA taken before then still hold it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

## Test
- `vta_sync::tests::an_applicants_hidden_vetting_key_never_leaves_the_device`
- `vta_sync::tests::a_synced_applicant_key_is_never_adopted_and_is_overwritten`
- `cargo test -p openvtc-core`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: spec(vtc)!: a vta-account storage config names the account's context as well as its identifier
body:
`StorageAuth`'s `vta-account` variant named only `account`, but a VTA names an
external account by the context that owns it and its identifier there: the
`external/credentials/issue` task the community sends requires both. A
community could only fill the gap from something outside the config, which
makes a config mean something only on the host that stored it, confines every
account a community uses to one context, and leaves each implementation to
fill the gap its own way.

`vta-account` now requires `context` (`ExternalAccountContextId`, the issue
task's `AccountContextId` form), and `CredentialState` carries it beside
`account`. Naming a context grants nothing: the VTA issues only to a consumer
bound to the account and holding `external-auth-use` in that context.
`vtc/storage/configs/create` item 5 addresses the account by that pair and
never by an identifier resolved against a context of the community's own
choosing; `unknownAccount` on create and update says so. A new invalid
example covers a missing context.

Breaking for the generated types: a new required member. No community could
create a `vta-account` config before this (the one implementation refused
every kind but `local`), so no stored config lacks it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

Checked locally: `npm run build`, `npm run check-bindings` (Rust, TS, Go and Dart regenerated and in agreement), and the `vtc::storage` conformance tests, including the new invalid example.

title: fix(vtc): the storage probe stages its canary without tempfile, a test-only dependency
body:
The probe added in #2052 staged its canary with `tempfile::tempdir()`, but
`tempfile` is an optional dependency of vtc-service enabled only by the
`test-support` feature. Every test and clippy build turns it on, so only the
MSRV job's plain `cargo check --workspace --locked` compiled the crate
without it, and main has failed that job since the merge.

The canary is now staged under the data directory, beside upload staging
(`room-blob-staging`), under a fresh name, and removed once the probe ends.
That directory is the service's own, rather than the system temp directory.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

Reproduced and verified locally: `cargo +1.95.0 check -p vtc-service --locked` failed with E0433 on `tempfile` before and passes after; `room_storage_configs` tests 13/13.

title: feat(vtc): credential issuers known by an X.509 chain — x5c trust anchors for EUDI PID and Rulebook credentials (#1988)
body:
feat(vtc): credential issuers known by an X.509 chain — x5c trust anchors for EUDI PID and Rulebook credentials (#1988)

An EUDI credential (the PID, or one a Rulebook governs) is issued by an https
URL whose JWS names its key by an x5c chain, not by a DID. The VTC now trusts
such an issuer only through operator-configured anchors, never by the chain
alone.

vta-sdk (feature `x509-issuers`): `x509_issuer` — `X509TrustAnchors`,
`x5c_issuer_key` (validity, CA flags, chain signatures, ends at an anchor or a
certificate an anchor signed, leaf key usage, leaf SAN URI = iss or dNSName =
its host; P-256, secp256k1, Ed25519) and `issuer_jws_key`. Token Status Lists
signed the same way verify through
`verify_status_list_token_with_anchors` / `resolve_token_status_with_anchors`.

vtc-service: `[oid4vp] x509_trust_anchors` (PEM files, read at boot; a missing
or empty file stops it). Wallet sessions and the credential-exchange path verify
with the anchors (`verify_vp_token_with_anchors`,
`verify_presentation_with_anchors`), and one `credential_status_fetcher`
replaces three hand-built ones. A certificate-named issuer meets only a
criterion whose `credentialIssuers` is `any`.

title: feat(vtc)!: storage configs — where a community keeps its rooms' files, changed only with consent
body:
Phase P4 (first part) of docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md §7.

vti-rooms: BlobHost no longer holds one store. It asks a `BlobStores`
resolver for the config a room's new uploads go to (`upload_target`) and
for the store holding a blob under the config it was written to
(`store_for`), so reassigning a room strands no file. Each config has its
own usage counter, and its `capacityBytes` is enforced at begin.
`FixedStore` keeps room-host on one store. Breaking: `BlobHost::new`
takes the resolver in place of a store and a config id.

vtc-service:
- `vtc.rooms.admin` (dtgwg-vti-spec#63): the host's authority over rooms,
  in community-admin's ceiling.
- `storage_configs` keyspace (backed up; no secrets): configs stored as the
  specification's `StorageConfig`, room assignments, last probe. First
  start seeds `local` at `[rooms.files] blob_dir` as the default; rooms are
  assigned to the default at creation (existing ones at boot).
- `vtc/storage/configs/{list,get,create,update,retire,probe}/0.1` and
  `vtc/rooms/storage/assign/0.1`. Create, update, retire and assign park in
  the administrator action list (`Act::ChangeStorage`, stake
  vtc.rooms.admin) and execute on the N-th approval with every check re-run;
  a no-op retire or assign parks nothing. Each change is audited
  (`RoomStorageChanged`, with approvers and reason).
- A `local` root must lie strictly beneath `[rooms.files]
  local_storage_bases` (default <data_dir>/room-storage) after symbolic
  links resolve, and never overlap another config's root, so an
  administrator cannot point the service at the rest of the machine and
  one config's collection never reaches another's files.
- The probe writes its canary under `probe/`, never a room's prefix, and
  scrubs credential-like text from backend errors.
- A draining config retires when its last blob is collected.

Only `local` configs are served; s3/gcs (VTA account or ambient,
downscoped per room), sealed and walrus follow, and are refused at create
until then. Their four codes that cannot yet arise are baselined in the
error-code census with that reason (ceiling 9 → 13).

Depends on dtgwg-vti-spec#63 for the capability's registry entry (the trust-tasks specs already presuppose it).

Local CI: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, nextest workspace (5665 passed), vtc-service + vtc-client (3046 passed), doc tests — all green.

title: feat(vta/pcs): the VTA as hidden-vetting (PCS) engine — applicant and vetter tasks
body:
A community that runs hidden vetting admits an applicant on a zero-knowledge
proof that enough distinct eligible vetters vetted them. Every vetter and
applicant holds a PCS secret key, and until now the member side ran only in a
client that links the PCS library — so a wallet with no PCS implementation
(a mobile app) could not take part at all.

This adds the vta/pcs/* family: the VTA holds the PCS keys and runs every
member-side operation; the client carries messages and never holds a key.

Applicant: applications/{create,show,delete}, verify-attestation, prove.
Vetter: root-request, root-accept, tokens/{request,accept,abandon}, attest,
vetter/show.

Shared rules (custody, one vetter key per context and community, keys derived
from the context base per VTI-KEY-030, audit that never pairs a vetter with an
applicant identifier) are in vta/_shared/0.4/CONVENTIONS.md; wire shapes in
vta/_shared/0.4/pcs-engine.schema.json. Two capabilities join
device/_shared's Capability enum: pcsVetter and pcsApplicant.

A vetter's withdrawal of one attestation is deliberately not in this family
yet: no community-side task accepts a withdrawal, so an engine task producing
one would have no consumer.

The hidden-vetting definitions vtc/vetting/hidden/publish and .../show each
carried inline (and vetting/attestation's StatementMeta) move to
vetting/_shared/0.1/hidden-vetting.schema.json, since the new tasks use them
too. Wire-identical: an in-place re-pin of draft specs.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

## Checks run locally
- `npm run build` / `npm run validate` — 757 specs, no new warnings
- `npm run check-bindings` — Rust, TS, Go, Dart all agree
- `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`
- `npx tsc -p trust-tasks-ts/tsconfig.json --noEmit`

## Consumer
verifiable-trust-infrastructure implements the engine in vta-service once this is released (design: openvtc `vetting-hidden-vetters-pcs.md` §13 C7).

title: docs(assurance): explain incremental RAHP assurance model
body:
## Purpose

Adds an explanatory design note for #17 describing how RAHP builds assurance incrementally across source preparation, evidence generation, RAHP assessment and assurance interpretation.

This is intended to help reviewers interpret the current convergence sequence before further increments build on #19, #20 and #21.

## What this note clarifies

- Why Increment 1 is part of RAHP even though it only establishes reproducible source preparation and replay.
- How observations, such as the TRQP time mismatch, should be treated before they become specification findings.
- Why validation and replay evidence do not by themselves establish assurance success.
- Why review vocabulary and reviewer accountability are method concerns, not merely implementation details.
- How example-local hypotheses should remain distinct from canonical corpus risks.
- What future convergence PRs should explain up front.

## Scope boundary

This PR is documentation-only. It does not change schemas, validators, corpus records, review records, examples, CI, or the accepted #17 delivery sequence. It also does not resolve the method questions raised on #20 or #21; it frames them so the task force can decide them more cleanly.

## Provenance

Prepared with AI assistance following review discussion on #19, #20 and #21 and the #17 convergence plan.

title: vta-service-v0.59.0
body:
### Added

- **services**: Complete DIDComm enable with a soft restart and a readiness wait ([#2045](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2045))

* feat(services): complete DIDComm enable with a soft restart and a readiness wait

  `services didcomm enable` published the DID document change but left the
  VTA without a running messaging runtime until the next manual restart. The
  operation now signals `ext["org.openvtc"].restarting` and performs a soft
  restart after the reply reaches the transport send boundary, and `pnm`
  waits for the restarted listener before returning.

  Also fixes a TEE fleet image that could not boot REST-only, by removing the
  baked `[messaging]` placeholder that pre-empted the tenant overlay's
  "materialize messaging only when a mediator_did is supplied" branch.



### Build & CI

- Trust-tasks-rs 0.30, affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.35 and affinidi-tdk 0.25 ([#2049](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2049))

Moves the Trust Task stack to trust-tasks-rs 0.30 (capability-client,
  https, didcomm, tsp and proof with it) and the Affinidi crates that move in
  lockstep with it (affinidi-tdk-rs #940): affinidi-messaging-sdk 0.35,
  affinidi-tdk 0.25, mediator-admin/tui 0.10 and test-mediator 0.21. One copy
  of each resolves; trust-tasks-rs 0.28 no longer appears in the graph.

  0.30 carries dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf #750, which makes the rooms/info and
  rooms/usage proofs REQUIRED. The interim DISPATCHED_WITHOUT_PROOF entry for
  rooms/info ([#2040](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2040)) and its skip in
  every_rooms_task_declares_the_proof_its_arm_requires are removed: the
  census now holds the VTC's rooms/info arm to the specification.



### Security

- **config**: Runtime config write-backs never write the boot-injected JWT key ([#2046](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2046))

Every runtime operation that persists configuration — `config/patch`, audit
  retention, `services {didcomm,webauthn} {enable,update,disable}` — wrote it
  back by serialising the whole in-memory `AppConfig`. On a hardened or
  KMS-backed VTA that includes `auth.jwt_signing_key`, which boot injects into
  memory precisely so it never reaches `config.toml`; the first such operation
  put it on disk. `VTA_AUTH_JWT_SIGNING_KEY` leaked the same way, replacing the
  file's own key with the environment's.

title: vta-keyspaces-v0.16.0
body:
### Added

- **vta**: External accounts — short-lived provider credentials with no inbound surface ([#2016](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2016))

* feat(vta): external-accounts capabilities and keyspaces

  Adds the two capabilities the external/* family (trust-tasks-tf #740) gates on: external-accounts-manage, derived by admin alone, and external-auth-use, derived by every role that holds sign (the account's binding, not the role, bounds a consumer). Both are non-additive members of the non-exhaustive Capability enum.

  Registers two keyspaces: external_accounts (settings, bindings, state) in BACKED_UP, and external_secrets (wrapped provider secrets) in EXCLUDED_FROM_BACKUP, so a portable password-protected backup is never a way to take a provider secret away. DID deletion: an account's binding names its consumer, so external_accounts blocks; external_secrets is unrelated.

  The device-binding Capability registry (device/_shared 0.2) does not list the two yet, so device listings carry them under ext until it does.

title: fix(vtc): a hidden-vetting criterion never counts named vetting statements
body:
A criterion that publishes hidden-vetting parameters fell through to the
named-statement count whenever a submission carried no PCS proof (or the
build lacked `vetting-pcs`, which compiles the hidden path out entirely).
Enough named statements from eligible vetters then satisfied it, admitting
an applicant under a hidden criterion with no proof at all.

That breaks the design rule that a criterion is named or hidden, never both
(vetting-hidden-vetters-pcs.md §12.1): a vetter who gave one applicant both a
named statement and a hidden attestation counts twice, and the community
cannot tell the two are one person.

`vetting_facts` now returns unsatisfied facts for a hidden criterion with no
counted proof. Named statements are recorded, unverified and not counted,
under `named-statement-on-hidden-criterion`; the applicant is told
`vetting:hidden:no-proof` (`vetting:hidden:unsupported` without the
feature). Named criteria are unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

## Test
- `join_requests::named_statements_never_satisfy_a_hidden_vetting_criterion`: two eligible named statements (the pair that admits under the named criterion) get `requestMore` + `vetting:hidden:*` and admit nobody.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` (default + `--features vetting-pcs` vetting subset), clippy `-D warnings` under both feature sets.

title: feat(vtc): EUDI verifier identity — x509_hash, access-certificate CSR and chain, pnm keys bundle-key (#1988)
body:
Part of #1988 (the VTC as an OpenID4VP verifier for swiyu and EUDI wallets; design: `docs/05-design-notes/oid4vp-wallet-verifier.md`). Custody A: the VTA mints the key and the VTC caches it.

An EUDI wallet identifies a relying party by its X.509 access certificate, not a DID: `client_id = x509_hash:<SHA-256 of the leaf>`, with the chain in the request object's `x5c`.

## Operator flow

```sh
vtc oid4vp request --identity eudi --out eudi-request.json            # VTC host, stopped
pnm keys create --key-type p256 --context eudi-verifier --label eudi-verifier
pnm keys bundle-key <key id> --recipient eudi-request.json --out eudi.armor
vtc oid4vp install --identity eudi --bundle eudi.armor --digest <digest>
vtc oid4vp csr --identity eudi --common-name … --organization … \
  --organization-identifier … --country DE --dns vtc.example.org --out eudi.csr
# registrar issues the access certificate
vtc oid4vp certificate --identity eudi --chain eudi-chain.pem \
  [--registration-certificate wrprc.jwt --registration-format <format>]
```

## Changes

- **`pnm keys bundle-key`** (`vta-cli-common`): seals one P-256 key that no DID publishes as `SealedPayloadV1::RawPrivateKey`. There is no wire change. The VTA audits the export, and the key leaves the CLI only sealed.
- **`VerifierKind::Eudi`**: `did` and `kid` are now optional on the record, and stored swiyu records still parse. The record gains `x5c` and `verifier_info`, and `client_id()` returns `Option`.
- **`oid4vp::x509`**:
  - `build_csr` writes a PKCS#10 request with rcgen. rcgen runs without a crypto backend; the identity's key signs, and its ES256 `r||s` is DER-encoded.
  - `check_chain` refuses a leaf for another key, an expired leaf, or one without `digitalSignature`. It also refuses a certificate not signed by the next, and a lone self-signed certificate.
  - A trailing self-signed root is left out of `x5c`.
- **Wallet sessions**:
  - An EUDI request carries `x5c`, with no `kid` and no swiyu `profile_version`, and includes `verifier_info`.
  - It offers `A128GCM` and `A256GCM`, and the wallet link uses `haip-vp://`.
  - An identity without its certificate is never chosen, and the start answers `verifierNotConfigured`.
- **Docs**: `docs/03-vtc/oid4vp-verifier.md` gets an EUDI walkthrough. One CLAUDE.md line now covers a foreign-protocol key certified by X.509 rather than published in a DID.

## Open question

The `verifier_info` format identifier for an EUDI registration certificate is operator-supplied (`--registration-format`), not guessed.

## Not in this PR

Credential issuers named by an `x5c` chain to a configured trust anchor (PID list / Rulebook). Issuers are still accepted only by DID.

## Tests

- Unit tests: the CSR verifies under the identity's key; an issued chain is accepted and its `client_id` is `x509_hash:`; wrong key, wrong order, wrong CA and expiry are refused; DER encoding; raw-key bundle install and refusals; `pnm` scalar extraction.
- Integration (`wallet_session`): an EUDI identity alongside a swiyu one, chosen by `clientIdPrefix: "x509_hash"`, completes a full round trip under `x5c`. Without its certificate it opens no session.
- Before the rebase onto #2049, all passed: VTC 3022, workspace 5665, doctests, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt.
- After the rebase: clippy is clean and the 36 OID4VP, wallet-session and bundle-key tests pass. The full suites were not re-run.

feat(vtc): EUDI verifier identity — x509_hash, access-certificate CSR and chain, pnm keys bundle-key (#1988) (#2050)

A VTC can now present itself to EUDI wallets as well as swiyu ones. An EUDI
wallet identifies a relying party by its X.509 access certificate, not a DID:
client_id is x509_hash:<SHA-256 of the certificate> and the request object
carries the chain as x5c.

- pnm keys bundle-key <key-id>: seals one P-256 key that no DID publishes
  (SealedPayloadV1::RawPrivateKey) to a recipient. The VTA audits the export
  (keys/export-secret/0.1); the key leaves the CLI only sealed.
- vtc oid4vp install accepts that bundle as an EUDI identity (VerifierKind::
  Eudi; did/kid are now optional on the record, which still reads stored
  swiyu records).
- vtc oid4vp csr writes a PKCS#10 request signed by the identity's own key
  (rcgen, no crypto backend; the signature is DER-encoded from ES256 r||s).
- vtc oid4vp certificate installs the issued chain: the leaf must certify the
  identity's key, be valid now and allow digitalSignature; each certificate
  must be signed by the next; a lone self-signed certificate is refused and a
  trailing self-signed root is left out of x5c. An optional registration
  certificate goes into every request's verifier_info, its format named by
  the operator.
- Wallet sessions: an EUDI identity signs with x5c (no kid, no swiyu
  profile_version), offers A128GCM and A256GCM, invokes haip-vp://, and opens
  no session until its certificate is installed (verifierNotConfigured).

Not yet: issuers named by an x5c chain to a configured trust anchor; today an
issuer is still accepted only by DID.

title: Post-quantum horizon: Security Considerations item 8, WG-18, a quantum horizon on every record, the proving-system split
body:
Following the 8 September call's point that the credential signature scheme is the critical, non-swappable choice — a post-quantum proof system does not mask a pre-quantum signature — this revision gives the specification a post-quantum reading it can be held to, without adopting a construction or promoting a state.

**Security Considerations item 8** now reads soundness apart from zero-knowledge and forgery apart from confidentiality. Soundness of pairing-based proof systems and unforgeability of discrete-log signatures and commitments fall under a cryptographically relevant quantum computer; zero-knowledge and hiding are information-theoretic and do not. So there is no retroactive loss, every record's exposure is forward-looking forgery (the one confidentiality case is the Tag_DDH pseudonym stream of the PCS route, records 023/024 option 1), and the credential signature is the layer a software update cannot swap. The issuance pattern with a post-quantum realisation at presentation cost today is the published-commitment branch of X3: a post-quantum signature over the root or leaf commitment, checked outside the proof, the proof verifying no signature — the set-root primitive of cred-tf #40 and the transition ETSI TR 119 476-1 §9.3 describes for salted-hash credentials. Where the sibling specifications stand is recorded: the Trust Tasks framework pins `mldsa44-jcs-2024` / `slhdsa128-jcs-2024`, VTI defines hybrid proof sets (VTI-KEY-103..105), the credential specification names `eddsa-jcs-2022` alone.

**Every construction record** carries a *quantum horizon* under its Horizon — which clauses or options fall to forgery, which lose confidentiality — as a new optional record field (`quantumHorizon { forgery, confidentiality }`; schema, renderer and validator updated). **Every proving-system entry** states post-quantum soundness and post-quantum zero-knowledge separately beside the existing `postQuantum` line: Groth16 falls / holds; Flock and ProveKit's core plausible / plausible, with the Groth16 wrapper named as where ProveKit stops being post-quantum and the 2025–26 proximity-gap results named as the bound a cost row must state; Longfellow plausible at the argument, classical at the statement.

**WG-18 — Discuss before implementation: post-quantum issuance contract**, opened beside WG-02: route (b) — signature over a published commitment, checked outside the proof — as the first profile's default or a reasoned alternative; the post-quantum root suite (ML-DSA-65, or SLH-DSA-128s for long-lived registry roots) as the profile's horizon rather than a V1 blocker; the hybrid overlap rule by reference to VTI; a decision on ADR-001's D3 against hash-based proof sizes. **D3** carries that proposed resolution; its status stays open.

**References added:** ETSI TR 119 476-1, NIST IR 8547, FIPS 204 and 205, W3C Quantum-Resistant Cryptosuites (FPWD 2026-06-16), Chiesa–Manohar–Spooner 2019, the proximity-gap results (Diamond–Gruen; Crites–Stewart; Ben-Sasson et al.; Kambiré), the DTG VTI and Trust Tasks framework specifications.

Appendix D and E updated; Appendix B pins evidence commit `0f7657f`. `validate` 24/24, conformance tests pass, render clean. No state promoted; nothing adopted.

Companion: [dtgwg-zkp-tf PR #29](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-zkp-tf/pull/29) carries the explanatory chapter (*Post-quantum considerations*) and the proposed LIV-ALG-09; either merges first.

title: Post-quantum considerations: the guide chapter, LIV-ALG-09 (proposed), Pages served from Actions
body:
A **Post-quantum considerations** chapter for the implementation guide, and one proposed requirement, following the 8 September call's point that the credential signature scheme is the critical, non-swappable choice.

**The chapter** explains the one sentence the specification gives the post-quantum horizon:

- **Two properties, read separately.** Soundness of pairing-based proof systems and unforgeability of discrete-log signatures and commitments fall under a cryptographically relevant quantum computer; zero-knowledge and hiding do not (they are information-theoretic). So: no retroactive privacy loss, no retroactive soundness loss, and every exposure is forward-looking forgery — the migration trigger is a verifier-policy event, not an archival one. ETSI TR 119 476-1 §9 is the reference.
- **The hash side holds.** The gadgets the records are built from keep both properties under Grover at 256-bit output, with the Poseidon-margin and secret-entropy caveats stated.
- **Hash-based proof systems** are plausibly post-quantum in the quantum random-oracle model (Chiesa–Manohar–Spooner), with the 2025–26 proximity-gap results named as a parameter caveat and the Groth16 wrapper named as where a hash-based core stops being post-quantum.
- **The signature is the layer that cannot be swapped**, and where the three sibling DTG specifications stand (Trust Tasks pins ML-DSA/SLH-DSA suites; VTI defines hybrid proof sets; the credential specification names `eddsa-jcs-2022` alone).
- **The pattern:** sign the root or leaf commitment with a post-quantum suite outside the proof; the proof verifies no signature. Why verifying ML-DSA inside a circuit is not available at presentation cost today (self-reported figures, stated as such).
- What stays off the post-quantum path (the PCS route of records 023/024; the as-signed Longfellow class), the regulatory clocks, and what is still unknown.

**Also in this PR**

- `cryptographic-background.md`: the "Post-Quantum Status" bullets now split soundness from zero-knowledge and point to the chapter.
- `proof-of-liveness-requirements.md`: **LIV-ALG-09 — Issuance separability (proposed 2026-10-12)** after LIV-ALG-08, with a changelog line. A profile states whether the issuer signature is verified inside the proof or over a published commitment outside it, and a profile that verifies a pre-quantum signature inside the proof states that its forgery horizon is the signature's. Proposed, not ratified.
- `guide/README.md`: Pages is now served from the GitHub Actions source (switched 2026-10-12; the deploy workflow ran green), so the guide is live at https://trustoverip.github.io/dtgwg-zkp-tf/ and the specification's cross-links resolve.

Companion: dtgwg-zkp-spec PR (same date) carries Security Considerations item 8, WG-18, a quantum horizon on every record and the proving-system split. Either merges first; the chapter and the specification text point at each other by section name.

title: feat(vtc): wallet evidence decides the join — on the named request, or the next submission (#1988)
body:
A wallet session's verified presentation (#2044) was recorded on the session
and read by no decision. It now counts, as `wallet-session/start/0.1` consumer
rule 11 says, toward the criterion the session was opened for and no other:

- With `requestId`: the evidence is recorded on that request (`join_wallet:`
  beside it, like the criterion and vetting records, deleted with it). A
  `deferred` request is decided again at once — its own presentation plus
  every wallet evidence on it, under the criterion it was decided under, the
  path a supplement takes (`orchestrate::redecide`, now shared). A `pending`
  request is recorded for its reviewer and not decided underneath them. A
  decided or withdrawn one takes nothing.
- Without: the evidence is held for the applicant's next submission until the
  session's `heldUntil`. A submission decided under that criterion counts it,
  binds the session to the new request (the status task then reports
  `requestId`, no `heldUntil`) and records the evidence there. Held evidence
  for other criteria stays held.

`PresentedCredential::only_for` carries the scope: a wallet credential is
offered only to the criterion whose `requirementsDigest` its session named.
It is bound to the applicant by the session — opened with their signed
document — not by a key; the wallet's holder key stays beside them, never as
them (rule 10). A supplement replaces the request's presentation and keeps its
wallet evidence. One wallet answer at a time is handed to the join, so two
sessions bound to one deferred request cannot both decide it from the same
state.

docs/03-vtc/oid4vp-verifier.md describes it. P3 of
docs/05-design-notes/oid4vp-wallet-verifier.md is complete for swiyu; EUDI's
x5c issuer keys come with its identity.
author: stormer78

title: security(config): runtime config write-backs never write the boot-injected JWT key
body:
Every runtime operation that persists configuration — `config/patch`, audit
retention, `services {didcomm,webauthn} {enable,update,disable}` — wrote it
back by serialising the whole in-memory `AppConfig`. On a hardened or
KMS-backed VTA that includes `auth.jwt_signing_key`, which boot injects into
memory precisely so it never reaches `config.toml`; the first such operation
put it on disk. `VTA_AUTH_JWT_SIGNING_KEY` leaked the same way, replacing the
file's own key with the environment's.

`AppConfig::to_runtime_toml` serialises the running configuration with
`[auth] jwt_signing_key` exactly as the file holds it, and refuses to
overwrite a file that does not parse. No runtime operation changes the key,
so the file's value is always the right one to keep; setup and a restore onto
a plain VTA, which do set it, keep using `save()`.

Deployments that already ran one of these operations on a hardened or KMS VTA
have the key in config.toml. Boot ignores it there (hardened) or overwrites
it (KMS), so the line can be deleted; whether the key itself needs replacing
depends on who could read that file.

## Testing

- `cargo nextest run -p vta-service -p vta-config -p vta-backup` — 1966 passed
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean

Found reviewing #2045, which relies on `persist_didcomm_enabled` for its soft-restart reload.

title: feat(services)!: complete DIDComm enable with a soft restart and a readiness wait
body:
## 1. `services didcomm enable` now completes the operation itself

Enabling DIDComm at runtime wrote and published the DID document change, but
the VTA never started the persistent messaging runtime that the change
describes — the new listener only appeared after a manual restart. The
operation now finishes the job.

**Server side.** `handle_enable` stamps a DIDComm enable response with
`ext["org.openvtc"].restarting = true` and asks a new `RestartGate` to
restart. The gate is the ordering mechanism: the restart fires once the
response reaches the transport's send boundary, so the caller's reply is not
lost to the teardown it triggers. A 30-second backstop covers handlers or
transport paths that request a restart without reaching a normal send
completion — a failsafe, not a promise that every slow send completes first.
It matches the current TSP reply budget (10s peer-mediator lookup + 20s
rate-limit retries) and is cancelled when the normal path fires the gate.

`TrustTaskOutcome` carries a `restart` flag so all three transports (REST,
DIDComm, TSP) propagate it identically rather than each re-deriving it, and
`AppConfig::reload_for_restart` re-reads `config.toml` for the next
generation while carrying forward the values boot injects and never persists
(the hardened/KMS `auth.jwt_signing_key`, a TEE-generated `vta_did`). On an
attested VTA it additionally refuses a reload that changed anything outside
the runtime-persisted `messaging`/`services` fields, so a soft restart cannot
be used to swap in a configuration the boot attestation never covered. The
carry-forward list is documented as a contract — a future boot-time mutation
that isn't added to it would be silently dropped on restart.

**Client side.** `pnm services didcomm enable` reads the `restarting` hint
and polls the restarted listener with trust-pings until it answers:

```bash
pnm services didcomm enable --mediator-did <did>              # waits up to 300s
pnm services didcomm enable --mediator-did <did> --wait-secs 120
pnm services didcomm enable --mediator-did <did> --no-wait
```

The readiness probe opens **one** trust-ping session for the whole wait
rather than one per probe. That is not only an efficiency point: opening a
session also provisions **PNM's own** allow-all mediator account. `--setup-acl`
provisions the *VTA's* account, which is what lets the VTA receive — but the
pong travels the other way as a forwarded delivery, so a mediator that refuses
those by default drops it unless the client's account accepts it too. Without
this the poll against a closed-ACL mediator ran the full deadline and failed,
while `pnm health` (which has always provisioned its own account before
pinging) succeeded immediately afterwards. Reusing the session also keeps the
probe windows honest — session setup costs ~4s of TDK/ATM/profile/websocket
work that a per-probe session would spend out of each 10s window — avoids
repeatedly reclaiming the client DID's single mediator socket, and means a
timed-out probe cancels only the ping, never the connection that owns it.

The restart is deliberately soft and scoped: it reloads configuration and
recreates the messaging runtime, but does not drain unrelated in-flight Trust
Tasks. The task that requested the restart is protected by the reply ordering
above; other work follows its normal idempotency and delivery semantics.
`services tsp enable` and REST/WebAuthn mutations are outside this flow.

## 2. A TEE fleet image could not boot REST-only

`config.fleet-base.toml` baked a placeholder `[messaging]`
section (`mediator_did = "OVERLAY_PLACEHOLDER_MEDIATOR_DID"`). Because
`messaging` is `Option<MessagingConfig>`, `apply_tenant_overlay` only
*materializes* it when the overlay supplies a real `mediator_did` — but the
baked placeholder meant the base was already `Some(..)`, so every un-baked
boot took the *patch* branch instead. A tenant with no mediator configured
therefore booted believing DIDComm was configured: it published the
placeholder as its mediator in the DID document (`vta-tee::did_autogen` adds
a `#vta-didcomm` entry whenever `messaging` is `Some`) and retried the
unresolvable connection forever (`server.rs` gates the `MessagingConnect`
supervisor on `messaging.is_some()`).

Removing the baked section fixes all of it with no logic change — both call
sites were already correct once `messaging` was genuinely absent. A tenant
that wants DIDComm at boot supplies it in the overlay; one that doesn't boots
REST-only and enables it later via the flow in (1).

## 3. `setup_acl` is overlay-passable

Fixing (2) changed which `apply_tenant_overlay` branch runs for an overlay
that *does* supply a `mediator_did` (materialize, not patch), and that branch
hardcoded `setup_acl: false`. Rather than hardcode a policy on either branch,
`TenantMessagingOverlay` gained `setup_acl: Option<bool>`, honored by both
branches and defaulting to `false` when absent — matching how `mediator_did`
and `mediator_url` already work.

## Files

**Restart gate + transports** — `server.rs` (`RestartGate`),
`trust_tasks/{mod,services,helpers,management,backup,idempotency,wire_v0_2}.rs`
(`restart` on `TrustTaskOutcome` + the enable response's `ext`),
`messaging/{handlers,tsp_inbound,service,shim,router}.rs` (propagation),
`restore.rs`, `test_support.rs`, `tests/it/mock_vta.rs`.

**Config** — `lib.rs` (`reload_for_restart` + tests),
`tenant_overlay.rs` (`setup_acl`, fleet-base regression test),
`config.fleet-base.toml`.

**Client** — `vta-sdk/src/protocol/{mod,services}.rs` (`restarting` /
`is_restarting`), `mod.rs` (`open_vta_ping_session`),
`services.rs` (readiness poll),
`Cargo.toml` (`session`, `acl-setup` features),
`pnm-cli/src/{cli,commands/services,main}.rs` (`--wait-secs` / `--no-wait`).

**Docs** — `runtime-service-management.md`.

## Testing

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy` — clean on `vta-config`, `vta-sdk`, `vta-cli-common`,
  `pnm-cli` (all targets) and `vta-service` (lib). Two pre-existing,
  unrelated errors elsewhere (`store.rs`,
  `mod.rs` test code — both untouched here,
  last modified in `cd08f58f` / `e3e6eac2`) are not addressed.
- `cargo test` — `vta-config`, `vta-sdk`, `vta-cli-common`, `pnm-cli` (113)
  all pass. `vta-service --features tee --lib`: **1424 passed, 1 failed.**

## Follow-up required: runtime DIDComm enable is still blocked on TEE

This PR makes `services didcomm enable` complete the operation *within* the
VTA, and makes a fleet TEE image boot REST-only so that enabling DIDComm later
is the intended path. On a Nitro Enclave deployment that path is **not yet
usable end to end**, for a reason entirely outside this diff — and the fix in
(2) is what makes it reachable.

`enclave-proxy` (`deploy/nitro/enclave-proxy`) is a separate, un-attested
process on the parent EC2 instance that bridges the enclave's vsock traffic to
real TCP/HTTPS. It enforces an outbound HTTPS `CONNECT` allowlist built
**exactly once, at its own process startup**:
`ProxyConfig::build_allowlist` adds `kms.<region>` + `dynamodb.<region>`, plus
the host derived from `mediator_did` — but only if a mediator was configured at
that moment. `run_https_proxy` then holds that list in a plain
`Arc<Vec<(String, u16)>>` for the process's lifetime and never mutates it.

So a VTA that boots REST-only (the behaviour this PR restores) starts alongside
a proxy whose allowlist is permanently `[kms, dynamodb]`. A later, in-enclave
`services didcomm enable` updates the VTA's own config and DID document, but has
no channel to tell the separate parent process about the new mediator host — the
handshake's outbound `CONNECT` is rejected before it leaves the instance:

```
[https] CONNECT to <mediator-host>:443 BLOCKED — not in allowlist.
        Current allowlist: ["kms.<region>.amazonaws.com:443",
                            "dynamodb.<region>.amazonaws.com:443"]
```

which surfaces inside the enclave as `affinidi_did_authentication` failing with
`TunnelUnsuccessful` against the mediator's `/authenticate/challenge`.

This is a pre-existing structural gap, not a regression from this PR —
previously the mediator was always known at boot, so the combination never
arose.

**Until that lands**, DIDComm enable on a TEE deployment requires the mediator
to be present in the proxy's startup inputs — i.e. supplied in the tenant
overlay at boot, or the proxy restarted afterwards.

title: feat(services)!: complete DIDComm enable with a soft restart and a readiness wait (#2045)
body:
feat(services)!: complete DIDComm enable with a soft restart and a readiness wait (#2045)

* feat(services): complete DIDComm enable with a soft restart and a readiness wait

`services didcomm enable` published the DID document change but left the
VTA without a running messaging runtime until the next manual restart. The
operation now signals `ext["org.openvtc"].restarting` and performs a soft
restart after the reply reaches the transport send boundary, and `pnm`
waits for the restarted listener before returning.

Also fixes a TEE fleet image that could not boot REST-only, by removing the
baked `[messaging]` placeholder that pre-empted the tenant overlay's
"materialize messaging only when a mediator_did is supplied" branch.

Signed-off-by: Yaroslava Kurash <yaroslava.k@affinidi.com>

* fix(services): attested restarts stay attested; the restart fires once the reply is out

Review fixes for the DIDComm-enable soft restart.

- An attested generation's successor is attested again. The orchestrator
  asked the reload whether to recapture the config digest, and the reload
  never has one (`#[serde(skip)]`), so `vta/attestation/config-report` went
  blank after the first restart and the next restart took the un-attested
  reload path.
- An attested restart keeps the running configuration instead of re-reading
  config.toml and refusing on any difference. Every runtime operation that
  persists configuration applies it in memory too, so the file holds nothing
  a restart needs; comparing it failed on drift that is not an edit (a fleet
  enclave's file is the baked base, without the overlay).
- One owner per step of a restart: a handler marks its outcome, the dispatch
  spine arms the gate (and its backstop), and each transport holds a
  `RestartOnDrop` across its send. REST releases it when hyper drops the body
  rather than before axum has the response; the TSP empty-body return and a
  DIDComm pack failure no longer wait out the 30s backstop.
- `pnm services didcomm enable` opens its ping session inside the readiness
  retry, so a session that will not open yet is waited out, not reported as a
  failed enable.
- `messaging.setup_acl` in the tenant overlay is recorded as a deliberate
  allowlist entry (struct docs, tenant-config-allowlist §3.3), with its
  neighbours kept baked by the poison test.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(services): a soft restart reads the config the generation ran with

An attested soft restart brought the next generation up with DIDComm
enabled and no mediator, so messaging never started and `pnm services
didcomm enable` waited out its 300s readiness poll.

There are two `AppConfig` values at runtime. `run()` owns a local one,
then `build_app_state(config.clone(), …)` wraps a *copy* in the shared
`Arc<RwLock<AppConfig>>`. Every runtime operation that persists
configuration — `enable_didcomm` among them — mutates the shared copy;
`run()`'s local never sees those writes.

That divergence was latent until the attested reload stopped reading
config.toml and returned `self.clone()` instead. `self` was `run()`'s
local, so the clone carried the boot config: `messaging: None`. Meanwhile
`services.didcomm` is re-read from fjall, which does say enabled — hence
enabled-with-no-mediator. Non-TEE was unaffected: with no attestation
digest the reload re-reads the file, which `persist_didcomm_enabled`
had written.

`reload_config_for_restart` now takes `&Arc<RwLock<AppConfig>>` and reads
the live config, rather than accepting any `AppConfig` a caller hands it.
The shared handle is the only value of that type in the process, so a
detached snapshot no longer compiles at the call site — the stale value
is unpassable rather than merely not-passed.

`reload_for_restart` itself is unchanged; its input was always documented
as "the running configuration", and the caller was what broke that.

Adds `soft_restart_keeps_a_mediator_enabled_at_runtime`, which mutates
only the shared copy the way `enable_didcomm` does and asserts the next
generation keeps the mediator. It is attested on purpose: that is the
branch that never consults the file, where a stale snapshot has no
backstop. Verified to fail without the fix.

Signed-off-by: Yaroslava Kurash <yaroslava.k@affinidi.com>

body:
The Release PR for every package in this repo. **Merging this is the release.**

| Package | Registry | Version | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trust-tasks` | crates.io | `0.30.0` → `0.30.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-capability-client` | crates.io | `0.30.0` → `0.30.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm` | crates.io | `0.30.0` → `0.30.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-didcomm-v1` | crates.io | `0.30.0` → `0.30.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-https` | crates.io | `0.30.0` → `0.30.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-proof` | crates.io | `0.30.0` → `0.30.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-rs` | crates.io | `0.30.0` → `0.30.1` | patch |
| `trust-tasks-tsp` | crates.io | `0.30.0` → `0.30.1` | patch |
| `@openvtc/trust-tasks` | npm | `0.25.0` → `0.25.1` | patch |
| `github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/trust-tasks-go` | Go (tag `trust-tasks-go/v0.7.1`) | `0.7.0` → `0.7.1` | patch |
| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.7.0` → `0.7.1` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: build(codegen): replace serde_yaml with serde-saphyr (RUSTSEC-2024-0449)
body:
`cargo deny` is failing on `main` (since #753) and on the Release PR #754: RUSTSEC-2024-0449 marks `unsafe-libyaml` unmaintained, with no safe upgrade. Its only path into the graph is `serde_yaml 0.9` (deprecated) in `trust-tasks-codegen`, which is `publish = false`.

Rather than adding another `deny.toml` ignore, this swaps the codegen's front-matter parser to `serde-saphyr` (the safe-Rust alternative the advisory recommends), deserialising straight into `serde_json::Value`.

title: feat(provision/vta): add the VTA Farm claim and redeem tasks for the vta-claim trigger-link flow
body:
## What it adds

The `provision/vta/*` family: how a wallet claims a VTA that a VTA Farm reserved behind a `vta-claim` trigger link (VTI-LNK-110 to VTI-LNK-117 in trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#58), and how it receives the hand-over once the person has confirmed the claim check on the Farm's page. Two tasks at `https://trusttasks.org/spec/provision/vta/<task>/0.1`, patterned on `auth/oob/claim` and `auth/oob/redeem`:

- **`claim`**: the first request of the trigger link. Payload `{ handle }`, equal to `parentThreadId`, signed by a fresh Ed25519 `did:key` for `authentication`; that key becomes the VTA's administrator, so there is no payload member through which another key could be named. The Farm locks the reservation to the key and answers a `trust-task-next-step` (`continuation: proceed`, expecting `redeem`). The task defines **no `#response`**: the outcome is not known until the person confirms or refuses the claim check, so nothing signed says "claimed" before it is true.
- **`redeem`**: the claimant long-polls with the same key. The Farm holds each poll up to 25 s and answers `redeem:pending` (`details.state` in `claimed`, `confirmed`, `provisioning`, plus `confirmBy` while a confirmation is awaited), `redeem:rejected` when the person said "Not mine", or the terminal `#response` once the key is written into the VTA and the VTA answers: `handle`, `vtaDid`, `operation` (`provisionVta` | `grantAcl`), and optionally `mediatorDid` and `didLogUrl`. Signed by the Farm for `assertionMethod`; the wallet keeps it as its record of the VTA.
- **`_shared/0.1`**: `vta.schema.json` with `Handle`, and `CONVENTIONS.md` with the reservation state machine (`open → claimed → confirmed → provisioning → released`; `rejected`, `lapsed` final) and the family codes `provision/vta:keyUnsupported`, `handleNotFound`, `handleExpired`, `notClaimant`. Task codes: `claim:alreadyClaimed`, `redeem:pending`, `redeem:rejected`. `keyUnsupported` mirrors `auth/oob:keyUnsupported` but cannot reuse it, since SPEC §8.5 confines an extended code's namespace to the emitting slug or a proper prefix of it.
- **Invalid examples** for both tasks, including a claimant-supplied `adminDid`, a wallet-asserted `confirmed`, a Farm-supplied `claimCheck`, the snake_case `provision_vta`, and a URL with userinfo.
- **Generated bindings** for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart.

The first push of this PR had a single task whose `#response` carried the VTA DID at the moment of acceptance; Vincent's review on the Farm side pointed out that this signed a success for an exchange the person could still refuse, and that a resend would replay it after the hold lapsed. The second commit is the fix described above.

## Why `provision/` and not `vta/`

The slug was floated on the VTI PR as `vta/claim`. `specs/vta/*` is the family of tasks a VTA itself consumes, and these tasks are consumed by a Farm, so they sit with `provision/integration`. Happy to move them if you want them elsewhere.

## Backwards compatibility

Additive. Every file is new except the generated index files, which only gain lines. No existing spec, schema, `$id`, Type URI or generated binding changes. No generator or tooling changes; no version bumps or changelog entries, per RELEASING.md.

## Testing

Run in a container with Node 24, Go, Dart and Rust:

- `TT_STRICT_SECURITY_PRIVACY=1 npm run build` passes: both specs validate, every example validates against the framework envelope schema, and the Security & Privacy lint passes in strict mode.
- `cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen && cargo fmt --all`, `npm run build-ts-bindings`, `npm run build-go-bindings` and `npm run build-dart-bindings` regenerated; `npm run check-bindings` reports the four languages agree; `npm test` in `trust-tasks-ts` passes 79/79.

## Related

- VTI spec: https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec/pull/58
- Farm implementation: https://github.com/ic3software/vtafarm-api/issues/75

A #response is terminal, and the claim's was issued while the person could still refuse the claim check on the Farm's page, so a Farm-signed success could describe an exchange that ended with nothing granted and be replayed after the hold lapsed. The claim now defines no response and answers a trust-task-next-step (continuation proceed) expecting provision/vta/redeem/0.1; redeem long-polls like auth/oob/redeem with pending (claimed, confirmed, provisioning), rejected, or the terminal hand-over once the key is written and the VTA answers. title: Update the explore walkthrough for the VTI-Eucalyptus release
body:
VTI-Eucalyptus ships VTA 0.50.0, Mediator 0.37.0 and a DID Hosting Daemon whose setup wizard no longer runs on a headless box: since 0.8.3 it refuses to continue without an OS keychain and no longer offers plaintext secrets interactively. The only way to keep the throwaway explore flow working is the non-interactive setup recipe, which still allows plaintext when `confirm_plaintext = true` is set explicitly.

- sysop/explore/01-server-setup.md: point the prebuilt-binary heading and the three `git checkout` lines at the VTI-Eucalyptus tag.
- sysop/explore/02-walkthrough.md: bump the VTA version to 0.50.0 and the Mediator version to 0.37.0 in the "Verified with" table.
- Step 4: replace the DID Hosting Daemon wizard tables with a `daemon.toml` recipe run twice via `did-hosting-daemon setup --from`, first as `offline-prepare` and then as `offline-complete` with the bundle path and expected digest added. Update the printed output for both phases and for the sealed bundle (template is now `did-host-didcomm`).
- The admin did:key is now generated in phase 2, so `vta contexts create` no longer takes `--admin-did`, and the saved values are renumbered: 4a digest, 4b DID Host DID, 4c Admin DID. The enrollment command now also prints a claim code the browser asks for.
- Drop the manual TSP selection in the VTA and Mediator wizards, which now default to both protocols.
- Add the new "Second administrator DID" prompt to the VTC wizard, and add an `[acl] single_admin_mode = true` step before starting the VTC, since the explore box has only one admin and the setting is config-only.

title: [OpenVTC, VTC] Cross-mediator join request does not appear in VTC Admin Panel
body:
## Summary

When my Personal VTA uses a different mediator from the VTC, submitting a Join Community request from OpenVTC does not result in any visible join request in the VTC Admin Panel.

The Mediator ACL setting is as the following:

```toml
mediator_acl_mode = "explicit_deny"
global_acl_default = "ALLOW_ALL"
```

And the recipe setup is as the following:

```
[security]
network_mode = "open"
```

I'm not sure whether there is an additional configuration required for cross-mediator communication or whether the request is getting lost somewhere in the routing path.

## Environment

- VTA: 0.12.46
- Mediator: 0.17.12
- DIDs: 0.8.2
- VTC: 0.11.37
- OpenVTC: 0.2.1

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure the Personal VTA to use a mediator different from the VTC mediator.
2. Launch OpenVTC.
3. Select Join Community.
4. Enter the VTC DID.
5. Submit the join request.
6. Check the VTC Admin Panel.

## Expected behavior

If two mediators network configured as Open, I would expect the join request to reach the VTC and appear in the Admin Panel.

## Actual behavior

No join request appears in the VTC Admin Panel.

title: Specify trigger links: the QR code or link that starts an exchange with a wallet (VTI-LNK-001 – 124)
body:
## Summary

Adds a chapter, **Trigger Links** (`spec/07a-links.md`, area `LNK`, profile `Links`), for the text an inviter shows as a QR code or a link so that whichever wallet a person uses can start an exchange with it. The chapter has two parts: **the trigger-link format**, which is protocol-neutral, and **VTI's use of trigger links**, which adopts the Trust Task first request (from #59). Two flows are registered: `sign-in`, a person signing in to a service's portal (a VTC, or another service such as DID hosting) by scanning or clicking the code it shows, and `vta-claim`, a wallet claiming a VTA from a VTA Farm.

```
https://link.trustoverip.org/t#_from=<VID>&_id=<handle>&_exp=<epoch>&_type=/vti/flow/sign-in/0.1
```

## What the chapter specifies

- **The link.** An `https` URL. Every field a reader uses is in the fragment, which no server receives. Readers ignore unknown names, so appended tracking parameters don't break a link. A repeated reserved name is refused.
- **Reading.** One reading order with named reasons, and five outcomes a person sees (`update`, `expired`, `unreachable`, `pass-on`, `invalid`). The reader never says which field failed.
- **Fields.**
  - `_from` is any VID.
  - `_id` is 16–32 random bytes as unpadded base64url, with one spelling per handle.
  - `_exp` is epoch seconds, with a 60 s clock allowance.
  - `_type` is a versioned flow URI. It may be written as a path that resolves against `https` and the link's lowercased host.
- **Flows.** A registry under `https://link.trustoverip.org/vti/flow/`, governed by this specification, with MAJOR/MINOR version rules.
- **After the link.**
  - Show the contact as unverified before any network activity. There's an exception for contacts already in the reader's records.
  - Verify the DID document, and take the transport only from it.
  - Each flow states its first request (VTI-LNK-057). VTI flows sign it with a fresh Ed25519 `did:key` and carry the handle as `parentThreadId` (VTI-LNK-054).
- **Security of the handle.** It confers nothing, no GET spends it, and readers never log it.
- **Producers.**
  - Emit ASCII only.
  - Keep the `https` form within 251 bytes at QR level M, or 177 at level Q (version 11).
  - Serve pages showing a link with `no-referrer` and `no-store`, with no third-party scripts.
  - Give redirects an explicit fragment.
  - Never put the link host on the page's own domain.
- **Link host.** Association files claim only the trigger path. A no-wallet page never reads the fragment.
- **`sign-in`.**
  - `_exp` is required, at most 300 s.
  - A reader acts only for a service already in its records. For one that isn't, it sends nothing until the person adds it, offering the relationship the verified document advertises (joining a community, or using a DID hosting service), then may continue with the same link (VTI-LNK-101).
  - The contact's document must list a `SignInPortal` service, or the reader stops with `no-portal-service` (VTI-LNK-102).
  - Before the first request the reader shows its own name for the service and the verified portal origin; a different name in a signed reply is flagged before anything else is approved (VTI-LNK-104).
  - The VTC uses a 16-byte handle.
  - Includes a size-budget note.
- **`vta-claim`** (VTI-LNK-110 – 117, added after review by the VTA Farm).
  - The contact is the Farm, not the VTA. `_exp` is required, at most 300 s.
  - The Farm is a first contact, so nothing is resolved before the person continues.
  - The fresh identifier that issues the first request becomes the VTA's administrator.
  - The Farm accepts one claim per handle.
  - A claim check (SHOULD) catches a bystander who scans first: the page and the wallet both show 6 characters derived from the claimed identifier, and the person confirms they match; if not, the Farm discards the identifier and returns the VTA to the pool (VTI-LNK-115).
  - A code that adds an administrator to a running VTA is shown only to the account that already controls it, after the claim check (VTI-LNK-117).
- **The contact rule** (VTI-LNK-118 – 124). A contact qualifies by what the reader can prove, not by naming DID methods, so future methods (`did:scid`, `did:webs`, ledger DIDs) need no spec change:
  - **Route A, host-named:** the DID names the host serving its document (`did:webvh`, `did:web`, `did:webs`).
  - **Route B, domain-linked:** any other method, if the portal's origin serves a DIF Well-Known DID Configuration with a valid Domain Linkage Credential from the DID (JWT EdDSA/ES256 or `eddsa-jcs-2022`), fetched only after the person continues, and served with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Failure is `domain-not-linked`.
  - A reader with no resolver for a method answers `unsupported-vid` (update). `did:key` and `did:peer` are `from-not-allowed`: a peer DID is pairwise, not a service identity.
- **Clicking the code** (VTI-LNK-056, 086, 105): a page SHOULD make its QR code a link to the same text, so a wallet on the same device can be used without scanning. A reader that sees the click, such as a browser extension, records the page's origin. For `sign-in` that origin MUST match the portal origin in the verified document (`wrong-origin`), which stops a page relaying a genuine portal code. This replaces the browser plugin's SIOPv2 login.
- **Path DIDs** (VTI-LNK-050): before the person continues, the reader shows the path as well as the domain.
- **Early resolution** (VTI-LNK-051): after a click on a page, a reader may resolve and verify the contact before the person continues (never for camera scans, pastes or `vta-claim`), and sends nothing to its services.
- **Services with several surfaces** (VTI-LNK-105), such as an operator console, serve them all from the `SignInPortal` origin.

Wiring: `specs.json`, the intro's structure and reading tables, `STRUCTURE.md`, the conformance area, profile and target tables, references, and one glossary term (`trigger link`). `Links` is MAY for every target. VTI-LNK-001 binds any target that reads, produces or hosts trigger links.

## Not in this revision

- **Agent names** in `_from` are reserved (VTI-LNK-032). Readers refuse them with `update` until three things are settled with the agent-names authors: their canonical form, what a community name resolves to, and the redirect contract.
- **The sign-in exchange after the first request** is specified in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#738 (`auth/oob/*`). The chapter notes that the first claimer locks the request.

## Open dependencies outside this PR

- Trust Over IP hosting `link.trustoverip.org`.
- Device tests of fragment survival across camera, browser and OS hand-offs (Keyring). If a platform drops the fragment, the link form needs another answer there.

title: vta-service-v0.58.0
body:
### Added

- **vta-sdk**: Foreign-protocol DID identities — JWK key slots, an unpublished update key, P-256 slots, and a swiyu-verifier template ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2036](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2036))

A VTC that verifies swiyu wallet presentations (OpenID4VP) needs an identity of
  its own, shaped by the Swiss Profile Anchor: a did:webvh with one P-256 key
  published as a publicKeyJwk (publicKeyMultibase is forbidden), no keyAgreement,
  service or @context, the Ed25519 update key kept to the log's updateKeys, and
  portable=false. DID templates could express none of that. This adds what they
  were missing, and the template.

  - `{SLOT}_KEY_JWK`: every key slot now also renders as a JWK object (kty, crv,
    x, y, alg), beside `{SLOT}_KEY_MB`. Either publishes the slot; a JWK
    placeholder for an undeclared slot, or declared as a variable, is refused
    like its multibase twin.
  - `KeySlot::publish` (default true; **breaking** — a new public field). Only the
    `signing` slot, the did:webvh update key, may be `publish: false`, and then
    the document must not use it. Its key record is named by its did:key, as the
    log names it, instead of a guessed `#key-0`.
  - Templates that declare slots but no `ka` slot get no key-agreement key
    published or recorded.
  - Additional signing slots may be P-256 (`derive_p256`'s domain-separated
    derivation).
  - `defaults.portable: false` is binding: the VTA mints the DID non-portable
    whatever the caller asked (pnm defaults to true). Only that direction.
  - Minted key records are matched to the document by publicKeyJwk as well as
    publicKeyMultibase.
  - Built-in `swiyu-verifier` template. Mint it serverless at the swiyu
    identifier-registry slot URL, then upload the log to that slot.



### Fixed

- **tsp**: A relationship accept beaten by a concurrent one was answered, not lost ([#2041](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2041))

Two invites from one peer that arrive together are both recorded first, each
  leaving the pair InviteReceived. The first accept moves it to Bidirectional
  and the second is refused (invalid transition: SendAccept in state
  Bidirectional), which both the VTA and the VTC logged as "could not send a
  TSP relationship accept ... the peer sees no answer". The peer did get an
  answer: an accept for the same pair went out a moment earlier, and receiving
  any accept completes its side.

  Seen at gt-vta on 2026-10-11 against the browser wallet, whose mediator
  socket was being replaced in a loop (fixed in vta-browser-plugin #319), so
  its invites arrived in pairs.

  accept_refusal_is_benign (vti_common::relationship_store) decides it the way
  the SDK's invite_refusal_is_benign does: re-read the relationship state after
  the refusal rather than match the error text (R3.7). Bidirectional means the
  invite was answered and is logged at debug; anything else is a real failure
  and keeps the warning. Both services use the one helper.

title: vta-keyspaces-v0.15.0
body:
### Added

- **vta**: External accounts — short-lived provider credentials with no inbound surface ([#2016](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2016))

* feat(vta): external-accounts capabilities and keyspaces

  Adds the two capabilities the external/* family (trust-tasks-tf #740) gates on: external-accounts-manage, derived by admin alone, and external-auth-use, derived by every role that holds sign (the account's binding, not the role, bounds a consumer). Both are non-additive members of the non-exhaustive Capability enum.

  Registers two keyspaces: external_accounts (settings, bindings, state) in BACKED_UP, and external_secrets (wrapped provider secrets) in EXCLUDED_FROM_BACKUP, so a portable password-protected backup is never a way to take a provider secret away. DID deletion: an account's binding names its consumer, so external_accounts blocks; external_secrets is unrelated.

  The device-binding Capability registry (device/_shared 0.2) does not list the two yet, so device listings carry them under ext until it does.

title: pnm-cli-v0.38.0
body:
### Added

- **rooms**: Pnm rooms file put/get, and signed sealed bodies for rooms put/get ([#2037](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2037))

A member can now put a file in a sealed room and fetch it from the CLI, end to
  end (data-rooms-files.md P6), and `pnm rooms put`/`get` work on sealed rooms.

  Sealed record body (vtc_client::rooms::body). This implements
  `SealedRecordBody` (rooms/_shared/0.1/room.schema.json,
  trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#747): the JSON inside a sealed record. It is
  signed by its author with a Data Integrity proof (eddsa-jcs-2022, or
  ecdsa-jcs-2019 for P-256) and names the room, key and version it was written
  for. `verify_record_body` is the only way to a `VerifiedRecordBody`. It
  refuses, rather than warns about, a body that:
  - names an unknown member or breaks a bound;
  - carries a proof that does not verify for `author` for assertionMethod, or
    uses another suite;
  - was signed for another location;
  - on attributed, was signed by someone other than the author the host recorded.
  There is no generated type for the body, because no host task carries it (the
  same as FileManifest).

  pnm rooms put on a sealed room:
  - reads the tier from `rooms/info`, signs the body as the operator, and seals
    it through the VTA's `rooms/keys/seal`, which seals what it is given and
    signs nothing;
  - predicts the version from the room head. The host assigns versions from a
    room-wide counter, so a write that lands at another version is re-sealed at
    the next one and rewritten over exactly what landed, up to 4 times, then
    named with the --expected-version to retry with.
  Without a file, `put` and `get` stay on records 0.1, which the VTC host serves.

  pnm rooms get:
  - verifies the sealed body before showing it;
  - reads `sealed` as the object the host returns. It had read it as a bare
    string, so it could open no sealed record.

  pnm rooms file put/get. A file is sealed and opened locally with one file's
  key from the VTA. `put` seals the file, uploads its ciphertext (begin, the
  missing chunks, commit; abort on failure), checks the committed blobRef, then
  writes a create-only record (records/put 0.2) whose signed body carries the
  FileManifest. `get` writes nothing unless every check holds:
  - the body is verified;
  - the blob is named on the record and is the one the author named;
  - each chunk matches the manifest;
  - the plaintext matches the author's digest.
  Another member's text has control characters stripped, and a file name keeps
  only its last path component, never written over an existing file. Files need
  records/put 0.2, which room-host serves and the VTC does not yet.

  Client calls:
  - vtc-client: begin/upload/commit/abort, get_blob/download_chunk, room_info,
    get_record_v2 and put_sealed_record_with_blobs, on the generated
    trust_tasks_rs types;
  - vta-sdk: VtaClient::room_seal, and
    trust_task_sign::sign_object_for_assertion for signing an object that is
    not a Trust Task.

title: vti-rooms-v0.13.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: Serve room files — blobs, records 0.2 and rooms/info, off until enabled ([#2040](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2040))

A community VTC now hosts room files the way room-host does
  (data-rooms-files.md P5), so `pnm rooms file put/get` works against a VTC.

  One implementation for both hosts: vti_rooms::blob_tasks. room-host's file
  handlers mapped each task onto BlobHost, with the spec's declared codes and
  generated response types. That mapping moves into vti-rooms. Each function
  takes the room, the authenticated presenter and the chain's authorization,
  and returns a body checked against the generated response type, or a Refusal
  the host renders. room-host keeps only its transport, parsing and chain
  verification, and its 47 tests pass unchanged. The VTC renders the same
  results through its own reply helpers, so the two hosts cannot answer one task
  two ways.

  The VTC:
  - registers, by generated payload type: rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,chunk,
    commit,abort}, rooms/blobs/{get,chunk}, rooms/info and
    rooms/records/{put,get,list} 0.2, and adds them to the shared
    ROOMS_DISPATCHED_URIS, pinned against the registry;
  - uses the same record path as room-host. put (0.1 too, since a rewrite that
    names no blobs releases them) holds prepare_record across the write and
    applies it after. A curate that retracts releases the record's blobs.
    get/list 0.2 read under a snapshot;
  - holds a BlobHost in AppState and runs a GC sweeper;
  - adds the keyspaces room_blobs (backed up: the index and usage) and
    room_blob_transfers (excluded: transfers in flight);
  - has a new `[rooms.files]` section mirroring room-host's flags.

  **Uploads are off by default** on a VTC (`enabled = false`). Until storage
  configs exist, a file goes to a local directory under limits that apply to
  every room alike, and an operator should choose that. When off, `begin`
  answers filesDisabled, while stored files and records without files are still
  served. room-host, a standalone host, keeps its default.

  Size gate. Upload chunks (360 KiB) and begin (320 KiB) declare sizes above the
  64 KiB default, which the VTC granted only to issuers with an ACL entry, and
  room members hold none. Room tasks now count as served for sizes. A large
  upload/chunk is admitted only from a claimed issuer holding an open, unexpired
  upload here (BlobHost::holds_open_upload). A large begin is admitted only when
  uploads are on and its payload names a room hosted here. Both are charged to
  the same per-address LargeDocumentBudget, and a claim that fails verification
  doubles the address's cost, like any other.

  rooms/info's specification said RECOMMENDED for its proof, though the chain
  must bind to the signer. trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#750 makes it
  REQUIRED. Until that reaches trust-tasks-rs, an interim
  DISPATCHED_WITHOUT_PROOF entry records why the rooms arm refuses an unsigned
  caller anyway. The census fails once the specification agrees, which forces
  the entry out with that bump.
