title: vta-sdk-v0.66.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: OpenID4VP wallet sessions — swiyu wallets present evidence for a join ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2044](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2044))

A swiyu wallet speaks OpenID4VP 1.0 over HTTPS and signs no Trust Task, so the
  applicant's own agent opens the exchange for it. The VTC now serves the whole
  round trip against an installed verifier identity ([#2039](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2039)).

  - `vtc/join-requests/wallet-session/start/0.1`: the proof signer opens a
    session for a criterion named by its `requirementsDigest` (and optionally
    their own join request). The VTC signs an ES256 request object as a JAR in
    swiyu's profile (`profile_version`, `aud` https://self-issued.me/v2,
    `client_id` `decentralized_identifier:<did>`), asking for the criterion's
    published DCQL query unchanged, with a fresh nonce, `state` and P-256
    response key, and returns the `swiyu-verify://` wallet URI. Every declared
    code is served: criterionNotFound, noWalletPresentation,
    verifierNotConfigured, requestNotFound (unknown and somebody else's alike),
    requestClosed, tooManySessions.
  - `GET /v1/oid4vp/request/{session}` answers the request object once;
    `POST /v1/oid4vp/response/{session}` accepts one `direct_post.jwt` answer.
    It is checked in order: decrypts (A256GCM) under the session key and echoes
    `state`; each presentation's issuer signature, validity and KB-JWT over the
    session nonce with the prefixed `client_id` as audience (VTI-CRD-020…022),
    one holder; status valid, never assumed (VTI-CRD-014); every issuer admitted
    by the criterion's `credentialIssuers`; the query satisfied
    (`DcqlQuery::evaluate_presentation`). Both are a declared foreign-protocol
    exception (VTI-OPS-095): REST_EXCEPTIONS and GOVERNED_UNAUTH rows, behind the
    unauthenticated governor; the response reads its body against
    `[oid4vp] max_response_bytes`.
  - `vtc/join-requests/wallet-session/status/0.1`: only the signer who opened a
    session reads it; the evidence names the wallet's holder key beside the
    applicant and each credential's query id, format, issuer and vct, never a
    claim value; a refusal names its reason.
  - New keyspace `oid4vp_sessions`, encrypted at rest, excluded from backup. A
    minute sweeper closes unanswered sessions at `expiresAt` (dropping the
    response key) and drops records an hour after closing, or when held evidence
    lapses. State changes run under one lock, so one response wins.
  - `[oid4vp]` config: session TTL, open sessions per applicant, evidence hold,
    response cap, default identity, wallet URI scheme.
  - Workspace floors: affinidi-openid4vp 0.1.4 (`direct-post-jwt`),
    affinidi-oid4vc-core 0.1.10 (`jwe`), affinidi-sd-jwt 0.1.7;
    trust-tasks-rs 0.28.1 for the wallet-session specs.

  Evidence is recorded on the session. Deciding a join on it — on the named
  request, or on the applicant's next submission — follows. P3 of
  docs/05-design-notes/oid4vp-wallet-verifier.md; docs/03-vtc/oid4vp-verifier.md
  covers operating it.

- SignInPortal in did-host-http* templates and a VTC DID self-check for wallet sign-in ([#2042](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2042))

* feat(vta-sdk): advertise SignInPortal from the did-host-http* templates

  Wallet sign-in with a trigger link (auth/oob, contract C4/C9) needs the
  service's DID document to list SignInPortal on the origin of its login
  page. DID hosting publishes <origin>/login for itself, but a node minted
  from a did-host-http* template lacked the entry, so wallets refused its
  sign-in links with "This code can't be used" (webvh.storm.ws).

  did-host-http, did-host-http-tsp and did-host-http-didcomm now declare
  SERVICE_SIGN_IN_PORTAL (null default, bare service member). When a
  template declares it and the caller does not supply it, the renderer
  derives { id: <did>#sign-in-portal, type: SignInPortal,
  serviceEndpoint: <origin of URL>/login } from URL, https only. A caller
  may supply its own entry or null to omit it. Templates for nodes with no
  login page (did-host-didcomm, did-host-tsp, didcomm-mediator) are
  unchanged. Existing DIDs are untouched; the doc explains adding the
  entry with pnm did-mgmt dids edit.

  New public helpers: sign_in_portal_endpoint, sign_in_portal_service,
  SIGN_IN_PORTAL_SERVICE_TYPE, SIGN_IN_PORTAL_SERVICE_VAR.

- **rooms**: Pnm rooms file put/get, and signed sealed bodies for rooms put/get ([#2037](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2037))

A member can now put a file in a sealed room and fetch it from the CLI, end to
  end (data-rooms-files.md P6), and `pnm rooms put`/`get` work on sealed rooms.

  Sealed record body (vtc_client::rooms::body). This implements
  `SealedRecordBody` (rooms/_shared/0.1/room.schema.json,
  trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#747): the JSON inside a sealed record. It is
  signed by its author with a Data Integrity proof (eddsa-jcs-2022, or
  ecdsa-jcs-2019 for P-256) and names the room, key and version it was written
  for. `verify_record_body` is the only way to a `VerifiedRecordBody`. It
  refuses, rather than warns about, a body that:
  - names an unknown member or breaks a bound;
  - carries a proof that does not verify for `author` for assertionMethod, or
    uses another suite;
  - was signed for another location;
  - on attributed, was signed by someone other than the author the host recorded.
  There is no generated type for the body, because no host task carries it (the
  same as FileManifest).

  pnm rooms put on a sealed room:
  - reads the tier from `rooms/info`, signs the body as the operator, and seals
    it through the VTA's `rooms/keys/seal`, which seals what it is given and
    signs nothing;
  - predicts the version from the room head. The host assigns versions from a
    room-wide counter, so a write that lands at another version is re-sealed at
    the next one and rewritten over exactly what landed, up to 4 times, then
    named with the --expected-version to retry with.
  Without a file, `put` and `get` stay on records 0.1, which the VTC host serves.

  pnm rooms get:
  - verifies the sealed body before showing it;
  - reads `sealed` as the object the host returns. It had read it as a bare
    string, so it could open no sealed record.

  pnm rooms file put/get. A file is sealed and opened locally with one file's
  key from the VTA. `put` seals the file, uploads its ciphertext (begin, the
  missing chunks, commit; abort on failure), checks the committed blobRef, then
  writes a create-only record (records/put 0.2) whose signed body carries the
  FileManifest. `get` writes nothing unless every check holds:
  - the body is verified;
  - the blob is named on the record and is the one the author named;
  - each chunk matches the manifest;
  - the plaintext matches the author's digest.
  Another member's text has control characters stripped, and a file name keeps
  only its last path component, never written over an existing file. Files need
  records/put 0.2, which room-host serves and the VTC does not yet.

  Client calls:
  - vtc-client: begin/upload/commit/abort, get_blob/download_chunk, room_info,
    get_record_v2 and put_sealed_record_with_blobs, on the generated
    trust_tasks_rs types;
  - vta-sdk: VtaClient::room_seal, and
    trust_task_sign::sign_object_for_assertion for signing an object that is
    not a Trust Task.

- **vta-sdk**: Foreign-protocol DID identities — JWK key slots, an unpublished update key, P-256 slots, and a swiyu-verifier template ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2036](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2036))

A VTC that verifies swiyu wallet presentations (OpenID4VP) needs an identity of
  its own, shaped by the Swiss Profile Anchor: a did:webvh with one P-256 key
  published as a publicKeyJwk (publicKeyMultibase is forbidden), no keyAgreement,
  service or @context, the Ed25519 update key kept to the log's updateKeys, and
  portable=false. DID templates could express none of that. This adds what they
  were missing, and the template.

  - `{SLOT}_KEY_JWK`: every key slot now also renders as a JWK object (kty, crv,
    x, y, alg), beside `{SLOT}_KEY_MB`. Either publishes the slot; a JWK
    placeholder for an undeclared slot, or declared as a variable, is refused
    like its multibase twin.
  - `KeySlot::publish` (default true; **breaking** — a new public field). Only the
    `signing` slot, the did:webvh update key, may be `publish: false`, and then
    the document must not use it. Its key record is named by its did:key, as the
    log names it, instead of a guessed `#key-0`.
  - Templates that declare slots but no `ka` slot get no key-agreement key
    published or recorded.
  - Additional signing slots may be P-256 (`derive_p256`'s domain-separated
    derivation).
  - `defaults.portable: false` is binding: the VTA mints the DID non-portable
    whatever the caller asked (pnm defaults to true). Only that direction.
  - Minted key records are matched to the document by publicKeyJwk as well as
    publicKeyMultibase.
  - Built-in `swiyu-verifier` template. Mint it serverless at the swiyu
    identifier-registry slot URL, then upload the log to that slot.

## `vti-common`
## [0.41.2](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-common-v0.41.1...vti-common-v0.41.2) — 2026-10-11 ### Fixed - **tsp**: A relationship accept beaten by a concurrent one was answered, not lost ([#2041](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2041)) Two invites from one peer that arrive together are both recorded first, each leaving the pair InviteReceived. The first accept moves it to Bidirectional and the second is refused (invalid transition: SendAccept in state Bidirectional), which both the VTA and the VTC logged as "could not send a TSP relationship accept ... the peer sees no answer". The peer did get an answer: an accept for the same pair went out a moment earlier, and receiving any accept completes its side. Seen at gt-vta on 2026-10-11 against the browser wallet, whose mediator socket was being replaced in a loop (fixed in vta-browser-plugin #319), so its invites arrived in pairs. accept_refusal_is_benign (vti_common::relationship_store) decides it the way the SDK's invite_refusal_is_benign does: re-read the relationship state after the refusal rather than match the error text (R3.7). Bidirectional means the invite was answered and is logged at debug; anything else is a real failure and keeps the warning. Both services use the one helper.
## `vti-rooms`
## [0.12.1](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vti-rooms-v0.12.0...vti-rooms-v0.12.1) — 2026-10-11 ### Added - **vtc**: Serve room files — blobs, records 0.2 and rooms/info, off until enabled ([#2040](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2040)) A community VTC now hosts room files the way room-host does (data-rooms-files.md P5), so `pnm rooms file put/get` works against a VTC. One implementation for both hosts: vti_rooms::blob_tasks. room-host's file handlers mapped each task onto BlobHost, with the spec's declared codes and generated response types. That mapping moves into vti-rooms. Each function takes the room, the authenticated presenter and the chain's authorization, and returns a body checked against the generated response type, or a Refusal the host renders. room-host keeps only its transport, parsing and chain verification, and its 47 tests pass unchanged. The VTC renders the same results through its own reply helpers, so the two hosts cannot answer one task two ways. The VTC: - registers, by generated payload type: rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,chunk, commit,abort}, rooms/blobs/{get,chunk}, rooms/info and rooms/records/{put,get,list} 0.2, and adds them to the shared ROOMS_DISPATCHED_URIS, pinned against the registry; - uses the same record path as room-host. put (0.1 too, since a rewrite that names no blobs releases them) holds prepare_record across the write and applies it after. A curate that retracts releases the record's blobs. get/list 0.2 read under a snapshot; - holds a BlobHost in AppState and runs a GC sweeper; - adds the keyspaces room_blobs (backed up: the index and usage) and room_blob_transfers (excluded: transfers in flight); - has a new `[rooms.files]` section mirroring room-host's flags. **Uploads are off by default** on a VTC (`enabled = false`). Until storage configs exist, a file goes to a local directory under limits that apply to every room alike, and an operator should choose that. When off, `begin` answers filesDisabled, while stored files and records without files are still served. room-host, a standalone host, keeps its default. Size gate. Upload chunks (360 KiB) and begin (320 KiB) declare sizes above the 64 KiB default, which the VTC granted only to issuers with an ACL entry, and room members hold none. Room tasks now count as served for sizes. A large upload/chunk is admitted only from a claimed issuer holding an open, unexpired upload here (BlobHost::holds_open_upload). A large begin is admitted only when uploads are on and its payload names a room hosted here. Both are charged to the same per-address LargeDocumentBudget, and a claim that fails verification doubles the address's cost, like any other. rooms/info's specification said RECOMMENDED for its proof, though the chain must bind to the signer. trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#750 makes it REQUIRED. Until that reaches trust-tasks-rs, an interim DISPATCHED_WITHOUT_PROOF entry records why the rooms arm refuses an unsigned caller anyway. The census fails once the specification agrees, which forces the entry out with that bump.

Client calls: - vtc-client: begin/upload/commit/abort, get_blob/download_chunk, room_info, get_record_v2 and put_sealed_record_with_blobs, on the generated trust_tasks_rs types; - vta-sdk: VtaClient::room_seal, and trust_task_sign::sign_object_for_assertion for signing an object that is not a Trust Task.
## `pnm-cli`
## [0.37.2](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/pnm-cli-v0.37.1...pnm-cli-v0.37.2) — 2026-10-11 ### Added - **rooms**: Pnm rooms file put/get, and signed sealed bodies for rooms put/get ([#2037](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2037)) A member can now put a file in a sealed room and fetch it from the CLI, end to end (data-rooms-files.md P6), and `pnm rooms put`/`get` work on sealed rooms. Sealed record body (vtc_client::rooms::body). This implements `SealedRecordBody` (rooms/_shared/0.1/room.schema.json, trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#747): the JSON inside a sealed record. It is signed by its author with a Data Integrity proof (eddsa-jcs-2022, or ecdsa-jcs-2019 for P-256) and names the room, key and version it was written for. `verify_record_body` is the only way to a `VerifiedRecordBody`. It refuses, rather than warns about, a body that: - names an unknown member or breaks a bound; - carries a proof that does not verify for `author` for assertionMethod, or uses another suite; - was signed for another location; - on attributed, was signed by someone other than the author the host recorded. There is no generated type for the body, because no host task carries it (the same as FileManifest). pnm rooms put on a sealed room: - reads the tier from `rooms/info`, signs the body as the operator, and seals it through the VTA's `rooms/keys/seal`, which seals what it is given and signs nothing; - predicts the version from the room head. The host assigns versions from a room-wide counter, so a write that lands at another version is re-sealed at the next one and rewritten over exactly what landed, up to 4 times, then named with the --expected-version to retry with. Without a file, `put` and `get` stay on records 0.1, which the VTC host serves. pnm rooms get: - verifies the sealed body before showing it; - reads `sealed` as the object the host returns. It had read it as a bare string, so it could open no sealed record. pnm rooms file put/get. A file is sealed and opened locally with one file's key from the VTA. `put` seals the file, uploads its ciphertext (begin, the missing chunks, commit; abort on failure), checks the committed blobRef, then writes a create-only record (records/put 0.2) whose signed body carries the FileManifest. `get` writes nothing unless every check holds: - the body is verified; - the blob is named on the record and is the one the author named; - each chunk matches the manifest; - the plaintext matches the author's digest. Another member's text has control characters stripped, and a file name keeps only its last path component, never written over an existing file. Files need records/put 0.2, which room-host serves and the VTC does not yet. Client calls: - vtc-client: begin/upload/commit/abort, get_blob/download_chunk, room_info, get_record_v2 and put_sealed_record_with_blobs, on the generated trust_tasks_rs types; - vta-sdk: VtaClient::room_seal, and trust_task_sign::sign_object_for_assertion for signing an object that is not a Trust Task.
## `vta-keys`
## [0.19.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-keys-v0.18.0...vta-keys-v0.19.0) — 2026-10-11 ### Added - **vta-sdk**: Foreign-protocol DID identities — JWK key slots, an unpublished update key, P-256 slots, and a swiyu-verifier template ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2036](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2036)) A VTC that verifies swiyu wallet presentations (OpenID4VP) needs an identity of its own, shaped by the Swiss Profile Anchor: a did:webvh with one P-256 key published as a publicKeyJwk (publicKeyMultibase is forbidden), no keyAgreement, service or @context, the Ed25519 update key kept to the log's updateKeys, and portable=false. DID templates could express none of that. This adds what they were missing, and the template. - `{SLOT}_KEY_JWK`: every key slot now also renders as a JWK object (kty, crv, x, y, alg), beside `{SLOT}_KEY_MB`. Either publishes the slot; a JWK placeholder for an undeclared slot, or declared as a variable, is refused like its multibase twin. - `KeySlot::publish` (default true; **breaking** — a new public field). Only the `signing` slot, the did:webvh update key, may be `publish: false`, and then the document must not use it. Its key record is named by its did:key, as the log names it, instead of a guessed `#key-0`. - Templates that declare slots but no `ka` slot get no key-agreement key published or recorded. - Additional signing slots may be P-256 (`derive_p256`'s domain-separated derivation). - `defaults.portable: false` is binding: the VTA mints the DID non-portable whatever the caller asked (pnm defaults to true). Only that direction. - Minted key records are matched to the document by publicKeyJwk as well as publicKeyMultibase. - Built-in `swiyu-verifier` template. Mint it serverless at the swiyu identifier-registry slot URL, then upload the log to that slot.
## `vta-service`
## [0.58.0](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-service-v0.57.0...vta-service-v0.58.0) — 2026-10-11 ### Added - **vta-sdk**: Foreign-protocol DID identities — JWK key slots, an unpublished update key, P-256 slots, and a swiyu-verifier template ([#1988](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1988)) ([#2036](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2036)) A VTC that verifies swiyu wallet presentations (OpenID4VP) needs an identity of its own, shaped by the Swiss Profile Anchor: a did:webvh with one P-256 key published as a publicKeyJwk (publicKeyMultibase is forbidden), no keyAgreement, service or @context, the Ed25519 update key kept to the log's updateKeys, and portable=false. DID templates could express none of that. This adds what they were missing, and the template. - `{SLOT}_KEY_JWK`: every key slot now also renders as a JWK object (kty, crv, x, y, alg), beside `{SLOT}_KEY_MB`. Either publishes the slot; a JWK placeholder for an undeclared slot, or declared as a variable, is refused like its multibase twin. - `KeySlot::publish` (default true; **breaking** — a new public field). Only the `signing` slot, the did:webvh update key, may be `publish: false`, and then the document must not use it. Its key record is named by its did:key, as the log names it, instead of a guessed `#key-0`. - Templates that declare slots but no `ka` slot get no key-agreement key published or recorded. - Additional signing slots may be P-256 (`derive_p256`'s domain-separated derivation). - `defaults.portable: false` is binding: the VTA mints the DID non-portable whatever the caller asked (pnm defaults to true). Only that direction. - Minted key records are matched to the document by publicKeyJwk as well as publicKeyMultibase. - Built-in `swiyu-verifier` template. Mint it serverless at the swiyu identifier-registry slot URL, then upload the log to that slot. ### Fixed - **tsp**: A relationship accept beaten by a concurrent one was answered, not lost ([#2041](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/2041)) Two invites from one peer that arrive together are both recorded first, each leaving the pair InviteReceived. The first accept moves it to Bidirectional and the second is refused (invalid transition: SendAccept in state Bidirectional), which both the VTA and the VTC logged as "could not send a TSP relationship accept ... the peer sees no answer". The peer did get an answer: an accept for the same pair went out a moment earlier, and receiving any accept completes its side. Seen at gt-vta on 2026-10-11 against the browser wallet, whose mediator socket was being replaced in a loop (fixed in vta-browser-plugin #319), so its invites arrived in pairs. accept_refusal_is_benign (vti_common::relationship_store) decides it the way the SDK's invite_refusal_is_benign does: re-read the relationship state after the refusal rather than match the error text (R3.7). Bidirectional means the invite was answered and is logged at debug; anything else is a real failure and keeps the warning. Both services use the one helper.

title: Runtime evidence request for keys/sign-jws and keys/sign-csr protocol-signature tasks
body:
## Context

This issue asks for runtime evidence or test guidance for the protocol-signature tasks introduced in:

- https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/749

That PR introduces two narrow tasks where the custodian builds the protocol bytes itself before signing:

- `keys/sign-jws/0.1`
- `keys/sign-csr/0.1`

The source/spec description is clear and useful. Downstream RAHP review has treated the change as a source/spec improvement, but it cannot yet close the corresponding runtime assurance questions because we do not have runnable traces or implementation-level evidence for the accepted and rejected cases.

Downstream tracking:

- Consolidated runtime evidence owner: https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit/issues/994
- Evidence scaffold PR: https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit/pull/995
- Case classification PR: https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit/pull/996
- Scope C evidence record PR: https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit/pull/997
- Local downstream runtime capability assessment PR: https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit/pull/998

The downstream conclusion so far is narrow: the available upstream material supports source/spec review, but downstream cannot produce runtime PASS/FAIL evidence because `rahp-toolkit` does not contain a runnable custodian/runtime harness or request fixture set for these tasks.

## Request

Could this repository provide, point to, or document runtime evidence for `keys/sign-jws/0.1` and `keys/sign-csr/0.1`?

The useful form would be one or more of:

1. runnable tests already present in this repository;
2. a fixture set showing valid and invalid requests;
3. command-line or integration-test instructions for exercising the tasks;
4. redacted runtime traces from a conforming implementation;
5. a statement that these are currently specification/binding definitions only and that runtime evidence belongs in another implementation repository.

## Cases we are trying to evidence

The downstream RAHP runtime evidence packet currently tracks the following Scope C cases.

### `C01-valid-sign-jws`

A valid `keys/sign-jws/0.1` request should produce a protocol-valid JWS from custodian-built signing input.

Evidence requested:

- source ref / implementation ref;
- redacted request fixture;
- resulting JWS or digest of the signed artifact;
- confirmation that the custodian constructed the signing input;
- audit / retained-evidence note.

### `C02-sign-jws-prohibited-header`

A `keys/sign-jws/0.1` request with prohibited or unsafe JWS header members should be rejected.

The PR text indicates refusal of at least:

- `alg`
- `crit`
- `b64`
- `jwk`
- `jku`
- `x5u`

Evidence requested:

- invalid request fixture;
- rejection result;
- error or non-positive outcome shape;
- confirmation that no signature is produced.

### `C04-sign-jws-wrong-purpose`

A wrong-purpose or wrong-audience `keys/sign-jws/0.1` request should not produce an authoritative protocol signature.

Evidence requested:

- how purpose/audience is represented, if at all, for this task;
- whether this is enforced by the task schema, the custodian implementation, the requester authority model, or deployment policy;
- accepted/rejected fixture if such enforcement exists;
- statement of non-applicability if purpose/audience is intentionally outside this task.

### `C05-valid-sign-csr`

A valid `keys/sign-csr/0.1` request should produce a constrained CSR binding subject, SANs and key public material.

Evidence requested:

- redacted request fixture;
- resulting CSR or digest/redacted PEM;
- confirmation that the custodian used the key’s own public key;
- confirmation of accepted subject attributes and SAN handling;
- audit / retained-evidence note.

### `C06-sign-csr-wrong-subject`

A wrong-subject CSR request should be rejected, or the boundary should be explicitly described if wrong-subject authority is outside this task.

Evidence requested:

- how requester authority over a CSR subject is determined;
- whether wrong-subject rejection is implemented by the task, custodian, controller, or deployment policy;
- invalid request fixture and rejection trace if available;
- non-applicability rationale if this is intentionally out of scope.

### `C07-sign-csr-arbitrary-extension`

A CSR request attempting arbitrary extensions should be rejected unless explicitly permitted.

The PR text says no extension except `subjectAltName` is requested.

Evidence requested:

- invalid CSR request fixture attempting an arbitrary extension;
- rejection result;
- confirmation that no CSR is produced with the arbitrary extension.

### `C08-generic-sign-substitution`

Generic opaque `keys/sign` should not substitute for protocol-valid `keys/sign-jws/0.1` or `keys/sign-csr/0.1`.

The PR text states that a custodian must not require `sign` for either task, and that a custodian framing `keys/sign` under its opaque signing domain should not accept `sign` in their place.

Evidence requested:

- test or explanation showing that generic `keys/sign` cannot produce a protocol-valid JWS or CSR for these task purposes;
- rejection trace or verification-failure trace;
- implementation guidance for consumers so they do not treat `keys/sign` as a fallback for `sign-jws` or `sign-csr`.

## Evidence format that would be sufficient

Any of the following would be sufficient for downstream assessment:

```yaml
case_id: C01-valid-sign-jws
task: keys/sign-jws/0.1
implementation_ref: "<repo/commit/tag>"
request_fixture: "<path or redacted inline fixture>"
expected_result: PASS
observed_result: PASS
artifact:
  type: jws | csr | rejection | verification_failure
  digest: "<digest if artifact is not included>"
retained_evidence:
  retained:
    - "<audit event / signing input digest / task record>"
  deliberately_not_retained:
    - "<payload / private key / sensitive material>"
notes: "<limits, assumptions, or non-applicability>"
```

Equivalent Markdown, JSON, test logs, or CI references would also work.

## Why this matters

The downstream RAHP assessment is not challenging the source/spec design. It is trying to separate:

- source/spec evidence;
- generated binding evidence;
- runtime implementation evidence;
- retained-evidence / audit evidence;
- non-repudiation and privacy boundaries.

At present, downstream can record that `keys/sign-jws/0.1` and `keys/sign-csr/0.1` are specified as narrow protocol-signing tasks. It cannot yet say that a runtime implementation accepts and rejects the relevant cases as intended.

## Non-goals

This issue is not asking for:

- changes to the Trust Tasks model;
- a RAHP-specific implementation;
- disclosure of private keys, bearer tokens, unredacted payloads, or sensitive runtime logs;
- upstream adoption of the downstream RAHP issue structure.

It is only asking where the runtime evidence for these task constraints should live, or whether it already exists.

## Related downstream links

- Consolidated downstream runtime evidence issue: https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit/issues/994
- Scope C initial evidence records: https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit/pull/997
- Scope C local runtime capability assessment: https://github.com/sankarshanmukhopadhyay/rahp-toolkit/pull/998

title: method(assurance): deliver a usable shared RAHP baseline through upstream convergence
body:
### Lifecycle stage

Not stage-specific

# RAHP upstream convergence: a functionally usable shared baseline

## Context and scope extension

The [maintainer proposal on #9](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/issues/9#issuecomment-6035912760) called for bringing reusable assurance-testing foundations from the downstream toolkit into this repository.

This issue began as a bounded inventory and fit assessment. [Draft PR #18](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/pull/18) supplies that assessment. The scope is now extended to track the sequenced convergence contributions below, informed by a local feasibility exercise. The original assessment remains supporting evidence; this extension does not imply task-force acceptance of every design choice or a wholesale toolkit import.

Use this issue as the parent delivery tracker. #9 remains the source of adoption requirements and feedback. Individual implementation issues/PRs should reference the relevant increment and its acceptance criteria.

## Objective

Deliver an upstream baseline that another working group can productively use to:

1. Select an immutable specification source and its own risk corpus.
2. Verify retained source identity.
3. Execute bounded evaluation checks.
4. Record findings, reasoning, supporting evidence and limitations.
5. Validate and reproduce the examination.
6. Reassess after material change while preserving earlier evidence.

Repository validation, examination results and assurance decisions remain distinct. Successful execution does not establish target assurance or risk acceptance.

## Basis and current evidence

- **#9:** adoption requirements, repository usability and maintainer direction.
- **Draft PR #18:** source-pinned inventory of eight candidate groups and 46 source assets, upstream mapping and proposed dispositions.
- **Local feasibility package:** isolated prototype, exact component/function manifest, proposed patch, 29 passing tests, seven reproduction checks, seven removal checks and TRQP replay compatibility evidence. Reproduction also passed after extracting the package.
- **Existing upstream foundations:** review schema/validator, explicit `--risks` selection, method/corpus structure, adoption documentation and worked examples.

The local exercise used upstream `ab191485b48bca805ea2cc962c2ea9476a65db66` and downstream `af58247e83d0aff4d47650d929bfc6280d9e41d3`. It retained zero corpus errors and 32 warnings with validation dependencies installed.

The feasibility package is a local artifact, not merged upstream evidence. It demonstrates a bounded TRQP examination, not VRC coverage, complete toolkit portability or unfamiliar-adopter success. The prototype's vocabulary parity check does not implement full consolidation, and its evidence sidecar is experimental. Refresh accepted source and pending PR state before implementation, including CI #14.

### Preparation status

- [x] Candidate inventory and upstream overlap assessment prepared in draft PR #18.
- [x] Local dependency trace and exact transfer manifest prepared.
- [x] Isolated bounded examination and negative tests executed.
- [x] Local TRQP replay compatibility and extracted-package reproduction checked.
- [ ] Increment 1 delivered upstream.
- [ ] Increment 2 delivered upstream.
- [ ] Increment 3 delivered upstream.
- [ ] Increment 4 delivered upstream.
- [ ] Increment 5 delivered upstream.
- [ ] Increment 6 aligned downstream with accepted upstream contracts.
- [ ] Increment 7 qualified and released.

Checked preparation items mean the stated work was performed; they do not mean upstream acceptance or completion of an implementation increment.

## Proposed architectural choices

| Topic | Proposed approach |
|---|---|
| First subject | TRQP first to establish the demonstrated foundations; VRC Spec 0.3 second to demonstrate reuse |
| Source acquisition | Explicitly supplied retained source initially; automated retrieval only when needed |
| Risk selection | Reuse upstream's existing `--risks` interface |
| Evaluation | Keep specification-specific checks alongside their examples |
| Assessment | Reuse the upstream review format, with explicit reasoning and limitations |
| Evidence representation | Start with a documented, structurally validated example-local sidecar; reconsider standardization after the second examination |
| Validation | Compose corpus and review checks through a supported entry point |
| Vocabulary | Maintain consistent definitions with tested schema synchronization |
| Transfer boundary | Move demonstrated foundations; retain controllers, portfolio routing, full engine contracts and bulk catalogue transfer downstream |

## Delivery sequence

### Increment 1 — Retained-source integrity and TRQP replay

**Purpose:** establish a reproducible source-to-observation path.

**Components**

- Extract and harden source-integrity verification from downstream `examples/standalone-trqp/replay.py::source_integrity` into a small helper, provisionally `review/source_integrity.py::verify_source`.
- Adapt `authorization_examples` and `replay` into an upstream real-source example without downstream orchestration dependencies.
- Retain the source manifest, source bytes, attribution, constructed fixtures and expected results.
- Add the example walkthrough and negative tests.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Target and method revisions are explicit.
- [ ] Altered, missing, unsafe or duplicate source entries are rejected.
- [ ] Positive and negative checks reproduce.
- [ ] Schema validity and semantic correctness remain distinguishable.
- [ ] Constructed fixtures and unassessed runtime behavior are identified.
- [ ] Execution requires no downstream checkout.

**Proposed commit:** `test(adoption): add retained-source specification replay`

### Increment 2 — Evidence-linked assessment

**Purpose:** connect observations to an inspectable RAHP assessment.

**Components**

- Reuse `review/spec-review.schema.json` and `review/validate_spec_review.py::validate_record`.
- Add the bounded examination adapter, provisionally `review/examine.py`.
- Define and validate the example-local evidence sidecar.
- Record justified risk references, inference, limitations and proposed treatment.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Review target matches the retained-source manifest.
- [ ] Evidence references resolve and cover every finding.
- [ ] Missing evidence and execution failures cannot become assurance success.
- [ ] Example-local hypotheses are distinguished from canonical corpus records.
- [ ] Existing review records remain valid.
- [ ] Missing authority, delegation and revocation evidence remains explicitly unassessed.

**Design question:** settle the sidecar's structure and relationship to the review record before treating it as a reusable contract. The current review schema disallows extra evidence/reasoning members; do not bypass that constraint with undocumented additions.

**Proposed commit:** `feat(review): bind examination evidence to review records`

### Increment 3 — Vocabulary and validation consolidation

**Purpose:** make the baseline consistent and convenient to operate.

**Components**

- Consolidate review vocabulary definitions.
- Implement schema synchronization or shared runtime checks.
- Compose corpus and explicitly selected review validation.
- Preserve existing commands and distinguish normal records from intentionally invalid fixtures.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Existing vocabulary meanings and valid records remain compatible.
- [ ] Vocabulary/schema drift is detected.
- [ ] Unknown risks, duplicate finding IDs, invalid values and missing resolution evidence are rejected.
- [ ] Invalid teaching fixtures are exercised through negative tests.
- [ ] Errors, warnings and exit behavior are documented.

**Proposed commit:** `feat(validation): compose review checks with shared vocabulary`

### Increment 4 — Validation hardening and CI evidence

**Purpose:** ensure successful checks mean the required validation actually occurred.

**Components**

- Reject missing schema-validation dependencies.
- Integrate with the CI contribution in #14 without duplicating its workflow.
- Preserve execution provenance, warnings, reports and generated-output evidence.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Missing dependencies cannot produce a misleading complete-validation result.
- [ ] Failed, skipped and incomplete checks remain distinguishable.
- [ ] Relevant checks run against the proposed changes.
- [ ] CI output distinguishes repository integrity from target assurance.
- [ ] Reproduction commands and retained evidence are documented.

**Proposed commit:** `fix(validation): reject missing schema-validation dependencies`

### Increment 5 — VRC examination and bounded reassessment

**Purpose:** demonstrate reuse beyond the initial TRQP example.

**Components**

- Recover the exact VRC Spec 0.3 source and relevant historical assessment materials associated with #6.
- Establish source-derived propositions and justified risk mappings.
- Apply the accepted ingestion, evaluation and assessment foundations.
- Demonstrate reassessment at another immutable revision when available.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] VRC source identity, scope and attribution are established.
- [ ] Checks and findings derive from actual source.
- [ ] Earlier records and evidence remain preserved.
- [ ] Changed source cannot silently inherit the previous assessment.
- [ ] Constructed reassessment examples are labeled when real revised-source evidence is unavailable.
- [ ] Findings identify their evidence, reasoning and remaining limitations.

**Dependency:** immutable VRC source reconstruction. The historical #6 description alone does not establish the specification revision to examine.

**Proposed commit:** `test(adoption): add source-pinned VRC examination`

### Increment 6 — Downstream compatibility alignment

**Purpose:** make convergence durable after upstream acceptance.

**Components**

- Consume or reference accepted upstream contracts and shared fixtures.
- Test common positive and negative behavior.
- Identify downstream extensions and version dependencies.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Shared behavior produces compatible results.
- [ ] Upstream versions and source provenance are recorded.
- [ ] Canonical definitions are not maintained in conflicting copies.
- [ ] Downstream extensions remain explicit.
- [ ] Neither repository silently depends on unpublished changes elsewhere.

**Proposed downstream commit:** `test(convergence): verify accepted upstream compatibility`

### Increment 7 — Adoption qualification and release

**Purpose:** establish a baseline another working group can use without contributor assistance.

**Components**

- Conduct an unfamiliar-adopter trial using a different target or instance.
- Resolve observed setup and interpretation gaps.
- Complete supported-workflow documentation and release evidence.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Installation, examination, validation and reassessment instructions are actionable.
- [ ] Trial results and unresolved limitations are retained.
- [ ] Supported and experimental capabilities are clearly distinguished.
- [ ] Documentation links and generated outputs are checked.
- [ ] Release notes identify capabilities, compatibility and reproduction instructions.

**Proposed commit:** `docs(adoption): qualify the shared RAHP baseline`

## Integration queue and maintainer merge order (2026-10-12)

The three implementation PRs are **stacked**, not independent main-branch changes. Review and merge only after the relevant acceptance criteria, CI and contribution checks pass:

1. **[#19 — Increment 1](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/pull/19)**: target `main`; independent review and maintainer acceptance first. Verify tests, source provenance and current-head DCO.
2. **[#20 — Increment 2](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/pull/20)**: currently targets `convergence/issue-17-increment-1`; after #19 merges, **retarget #20 to the then-current `main`**, remove any already-accepted duplicated commits/diff, rerun all regression and examination checks, verify DCO and seek independent review. Merge only the Increment 2 delta.
3. **[#21 — Increment 3](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/pull/21)**: draft, currently targets `convergence/issue-17-increment-2`; after #20 merges, retarget to accepted `main`, reconcile the commit stack without duplicating #19/#20, rerun the corpus/review examples and negative regression tests, verify author-matching DCO on every contribution commit, and seek maintainer review. Do **not** mark ready or merge until these checks are evidenced.

**Related but not on the hard dependency chain:**

- [#14 — CI validation](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/pull/14) targets `main` independently. It may be reviewed/merged before or alongside the above sequence. Before declaring Increment 4 complete, reconcile its workflow with the accepted combined validator; do not install competing workflows or silently assume unmerged CI is active.
- [#18 — baseline assessment](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-rahp-tf/pull/18) remains draft supporting inventory/feasibility evidence, not a prerequisite to #19–#21. Maintainers may request its completion/merge separately.

**Evidence and acceptance boundaries:** PRs #19 and #20 contain reported implementation test evidence and passing current-head DCO assertions, but independent review remains pending. PR #21 contains implementation, tests and documentation. On 2026-10-12, its three commits were reconstructed with author-matching DCO sign-off trailers (head `a3919f221ddcfb934bbbb05aad0db97a65c9506a`), with their exact file trees retained. GitHub EasyCLA is green; automated DCO and test workflows were not returned for that head. Complete-checkout test execution and maintainer review remain pending. GitHub EasyCLA success is **not** DCO proof. Never treat absence of a CI run as PASS or a draft's reported mergeability as substantive review. Any accepted predecessor change can require retargeting and renewed verification. Existing unchecked increment delivery criteria remain unchecked until accepted upstream.

**After #21:** draft PR #22 proposes Increment 4's fail-closed dependency fix; #14 supplies CI evidence after upstream acceptance. Increment 5 exercises source-pinned VRC and reassessment; Increment 6 aligns downstream; Increment 7 qualifies adoption and release. Keep #17 open through those gates.

### Increment 4 implementation and CI qualification status (2026-10-12)

title: Worker: pass a 304 from the asset store through instead of reporting it as a redirect
body:
## Problem

Refreshing any registry page in a browser rendered it unstyled; a second refresh brought the stylesheet back.

A refresh revalidates the cached stylesheet with `If-None-Match`. The worker forwards that header to the Pages asset store, which answers `304 Not Modified`. The redirect guard in `site/_worker.js` treated every 3xx as an asset-layout redirect and turned the 304 into a 500, so the page rendered with no stylesheet. The browser then dropped its cache entry, and the next refresh fetched the stylesheet unconditionally and got a 200, which is why the second refresh looked fine.

Reproducible against production today:

```
$ curl -sS -D - -H 'If-None-Match: "6580ca74306ee78ec5b17d29ab887a35"' https://registry.trustoverip.org/assets/site.css
HTTP/2 500
Asset layout error: /assets/site.css redirected (304). The build must emit <path>.html, not <path>/index.html.
```

The HTML pages would hit the same path if the edge sent an ETag for them; today it does not, so only the stylesheet was affected.

## Change

- A 304 from the asset store is no longer treated as a redirect. It passes through with the same headers a 200 carries (media type, Vary, CORS, Cache-Control, Link) and no body, so the cache entry it refreshes stays consistent.
- The asset-store stub in `site/_worker.test.mjs` now emits an ETag per asset and answers a matching `If-None-Match` with a 304. A new test covers the stylesheet, a negotiated JSON-LD path, and a stale validator still getting the full 200.

## Verification

- `docker compose run --rm test`: 26 pass. The new test fails with `actual: 500, expected: 304` on the old worker.
- Against `wrangler pages dev` in the container, a conditional request for `/assets/site.css` and for `/dtg` now returns 304 with the worker's headers.

title: feat(vtc): OpenID4VP wallet sessions — swiyu wallets present evidence for a join (#1988)
body:
A swiyu wallet speaks OpenID4VP 1.0 over HTTPS and signs no Trust Task, so the
applicant's own agent opens the exchange for it. The VTC now serves the whole
round trip against an installed verifier identity (#2039).

- `vtc/join-requests/wallet-session/start/0.1`: the proof signer opens a
  session for a criterion named by its `requirementsDigest` (and optionally
  their own join request). The VTC signs an ES256 request object as a JAR in
  swiyu's profile (`profile_version`, `aud` https://self-issued.me/v2,
  `client_id` `decentralized_identifier:<did>`), asking for the criterion's
  published DCQL query unchanged, with a fresh nonce, `state` and P-256
  response key, and returns the `swiyu-verify://` wallet URI. Every declared
  code is served: criterionNotFound, noWalletPresentation,
  verifierNotConfigured, requestNotFound (unknown and somebody else's alike),
  requestClosed, tooManySessions.
- `GET /v1/oid4vp/request/{session}` answers the request object once;
  `POST /v1/oid4vp/response/{session}` accepts one `direct_post.jwt` answer.
  It is checked in order: decrypts (A256GCM) under the session key and echoes
  `state`; each presentation's issuer signature, validity and KB-JWT over the
  session nonce with the prefixed `client_id` as audience (VTI-CRD-020…022),
  one holder; status valid, never assumed (VTI-CRD-014); every issuer admitted
  by the criterion's `credentialIssuers`; the query satisfied
  (`DcqlQuery::evaluate_presentation`). Both are a declared foreign-protocol
  exception (VTI-OPS-095): REST_EXCEPTIONS and GOVERNED_UNAUTH rows, behind the
  unauthenticated governor; the response reads its body against
  `[oid4vp] max_response_bytes`.
- `vtc/join-requests/wallet-session/status/0.1`: only the signer who opened a
  session reads it; the evidence names the wallet's holder key beside the
  applicant and each credential's query id, format, issuer and vct, never a
  claim value; a refusal names its reason.
- New keyspace `oid4vp_sessions`, encrypted at rest, excluded from backup. A
  minute sweeper closes unanswered sessions at `expiresAt` (dropping the
  response key) and drops records an hour after closing, or when held evidence
  lapses. State changes run under one lock, so one response wins.
- `[oid4vp]` config: session TTL, open sessions per applicant, evidence hold,
  response cap, default identity, wallet URI scheme.
- Workspace floors: affinidi-openid4vp 0.1.4 (`direct-post-jwt`),
  affinidi-oid4vc-core 0.1.10 (`jwe`), affinidi-sd-jwt 0.1.7;
  trust-tasks-rs 0.28.1 for the wallet-session specs.

Evidence is recorded on the session. Deciding a join on it — on the named
request, or on the applicant's next submission — follows. P3 of
docs/05-design-notes/oid4vp-wallet-verifier.md; docs/03-vtc/oid4vp-verifier.md
covers operating it.

title: vti-rooms: openmls stack locks libcrux-kem 0.0.9 (RUSTSEC-2026-0330/0331) into downstream Cargo.lock
body:
## Summary

`vti-rooms` pulls in the openmls stack, which puts `libcrux-kem` 0.0.9 into the `Cargo.lock` of every consumer of `vta-service`. Two advisories apply to that version:

- **RUSTSEC-2026-0330**: hybrid encapsulation from seed panics on a short seed.
- **RUSTSEC-2026-0331**: decoding short hybrid keys panics.

Both are fixed in `libcrux-kem` 0.0.10.

## Chain (as of vta-service 0.57.0)

```
vti-rooms -> openmls 0.9 -> openmls_rust_crypto 0.6.0 -> hpke-rs 0.7.0
  -> hpke-rs-libcrux 0.7.0 (optional, `libcrux` feature) -> libcrux-kem =0.0.9
```

`hpke-rs-libcrux` 0.7.0 pins `libcrux-kem = 0.0.9` exactly. `hpke-rs-libcrux` 0.8.0 pins `=0.0.10`. But the newest `openmls_rust_crypto`, 0.6.0, still requires `hpke-rs ^0.7`, so the lockfile can't move from inside VTI.

## Impact: low; the vulnerable code is never compiled

Nothing in the workspace enables `hpke-rs`'s `libcrux` feature. `cargo tree -i hpke-rs-libcrux --workspace --all-features --target all -e all` prints nothing, so `hpke-rs-libcrux` and `libcrux-kem` are in `Cargo.lock` only. That's why VTI's CI, which uses `cargo deny` and only checks what gets built, passes (`advisories ok`).

`cargo audit` scans `Cargo.lock` and doesn't consider features, so it flags both. Downstream, OpenVTC runs `cargo audit` in CI and reaches this chain through its `vta-service` dev-dependency (MockVta). It has to carry `ignore = ["RUSTSEC-2026-0330", "RUSTSEC-2026-0331"]` in `.cargo/audit.toml` (added in openvtc #483, still needed at #484).

## Fix

When openmls publishes an `openmls_rust_crypto` on `hpke-rs` 0.8, which pulls `libcrux-kem` 0.0.10, bump `openmls` / `openmls_rust_crypto` in `vti-rooms` and release. OpenVTC then drops its two audit ignores on its next `vta-service` bump.

Nothing needs to change in VTI before then. This issue is here to track the upstream release, so the dependency doesn't stay behind once it lands.

title: feat: SignInPortal in did-host-http* templates and a VTC DID self-check for wallet sign-in
body:
Wallet sign-in with a trigger link (`auth/oob`, sign-in trigger-link contract C4 and C9) needs the service's DID document to list `TrustTaskHTTPS` (a base; clients POST `<base>/trust-tasks`) and `SignInPortal` (whose origin is the sign-in page's). On **webvh.storm.ws**, a DID hosting server minted from the `did-host-http` template, there was no `SignInPortal`, so wallets refused its codes with "This code can't be used" and nothing server-side noticed.

## A. vta-sdk: `SignInPortal` in the `did-host-http*` templates

- `did-host-http`, `did-host-http-tsp` and `did-host-http-didcomm` now publish exactly what DID hosting publishes for itself: `{ "id": "<did>#sign-in-portal", "type": "SignInPortal", "serviceEndpoint": "<origin of URL>/login" }`, placed after `TrustTaskHTTPS` (`{URL}/api`).
- The template format can't compute an origin. So the templates declare `SERVICE_SIGN_IN_PORTAL` (a null default, as a bare service member), and the renderer derives it from `URL`, the same way it derives `WS_URL`. It does this only for `https`. A plain-http dev URL gets no entry. A caller can supply its own entry, or `null` to omit it.
- Nodes that serve no `/login` page keep their templates unchanged: `did-host-didcomm`, `did-host-tsp` (witness/watcher) and `didcomm-mediator`. `vtc-host` already publishes its own `SignInPortal` (`/members/`).
- New additive public items: `sign_in_portal_endpoint`, `sign_in_portal_service`, `SIGN_IN_PORTAL_SERVICE_TYPE`, `SIGN_IN_PORTAL_SERVICE_VAR`. There are no breaking changes.
- Backwards compatible: existing DIDs are untouched, and only new mints get the entry. `docs/02-vta/did-templates.md` explains how to add it to an existing DID with `pnm did-mgmt dids edit --did <did>`.

## B. vtc-service: DID self-check for wallet sign-in

- `vtc-service/src/did_self_check.rs` resolves the VTC's own DID about 5 s after boot (spawned in `server::run`, off the startup path). After that it re-checks lazily, caching a result for 5 minutes, or 30 s if the result was unknown. It checks the **published** document using the portal's own checks (`member_portal::oob::check_trust_task_https` / `check_sign_in_portal`), so it can't disagree with the flow. `VTCRest` is not checked, because neither the portal nor the wallet flow reads it.
- When something is missing, it logs one warning. The warning names what is missing, gives the exact JSON entries, and gives the fix: `pnm did-mgmt dids edit --did <vtc-did>`, then `cnm did-log install` for a VTC serving its own log. It logs again only when the result changes.
- It never blocks startup. If resolution fails, the result is `unknown`, not `missing`.
- `GET /v1/member/sign-in/config` gains `didDocument`: `{"status":"ok"}`, `{"status":"unknown"}` or `{"status":"missing","missing":["SignInPortal"]}`. It carries only facts from the public document.
- The shared `WalletSignIn` component (member portal and console login) now fetches that config when it mounts. When the status is `missing`, it replaces "Show sign-in code" with a short note naming the missing services, and the other sign-in options stay as they are.

## Tests

- vta-sdk: `cargo nextest run -p vta-sdk -p vta-cli-common`, 1147 passed. New template tests cover: every `did-host-http*` template gets the exact entry; the origin is used, not the path; the `{DID}` sentinel is kept; plain http gets no entry; a caller can override or omit it; templates without a login page don't declare it.
- vta-service template, did_webvh and provision tests: 310 passed.
- vtc-service: full nextest run. The only failures were the 10 admin-UI-embedding tests, run with `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1`; they pass with the UI built. New tests: `did_self_check` unit tests, plus the sign-in config route returning `didDocument: {status: unknown}` with no resolver.
- admin-ui: `npm test` (85 files, 988 tests) and `npm run lint` pass. New tests cover: the note names the missing services; there is no code button when services are missing; the code is still offered when the status is unknown, ok or absent.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` are clean.

title: fix(tsp): a relationship accept beaten by a concurrent one was answered, not lost
body:
When two TSP relationship invites from the same peer arrive at once, the VTA and the VTC both warned that "the peer sees no answer". The peer had in fact been answered.

## What happens

1. Both invites are recorded first, and each leaves the pair `InviteReceived`.
2. The first `accept_relationship` moves the pair to `Bidirectional` and sends the accept.
3. The second is refused by the state machine: `invalid transition: SendAccept in state Bidirectional`.
4. That refusal was logged as `could not send a TSP relationship accept; … the peer sees no answer`.

An accept for the same pair went to the same peer a moment earlier, and receiving any accept completes its side. So the invite was answered, and the warning said the opposite.

Seen at gt-vta on 2026-10-11 15:49:44 UTC, against the browser wallet. The wallet's mediator socket was being replaced in a loop (fixed in OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#319), so its invites arrived in pairs. A client retrying, or two sessions of one client re-forming the same relationship, can produce the same pair.

## Fix

`accept_refusal_is_benign` (`vti_common::relationship_store`) decides it the same way the SDK's `invite_refusal_is_benign` does: it re-reads the relationship state after the refusal rather than matching the error text (R3.7).

- **`Bidirectional`:** the invite was answered. Logged at debug.
- **Anything else:** the accept failed for its own reasons (no route, no key, the mediator refused it). The existing warning and the not-collecting accounting are unchanged.

The VTA (`messaging/service.rs`) and the VTC (`messaging.rs`) carried the same handler and now share the one helper.

## Tests

- 3 unit tests pin the decision: `Bidirectional` is benign; `InviteReceived`, `None` and `Pending` are not. The race itself sits between two awaits and cannot be staged, which is how the SDK pins its counterpart too.
- `cargo clippy -p vti-common -p vta-service -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. `tsp` is on by default in both services, so this compiled the new code.
- `cargo test -p vta-service --lib messaging`: 129 passed. `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib messaging`: 41 passed.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2)
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): read-only re-read of the store.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): no retries added.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): the listener is untouched; a failed re-read falls through to the existing warning.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6)
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): none.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*)
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): the point of the change; a real accept failure still warns.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): no mutation added.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none.

title: feat(vtc): serve room files — blobs, records 0.2 and rooms/info, off until enabled
body:
A community VTC now hosts room files the way `room-host` does (`data-rooms-files.md` P5), so `pnm rooms file put/get` (#2037) works against a VTC.

### One implementation for both hosts
`vti_rooms::blob_tasks` (new) maps each file task onto `BlobHost`, with the spec's declared codes and generated response types. It takes `(room, presenter, authorization)` and returns a checked response body or a `Refusal`. Each host keeps only its transport, parsing, chain verification and reply rendering.
- `room-host`'s handlers become thin wrappers; all 47 of its tests pass unchanged.
- The VTC renders the same results through its own helpers, so the two can't answer one task two ways.

### The VTC
- **Tasks**, registered by generated payload type: `rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,chunk,commit,abort}`, `rooms/blobs/{get,chunk}`, `rooms/info` and `rooms/records/{put,get,list}` 0.2. All are added to the shared `ROOMS_DISPATCHED_URIS` and pinned against the registry.
- **Record path, as room-host's:**
  - put (0.1 too, since a rewrite naming no blobs releases them) holds `prepare_record` across the write and then `apply`s it;
  - retract releases the record's blobs;
  - get/list 0.2 read under a snapshot.
- **State:** `AppState::room_files: Arc<BlobHost>` plus a GC sweeper.
- **Keyspaces:** `room_blobs` is **backed up** (the index and usage); `room_blob_transfers` is **excluded** (transfers in flight).
- **`[rooms.files]`**: mirrors room-host's flags. **Uploads are off by default.** Until storage configs exist, files go to a local directory under limits that apply to every room alike, and an operator should choose that. When off, `begin` answers `filesDisabled`; stored files and records without files are still served.

### Size gate
Upload chunks (360 KiB) and `begin` (320 KiB) declare sizes above the 64 KiB default. The VTC only granted that to issuers with an ACL entry, and room members have none.
- A large `upload/chunk` is admitted only from a claimed issuer that **holds an open, unexpired upload** here.
- A large `begin` is admitted only when **uploads are on and it names a room hosted here**.
- Both are charged to the same per-address `LargeDocumentBudget`, and a claim that fails verification doubles that address's next cost, like any other.

### `rooms/info` proof
Its spec said RECOMMENDED though the chain must bind to the signer. trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#750 (merged) makes it REQUIRED. Until that reaches `trust-tasks-rs`, an interim `DISPATCHED_WITHOUT_PROOF` entry records why the rooms arm refuses an unsigned caller anyway. The census fails once the spec agrees, forcing the entry out with that bump.

### Tests
- VTC, through the dispatcher with signed documents:
  - a file uploaded, named by put 0.2, read back by get/list 0.2, downloaded and counted;
  - `blobNotFound` for an uncommitted blob;
  - retraction and a 0.1 rewrite each releasing the file;
  - another party's chunks to someone's upload answered `notFound`.
- The size gate's room standing.
- `[rooms.files]`: off by default, a misspelt key refused.
- Census and backup tests updated.
- Full CI-equivalent run: fmt and clippy clean, 5,629/5,629 workspace tests, 2,979/2,979 vtc tests, doctests.

### Next
Storage configs, with credentials from the community VTA's external accounts (P4/P4b, `vtc/storage/*`), replace the single local directory.

title: fix(tsp): apply unclaimed relationship control frames instead of refusing them forever
body:
TSP relationship control messages (invite, accept, cancel) that no request is waiting for were refused and never acknowledged, so the mediator redelivered them on every reconnect, forever.

## What was happening

`ensureRelationship` claims the accept it is waiting for. Every other control frame reaches the inbox:
- an accept that arrives after the 5 s handshake stopped waiting
- a cancellation
- the VTA's own invite

The inbox read every TSP frame as a Trust-Task document. A control frame has an empty body, so `openTspEnvelope` threw `payload is not JSON: Unexpected end of JSON input`. The throw went back to the transport, so no ack was sent, and the mediator kept the frame.

Seen against glenn-vta on 2026-10-11: the offscreen console showed the same four 580-byte frames (`-EB4YTSP-AAC…`) refused after every reconnect.

## Fix

- **`unpackInboundTsp`** returns the verified control message (`InboundTspControl`, discriminated by `isInboundTspControl`) instead of parsing it as a document. Its sender is proven by the same `unpack` as a document's.
- **`applyInboundControl`** (`vta/tsp-relationship.ts`) applies it using the specification's own rules from `@openvtc/vti-tsp-js`:
  - **accept:** `resolveAccept` adopts only an accept that answers our outstanding invite, which moves the relationship to `bidirectional`. Anything else is ignored.
  - **cancel:** `resolveCancel` removes a relationship we hold. A cancellation naming one we do not hold is ignored rather than answered, so nobody can probe which relationships we hold.
  - **invite:** ignored. The wallet initiates its relationships, and a Rev 3 peer may send application messages over an invite it is still waiting on (§3.6).
- **The offscreen inbox** applies the message to the shared `tspRelationships` store and returns, so the frame is acknowledged. A control frame carries no consent request, so there is nothing for persist-before-ack to hold (R1.6).

## Not done

§7.3's answering cancellation when both halves were held. It is logged as owed, not sent: the peer has already forgotten the relationship, and the next request re-invites. Sending it needs a routed TSP send from the inbox path, which is more than this change should take on.

## Tests

- **`core/tests/tsp.inbound.mjs`:**
  - an accept and a cancel come back as control, from the proven sender
  - a control frame from a sender that cannot be verified is still refused (`e.p.msg.unauthorized`)
  - a document still comes back as a document
- **`core/tests/tsp.inbound-control.mjs` (new):**
  - a late accept completes the relationship
  - an accept to an invite we did not send, or with nothing outstanding, changes nothing
  - a cancellation of a bidirectional relationship removes it and reports the answer owed
  - a cancellation naming an unknown relationship is ignored
  - an invite is ignored

`npm run lint`, `npm test` and `npm run build` pass locally.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2)
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): the relationship store is in-memory and only reflects what the peer sent.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4): removes an unbounded redelivery.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): a control frame is acked after it is applied, and carries no consent request to persist. Document frames are unchanged.
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): none on the wire. `unpackInboundTsp`'s return type widened; its one caller is updated.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): an unverifiable control frame is still refused.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*): each outcome is logged, including the owed answer.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): an in-memory record lost to a teardown means the next request re-invites.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none.

title: feat(sign-in): explain document-level refusals in the window's Details
body:
## Problem

When a service's DID document had no `SignInPortal` service, the sign-in window said only "Code not accepted / This code can't be used." The operator testing it had no way to find out why.

## Change

The headline and message for every refusal stay as they were. Reasons that come from parsing the link (bad-from, bad-type, bad-id and so on) also stay vague, as VTI-LNK-021 requires: a reader never says which link field failed.

Refusals caused by the **contact's DID document or the page** are not link fields. These now carry a `detail` (`SignInRefusalDetail` in `bridge-protocol.ts`) from the flow to the window. The window shows it in a collapsed **Details** block with a Code row, a Meaning row and a DID row. The DID uses the existing `CopyableDid` pattern (selectable text plus a Copy button).

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `no-portal-service` | This service's DID document doesn't list a sign-in portal (a SignInPortal service). Ask its operator to add one. |
| `no-portal-service` (listed, unusable) | …lists a sign-in portal (a SignInPortal service), but its endpoint isn't usable: it must be an https URL on a public host name, with no port or credentials. Ask its operator to fix it. |
| `no-common-transport` (no `TrustTaskHTTPS`) | …doesn't list a Trust-Task endpoint (a TrustTaskHTTPS service), so the wallet has nowhere to send the sign-in. Ask its operator to add one. (There is also a listed-but-unusable variant.) |
| `wrong-origin` | This page (https://a) isn't the service's sign-in page (https://b). Start sign-in from https://b, or ask the operator to point the SignInPortal service at this page. |
| `did-document-unverified` | The wallet couldn't fetch or verify this service's DID document. Check that the DID below is published and its log verifies, and that its host is a public name on the default https port. (Shows the DID.) |
| `from-not-allowed` | Sign-in doesn't accept a did:key DID as the service's identifier. The service needs a DID that can list a sign-in portal, such as did:webvh. |
| `unsupported-vid` (resolver missing) | This wallet can't resolve did:x DIDs yet, so it can't check this service. An update may add it. |
| `domain-not-linked` | The website (https://portal) doesn't publish a DID Configuration that links it to the community's DID, so nothing was sent to it. Its operator needs to serve /.well-known/did-configuration.json with a Domain Linkage credential for the DID below. |

What changed in each layer:

- **Core:** `selectSignInServices` now says which service type is missing (`SignInPortal` or `TrustTaskHTTPS`) and whether one was listed but has an unusable endpoint. A missing `TrustTaskHTTPS` already had its own reason (`no-common-transport`, outcome `unreachable`), so it did not need to be split from `no-portal-service`. `parseTriggerLink`'s `from-not-allowed` now carries the contact's DID method.
- **Plumbing:** the offscreen and background layers already pass `SignInStepResult` through unchanged. The background console line still uses `failureLogFields`, so no DID or origin is ever logged (VTI-LNK-073). A test checks this.
- **README:** a new "When a sign-in code isn't accepted" section under the sign-in section. It lists what each Details line means, how an operator fixes it, the three services a DID hosting service needs, and `pnm did-mgmt dids edit --did <did>`.

This also closes the backlog item to make the wrong-origin error name both origins.

## Tests

- Core: `selectSignInServices` reports missing and unusable for both service types. `from-not-allowed` names the method and nothing else of the contact.

title: perf(tsp): unpack each inbound frame once, however many requests are waiting
body:
Each inbound TSP frame is now unpacked once and the result shared by every request waiting on the socket. Previously each waiting request unpacked the frame itself.

## Why

Every inbound frame on a mediator socket is offered to each outstanding TSP request in turn (`onTspFrame` in `didcomm/index.ts`). Each request's `claims` did a full `unpack` (HPKE decrypt and signature verify) before it could read the thread id and decline. With N requests waiting, a burst of N replies cost about N²/2 unpacks, serially, on the offscreen thread that also sends.

A console switched between agents a few times a second leaves six requests waiting per page load for up to 30 s. Nothing cancels them when the page goes away.

Against gt-vta on 2026-10-11:
- The VTA log shows the same six-request bundle about 14 times in six seconds, so ~80 requests were outstanding at once.
- One unpack takes about 1.4 ms in Node, and longer in a browser. That's seconds of blocked thread per burst.
- The wallet's own sends came out bunched behind that work: four page loads reached the agent within 15 ms.

## Change

- **`openReplyOnce`** (`vta/tsp-channel.ts`) caches the opened reply, either `{ sender, doc }` or a decline reason.
  - It is keyed on the frame object, in a `WeakMap`, so the entry goes away with the frame. The transport hands every waiter the same `bytes` object.
  - It is also keyed on the public halves of the keys involved, so a waiter holding different keys never reads another's result.
- **`TspChannel.send`'s `claims`** uses it, then does only the sender and thread-id checks.

Behaviour is otherwise unchanged, including the decline reasons reported on a timeout (`lastDecline`, `framesSeen`).

## Not claimed

This does not explain the six replies in the same incident that reached the wallet more than 30 s late. A backlog of a few seconds would have delayed most replies, not exactly six. That is still open, pending the `fpdev-mediator` log for the window.

## Tests

`core/tests/tsp.unpack-once.mjs` (new):
- 50 waiters offered one frame share one unpack
- a waiter with different keys gets its own result, and a decline
- a different frame object is unpacked afresh even with identical bytes

The existing `tsp.channel`, `tsp.relationship` and `tsp.timeout-diagnosis` tests pass unchanged. `npm run lint` and `npm test` pass locally.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2)
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1): an in-memory cache keyed on the frame object.
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4)
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5)
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): the frame dispatch and ack order are unchanged.
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*): none.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*): a frame that does not verify under a waiter's keys is still declined for that waiter.
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*)
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): nothing persisted.
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers: none.

title: Interop: receive and verify ES256 SD-JWT VCs from did:web / did:webvh issuers with IETF Token Status List (swiyu, EUDI)
body:
**Summary.** An SD-JWT VC issued on the Swiss swiyu stack or on the EU EUDI profile cannot be received or verified by OpenVTC today. Those profiles use ES256 / P-256, `did:web` or `did:webvh` issuers, holder binding with a P-256 `cnf.jwk`, and the IETF Token Status List (`statuslist+jwt`). This makes the stack unable to take in the credentials that Swiss and EU wallets carry, for example to admit a member on the strength of one.

**What we ran** (at `49f5f1b`, 7 Oct 2026). We used a real IterationSeal credential minted by our own seal library with a throwaway key. It verifies with its embedded public key in our verifier, and the vector is below. We fed it to `vta_vault::receive::receive_sd_jwt_vc` in a local test:

| Case | Result |
| :- | :- |
| As issued: `iss` = `did:web:validant.ai`, `alg` = ES256 | `` Validation("issuer `iss` (did:web:validant.ai) is not a resolvable did:key: Decoding error: Expected 'did:key:' prefix") `` |
| `iss` swapped to an Ed25519 `did:key` (header still ES256) | `Validation("issuer signature verification failed: Verification error: unexpected alg (want EdDSA)")` |

**Where the limits are**:
- `vta-vault/src/receive.rs`, lines 93 to 97: `alg` must be `EdDSA`. Around line 183, the issuer must be a `did:key`.
- `vtc-service/src/credentials/vm_resolver.rs`, lines 65 to 90: Ed25519 verification methods only.
- `vtc-service/src/credentials/exchange/jwt.rs`, lines 36 to 45: the `cnf.jwk` must be OKP Ed25519.
- `vta-vault/src/status.rs`: the resolver expects a W3C `BitstringStatusListCredential`, so a `statuslist+jwt` fails.

**Request**:
1. ES256 / P-256 issuer signatures in vault receive and in the VTC verifier, with issuer keys resolved from `did:web` and `did:webvh`.
2. P-256 `cnf.jwk` holder binding.
3. A Token Status List resolver next to the Bitstring one. It must verify the token's signature before decoding, and check that `sub` equals the referenced URI.
4. Later: plain HTTPS OID4VCI/VP bindings, so a swiyu or EUDI wallet can talk to a VTC directly.

We are happy to provide more test vectors and to test a branch. Context: we issue AI fairness assessments as SD-JWT VCs on the swiyu stack, and we are proposing an `assessed` statement predicate for the DTG graph. We would like both expressions of one assessment to be usable inside OpenVTC communities.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.30.0
body:
### Specifications

- **rooms**: Rooms/info and rooms/usage require a proof, like every other rooms/* task ([#750](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/750))

Both said a proof was RECOMMENDED, on the reasoning that the room-issued chain
  is "bound to whoever the host authenticated". A room operation carries no
  session, so the only party a host can authenticate is the proof's signer. The
  chain's leaf must be that party. Without a proof there is nobody to bind it
  to, and the presentation becomes a bearer token. Every other rooms/* task
  already requires a proof for this reason. A host implementing the chain rule
  refuses an unsigned info or usage request anyway, so the RECOMMENDED was
  already unworkable.

  Breaking for a producer that sent these unsigned. Both specs are drafts.

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in

- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags

- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*

- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.
