title: feat(vtc): shared design tokens and the operator console shell
body:
Phase 1 of the operator console redesign: one token file and one typeface for the community's three surfaces, and a console frame that says which community it runs. The four design decisions from the reviewed proposal are applied:

1. **Indigo is the brand base**, from the home page and member portal (500 `#5b5bd6` light, 400 `#7c7ce8` dark, violet accent `#8b5cf6`). A community accent overrides it when one is set.
2. **IBM Plex Sans and Plex Mono are used everywhere**, self-hosted. Fraunces is dropped.
3. **Ceremonies is shown as "Policies".** Only the label changes; the route stays `/ceremonies`.
4. **Personal settings move into an account menu** in the top bar. The signing-key expiry warning moves into the attention strip.

## What changed

### Shared tokens (`admin-ui/src/styles/tokens.css`)
- **Contents:** the indigo brand ramp and roles, the semantic colours with soft variants, a grey ramp, type, weights, spacing (4px grid), control and row heights (36 / 28 / 40px), radius, motion and elevation, all with light and dark values.
- **Verdict colours:** `--vd-allow`, `--vd-deny`, `--vd-refer` and `--vd-more` keep their current values, because Policies (ceremonies) depends on them.
- **Density:** the console stays at a 14px base.
- **Community accent:** the accent is the Branding card's colour (`vtc/community/branding/show`). When it is set, the console puts it on `<html>` as `--community-accent` together with `data-community-accent`, and that overrides `--brand`.
  - The foreground is white or near-black, whichever passes 4.5:1.
  - In dark mode the accent is lifted towards white so it stays legible.
  - Anything that is not `#rrggbb` is ignored.
- **Who uses it:** the console imports this file, and so does the member portal. The home page carries a byte-identical copy (`website-default/tokens.css`). A new test in `website/default_site.rs` fails if the copy drifts.

### Type
- **Console and portal:** both load Plex from the `@fontsource` packages the console already bundled. Weight 700 is added; it comes from the same package.
- **Home page:** loads Plex from woff2 copies under `website-default/fonts/` (Latin and Latin Extended, OFL 1.1, with the licence alongside).
- **CSP:** the page links `fonts.css` and `tokens.css` before `site.css`. Everything is served from the same origin, so it works under `default-src 'self'` and makes no third-party request.
- **Fraunces:** nothing else used it, so the `@fontsource-variable/fraunces` dependency is removed. `--font-display` is kept as an alias of the sans face, so any rule that reads it still resolves.

### Shell (`App.tsx`)
- **Top bar:**
  - The community's mark and name, read from `/v1/community/public-profile`. The logo is shown only when it is same-origin, because the console's CSP is `img-src 'self' data:`; otherwise the gradient mark is used.
  - An "Operator console" pill.
  - The live indicator.
  - The account menu.
- **Account menu:**
  - The operator's name (from the name book), or their shortened DID if no name is known, with the full DID.
  - **My passkeys** and **Signing keys**. Their routes are unchanged. Signing keys shows a "Renew soon" flag when the key is close to expiry.
  - The existing theme switcher.
  - **Sign out.**
  - It closes on Escape (focus returns to the trigger), on an outside click and on navigation.
- **Grouped sidebar:**

  | Group | Entries |
  |---|---|
  | Overview | Dashboard, Actions, Audit trail |
  | Membership | Join requests, Members, Invitations, Vetting, Relationships |
  | Governance | Policies, Roles, Access control, Sessions |
  | Community | Profile, Recognition, Data rooms, Repos |
  | More | Any plugin that names no group |

  - A group is hidden when the viewer can see none of its entries.
  - The badges are unchanged.
  - The collapsed rail is unchanged and keeps the same localStorage key (`vtc-admin-nav-collapsed`). Collapsed group headings become thin rules.
  - The mobile slide-over is unchanged and now opens from the top bar.
- **Attention strip:** one strip replaces the stacked banners.
  - Items are ordered most severe first, with a count ("3 things need attention") and a "Show N more" control.
  - **Critical items** (an unacknowledged operator write, a cooling-off against you, break-glass and its "cannot be checked from this browser" variant) and **single-administrator mode** (VTI-APV-022) are always visible and cannot be dismissed.
  - The **signing-key expiry** item, with its Renew link, now lives here.
  - **Actions waiting** stays dismissible for the session.
  - Every message keeps its wording, its links and its ARIA role. The old banner components are kept and still exported.

### Plugin API (additive)
- `registerPlugin` accepts an optional `group?: "overview" | "membership" | "governance" | "community" | "account"`. The built-ins set it.
- A plugin without a group, or with an unknown value, is listed under **More**.
- `window.VtcPluginApi` and custom-element plugins are unchanged.
- `docs/03-vtc/admin-ui-plugins.md` documents the field.

## Backwards compatibility
- **Routes:** every route under `/admin` is unchanged, including `/step-up`, `/install`, `/enrol-*`, `/ceremonies`, `/profile`, `/my-passkeys` and `/console-keys`.
- **localStorage:** `vtc-admin-theme` and `vtc-admin-nav-collapsed` keep their keys and values.
- **Plugin API:** the change is additive only. `nav-groups.test.ts` registers a pre-groups custom-element plugin through `window.VtcPluginApi` and checks that it registers, routes and is listed under More.
- **Directory mode:** operators running `admin_ui.mode = "directory"` keep their exported copy until they re-export. `vtc admin-ui export` writes the whole baked bundle, so the new fonts and CSS are included. The release notes should say to re-export to pick up the redesign.
- **Custom home pages:** a custom `website.root_dir` is served exactly as before. The new `tokens.css`, `fonts.css` and `fonts/` live only in the embedded default site, so a custom page that doesn't link them is unaffected.
- **Test ids:** existing test ids and `data-*` attributes are kept. The strip adds `data-testid="attention-strip"`.
- **Parallel sign-in work:** `feat/admin-wallet-sign-in` is changing the login page and adds a scoped `signin/signin.css` that carries its own copy of the old site tokens. This PR doesn't touch `Login.tsx` or `WalletSignIn.tsx`. Once both land, dropping that scoped token block lets the sign-in pages pick up `tokens.css` directly.

## Testing
- **Admin UI:** `npm run lint` (wire check + `tsc`) passes, and `vitest` passes (77 files).
  - New tests: `AppShell.test.tsx` (top bar, grouped sidebar, account menu, collapse, key-expiry item), `AttentionStrip.test.tsx`, `nav-groups.test.ts` and `community-identity.test.ts`.
  - The existing banner tests (`AppActionsBadge`, `BreakGlass`) pass unchanged.
- **Rust:**
  - `cargo build -p vtc-service` builds the UI through `build.rs`.
  - `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 2929 passed.
  - `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -D warnings` are clean.
- **Visual checks:** I ran the console in headless Chrome against a mocked backend and checked:
  - every main screen in light and dark at 1400px and 400px;
  - the account menu, the collapsed rail, the mobile slide-over, an expanded strip and a community accent;
  - the home page and the member portal.

  Screenshots are in a comment below.

title: build: trust-tasks-rs 0.27.8, with auth/oob on its generated types
body:
Moves the workspace to `trust-tasks-rs` 0.27.8. That release carries:
- `auth/oob/*`, out-of-band wallet sign-in (trust-tasks-tf #738)
- room files: `rooms/blobs/*`, `rooms/records/{put,get,list}/0.2`, `rooms/info`, `rooms/usage`, `rooms/keys/file-key`, `vtc/rooms/*` and `vtc/storage/*` (#739)
- the VTA's `external/*` accounts (#740)

**Prerequisite** for the external-accounts and room-files PRs, which build on these generated types.

## auth/oob now uses the generated types

The release generates the eight `auth/oob` tasks, so the census refused the hand-written copies. They are replaced:

- **VTA, `vta-service` `oob_sign_in`:** `IdentifyPayload`, `GrantPayload` and `GrantDecision` are the generated types.
- **VTC, `member_portal::oob::types`:**
  - re-exports the generated payloads and responses, and type URIs come from `TYPE_URI`;
  - responses are built through the generated types, so each is checked against its specification;
  - step 1 is stored as the JSON it was signed as, and step 2 is built from it.
- **Proof and recipient** requirements are now the specifications' own policy, enforced by the spine. `oob_tasks::precheck` keeps only the Ed25519 key rule.
- **Tests:** the tripwires are gone (the dispatcher test's exception and the manifest's unpublished allowance), and the census baselines lose the deleted types.

## Wire differences now enforced (the specification is normative)

| Member | Now accepted | No longer accepted |
|---|---|---|
| grant `notAfter` | integer epoch seconds | an RFC 3339 string |
| grant `contextDigest` | `z` or `u` multibase | hex (`f`) |
| `origin` | `https://` only | `http://localhost`, on either side |
| `requestId` | 22–43 base64url characters | the VTA's old 16–128 range |

The wallet extension produces the identify and grant documents, so it should be checked against these. The member portal's JS produces only request, redeem and cancel, and is unaffected.

## Checks (local)
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 5513 passed
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`: 2927 passed
- `cargo test --workspace --doc`: ok
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean

copies go:

- vta-service's oob_sign_in IdentifyPayload, GrantPayload and GrantDecision
  are the generated types, re-exported under the same names.
- vtc-service's member_portal::oob::types re-exports the generated payloads
  and responses; type URIs come from each payload's TYPE_URI. Responses are
  built from JSON through the generated types, so each is checked against
  its specification as it is made. The stored step 1 is kept as the JSON it
  was signed as, and step 2 is built from it.
- oob_tasks::precheck keeps only the Ed25519 key rule; proof and recipient
  are now the specifications' own policy, enforced by the spine. The
  dispatcher test's auth/oob exception and the manifest's eight-URI
  unpublished allowance are gone.
- The census baselines lose the entries for the deleted types.

Wire differences, where the specification is normative and now enforced:

- grant notAfter is integer epoch seconds only; the VTA no longer accepts an
  RFC 3339 string.
- grant contextDigest is DigestMultibase, z or u; a hex (f) digest is refused.
- origin is https only; http://localhost is no longer accepted by either side.
- requestId is 22 to 43 base64url characters (was 16 to 128 at the VTA).
- a request whose purpose or mode is not served still answers
  purposeUnsupported / modeUnsupported, read before the generated enums.

title: feat!: verify ES256 / ES256K SD-JWT-VCs from did:web and did:webvh issuers (#1988)
body:
Part of #1988 (phase 1 — see [the plan on the issue](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/issues/1988#issuecomment-6100644681)).

SD-JWT-VCs issued on the swiyu stack and the EUDI profiles — ES256 / P-256, `did:web` / `did:webvh` issuers, P-256 `cnf.jwk` holder binding — could not be received into the vault or verified by the VTC. This adds EdDSA, ES256 and ES256K alongside each other on both paths.

## Changes

- **`vta_sdk::jws` (new).** Compact-JWS verification over a resolved key: Ed25519 (`EdDSA`), P-256 (`ES256`), secp256k1 (`ES256K`). The `alg` header must be the one the resolved key signs with, checked before the signature. `crit` is refused, and a `cnf.jwk` carrying `d` is refused. `sd_jwt_issuer_method` binds the issuer `kid` to `iss`:
  - a `did:key` issuer verifies with its own key, whatever fragment the `kid` carries (issuers here write `#key-0`);
  - any other DID must name the signing method with a DID-URL `kid` under `iss`, which is the SD-JWT VC rule for DID issuers. Nothing is guessed (VTI-CRD-002).
- **`TrustTaskVmResolver`** reads `publicKeyJwk` methods (Ed25519, X25519, P-256, secp256k1) and secp256k1 Multikeys. PQC keys stay Multikey-only.
- **`vta-vault`**
  - `receive_sd_jwt_vc` / `stored_claims` take the issuer resolver, and resolve for `assertionMethod`.
  - `receive(.., IssuerKey::None, ..)` resolves locally (`did:key` / `did:peer`). The VTA's issued-credential path and persona derivation pass the DID cache.
  - A credential carrying an IETF `status.status_list` reference is stored `Unknown`, not `Valid`. No `statuslist+jwt` resolver exists yet, so its status cannot be read (VTI-CRD-012).
- **`vtc-service`**: the SD-JWT-VC presentation verifier takes ES256 / ES256K issuers and P-256 / secp256k1 holders. The proven holder is that key's `did:key` (`did:key:zDn…`, `did:key:zQ3s…`).

## Breaking

`vta_vault::receive_sd_jwt_vc` takes a `&dyn PurposeVmResolver` after `compact`, and `vta_vault::stored_claims` is now async and takes one. `TrustTaskVmResolver::did_key_only()` gives the previous behaviour.

## Not in this PR (tracked on #1988)

- IETF Token Status List resolver. The decoder goes into the TDK's `affinidi-status-list` first.
- Plain-HTTPS OID4VCI / OID4VP bindings.
- Sign-in and Trust Task signing for P-256 / secp256k1 member identities (`ecdsa-jcs-2019`). `holder_signature.rs` remains Ed25519-only and refuses other curves.
- ES256 key-binding JWTs when presenting from a VTA vault.

## The reporter's vector

Its ES256 signature verifies against the published JWK (`jws::tests::the_issue_1988_es256_vector_verifies`). It names no `kid` on a `did:web` issuer, so receive refuses it for that reason, not as a bad signature (`the_issue_1988_vector_is_refused_for_its_missing_kid`). A conforming vector has been requested on the issue.

## Testing

- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client` — 5446 passed.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --doc` — passed.
- `cargo nextest run -p vtc-service -p vtc-client` — 2868 passed. The 6 failures were the admin-SPA embedding tests under `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1`; all pass with the UI built.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.

New tests cover:
- `did:web` + `JsonWebKey2020` P-256 resolution through to ES256 verification;
- P-256 / secp256k1 `did:key` round-trips;
- an ES256K round trip;
- `alg`/key mismatch for issuer and holder;
- a `kid` outside `iss`;
- a `did:web` issuer without a `kid`;
- `IssuerKey::None` refusing `did:web`;
- Token Status List references stored as `Unknown`.

the vault only a `did:key` issuer, the shared resolver only a

  issuer's own key whatever the fragment, any other DID must name its
  method with a DID-URL `kid` (VTI-CRD-002: the issuer is resolved, not
  guessed).
- `TrustTaskVmResolver` reads a `publicKeyJwk` method (Ed25519, X25519,

- `vta-vault`: `receive_sd_jwt_vc` and `stored_claims` take the issuer
  resolver, so a `did:web` / `did:webvh` issuer resolves for

  stored `Unknown`, not `Valid`: no `statuslist+jwt` resolver exists yet, so
  its status cannot be read (VTI-CRD-012).

  issuers and P-256 / secp256k1 `cnf.jwk` holders.

`&dyn PurposeVmResolver` after `compact`, and `vta_vault::stored_claims` is

| `trust_tasks` | pub.dev | `0.5.8` → `0.5.9` | patch |

What merging does, per registry (all in `publish.yml`, each keyed on "this
version is not published yet"):

- **crates.io** — `release-plz-release` tags `<crate>-v<version>`, publishes in
  dependency order and creates a GitHub Release per crate. Bump levels come from
  `cargo-semver-checks`.
- **npm** — `publish-npm` publishes with OIDC provenance and tags
  `<prefix>-v<version>`.
- **Go** — `publish-go` builds, vets and tests, then pushes the tag, which *is*
  the publication. **Irreversible**: proxy.golang.org never forgets a tag.
- **pub.dev** — `tag-dart` verifies against the *published* core and pushes the
  tag; `publish-dart.yml` publishes from it.

The npm, Go and Dart bumps are only as accurate as the commit subjects — nothing
checks their APIs the way `cargo-semver-checks` checks the crates. Look for a
missing `!` before merging.

This branch is regenerated from `main` on every push, so do not commit to it —
edits are force-pushed away. See RELEASING.md.

title: feat(external): VTA external accounts — management, credential issuance and Sui signing
body:
Adds the `external/*` family: a VTA holds identities at clouds and third-party services, and lets bound integrations use them only through short-lived, downscoped credentials or protocol-defined signatures. Design: [`vta-external-accounts.md`](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/blob/main/docs/05-design-notes/vta-external-accounts.md) in verifiable-trust-infrastructure.

- **Management:** `external/accounts/{list,get,create,update,secret/set,bindings/grant,bindings/revoke,setup,probe,keys/rotate,suspend,resume,archive,restore,delete}/0.1`. Changing an account is recommended to need consent, with approvers signing with their own DIDs. Suspend and revoke never need it.
- **Use:** `external/credentials/issue/0.1`. The custodian does the exchange and downscopes the result itself, and the response is a `sealed_transfer` bundle.
- **Signing:** `external/sign/0.1`, for `sui-signer` only. It signs only allow-listed Move calls, under gas and amount caps, and the custodian builds the digest.
- **Models:**
  - `aws-roles-anywhere`
  - `gcp-wif-pinned`
  - `azure-cert`
  - `oauth2-private-key-jwt`
  - `s3-static-presign`
  - `sui-signer`
  - `static-secret`, which is never released

  None of them needs the custodian to be reachable inbound. Plain OIDC discovery federation is excluded, and `_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md` says why.

Unverified, and written as options:
- whether GCP accepts ES256 (`signingAlgorithm`);
- whether a Roles Anywhere session accepts a per-request session policy (the `chainedRoleArn` fallback);
- the exact Sui secp256r1 digest; conformance requires Sui's reference verifier to accept the signature.

Bindings are regenerated for all four languages. `validate`, `check-bindings` and the Rust conformance tests pass.

* feat(external): VTA external accounts — management, credential issuance and Sui signing

Adds the external/* family: external/accounts/{list,get,create,update,secret/set,bindings/grant,bindings/revoke,setup,probe,keys/rotate,suspend,resume,archive,restore,delete}/0.1, external/credentials/issue/0.1 and external/sign/0.1, with shared shapes and family conventions in external/_shared/0.1.

A key custodian holds an identity at a third party and never releases its key or secret. Integrations bound to the account get short-lived credentials the custodian obtained and downscoped itself, sealed to the caller, or signatures over Sui transactions the custodian decoded and checked against an allow-list. Every model pins the custodian's verification material at the provider, so none needs the custodian to be reachable from the internet; plain OIDC discovery federation is excluded for that reason.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(external): generated bindings for the external/* family

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(external): implementation feedback — wrapping-key sealing, sealed payload shapes, no existence oracle in issue, complete probes

From the VTA implementation of E0 and E3:
- secret/set seals to a single-use wrapping key from keys/import-wrapping-key, never to the custodian's DID; its plaintext is a new ExternalSecretPayload naming context and account, so a bundle cannot be replayed into another account.
- credentials/issue: the plaintext is a new ExternalCredentialPayload (awsSession | bearerToken | presignedRequest); sealed to the caller's key-agreement key (did:key X25519 derivation, else the first X25519 keyAgreement method; noKeyAgreement otherwise); PinnedOnly producer assertion anchored by the REQUIRED response proof; the bound-consumer check runs first, so unbound callers and unknown accounts get the same notFound.
- probe reports complete; providerSetupRequired clears only on an ok and complete probe; storage settings gain probePrefix; egressHosts includes probe destinations.
- New external:archived family code and create:modelUnsupported; an unknown context is the standard notFound.
- AccountSettings branches are inline with a model const, so codegen emits a tagged enum and a bad setting can be answered as invalidSettings.
- SecretFingerprint (hmacsha256:, keyed at the custodian) replaces DigestMultibase for secret fingerprints.
- Registers externalAccountsManage and externalAuthUse device capabilities.
- Consent is RECOMMENDED operator policy; enforcement may be off.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* chore(bindings): regenerate Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart for the external/* feedback

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec: declare the not-found codes the framework does not define

The framework's standard vocabulary has no notFound. rooms/keys/file-key gains rooms/keys/file-key:noGroup; external/accounts/create answers external:notFound for an unknown context.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(external): secret/set names its wrapping key; schema-invalid settings are malformedRequest

secret/set gains a required wrappingKeyId so the custodian can discard the one key it tried whether or not the bundle opens. create states that external:invalidSettings covers settings the schema accepts but the custodian cannot use.

title: feat: wallet sign-in with a trigger link (auth/oob/*)
body:
## Summary

Adds wallet sign-in with a trigger link (`auth/oob/*`) to `@openvtc/rp-sdk`.

- **New entry point `@openvtc/rp-sdk/browser`.** `createSignIn` is the starter. It generates a non-extractable WebCrypto Ed25519 key `K_b`, sends `auth/oob/request`, builds the trigger link, renders it as a clickable SVG QR code at level M, hides it on `visibilitychange`, and long-polls `auth/oob/redeem`.
- **Server helpers on the main entry.**
  - `verifyOobClaim`, `verifyOobIdentify` and `verifyOobGrant`.
  - `verifyDidKeyDocument` and `computeContextDigest`.
  - `OobSignInService`, a reference state machine over a pluggable `OobRequestStore`.
  - `OOB_ERRORS`.
  - `trustTaskEndpoint(doc)` and `signInPortalOrigin(doc)`.
- **Wire format** follows the agreed contract (C1, C2, C7, C9) and is checked against the `auth/oob/*` schemas.
- **`trustTaskEndpoint(doc)`** treats a `TrustTaskHTTPS` `serviceEndpoint` as a base URL, following HTTPS binding 0.2 §6. It removes one trailing slash and appends `/trust-tasks`. For example, `https://members.example.org/v1` becomes `https://members.example.org/v1/trust-tasks`, and `…/api` becomes `…/api/trust-tasks`. The constant is exported as `TRUST_TASK_HTTPS_PATH`.
- **SIOPv2 deprecation.** The SIOPv2 helpers are marked `@deprecated` in JSDoc only (contract C7). They still work.

## Backwards compatibility

Nothing is removed or renamed, and no existing behaviour changes.

- **Existing exports.** I built `origin/main` and this branch, then diffed the generated `.d.ts` files. For `confirm`, `did-resolver`, `jcs`, `session` and `verify-id-token`, the only differences are doc comments, meaning the new `@deprecated` tags. `index.d.ts` only gains new exports, and no new name collides with an existing one. `verifyIdToken`, `IdTokenVerificationError`, `constantTimeEqual`, `KeyResolver`, `buildSessionCookie`, `establishSession` and the confirm helpers keep their names, signatures and types. The internal `eddsa-jcs-2022` refactor of `confirm.ts` is covered by the existing confirm tests.
- **The `package.json` `exports` map.** `main` already had an `exports` map with only `"."`, so deep imports were already blocked before this change. `"."` is unchanged (`types` + `import`), and `./browser` is added next to it. Neither version has `typesVersions`. The package is ESM-only before and after, so there is no CJS output to check. `npm pack --dry-run` includes `dist/browser*`.
- **The main entry's dependencies (fixed in this PR).** Originally, the main entry re-exported `defaultQrEncoder` from a module that imported `qrcode-generator`, so `import "@openvtc/rp-sdk"` on a server loaded the QR library.
  - The QR core (`oob/qr.ts`) now has no third-party import and no DOM use.
  - `defaultQrEncoder` and `createTriggerLinkElement` live in `browser/qr.ts`, which only `@openvtc/rp-sdk/browser` imports.
  - From the main entry, `renderQrSvg` and `renderTriggerLinkHtml` take a required `encoder`. From the browser entry, the encoder defaults to `qrcode-generator`.
  - Three checks guard this:
    - `npm run lint` now also compiles `src/index.ts` without the DOM lib (`tsconfig.server-check.json`). I confirmed this check fails on the browser entry.
    - A test walks the main entry's import graph.
    - A Node module-resolution trace shows `dist/index.js` loads no `qrcode-generator`, and only `dist/browser.js` does.
- **Minimum Node version and TypeScript target.** `engines.node` is still `>=18.0.0`, and the `tsconfig.json` target is still ES2022. Both are unchanged.
- **Version and changelog.** I followed the repo convention: entries go under `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`, and the version is bumped in a separate release commit (PR #6 did not bump either). The additions are minor-level, so the next release should be **0.3.0**.

## Testing

- `npm run lint` passes. It covers `tsc --noEmit`, the new no-DOM check of the main entry, and `prettier --check`.
- `npm test` (vitest) passes: 12 files, 133 tests. These include schema validation of emitted documents against the `auth/oob/*` schemas, the starter state machine, the service, QR rendering and entry-point isolation.
- `npm run build` passes. I also checked runtime imports of `@openvtc/rp-sdk` and `@openvtc/rp-sdk/browser` under Node.
- The repo has no `.github/workflows`, so these local checks are the CI-equivalent run.

## Third-party dependency: approval needed

This PR adds **`qrcode-generator` 2.0.4**, pinned. It is MIT-licensed and has no dependencies of its own. Its approval under the organization's third-party dependency policy is **still pending**, so please do not publish a release until it is approved.

The library sits behind the `QrEncoder` interface (`(text) => { size, isDark(row, col) }`) and is loaded only by `@openvtc/rp-sdk/browser`. If it is not approved, you can swap it by passing `encoder` or by replacing `defaultQrEncoder` in one file (`src/browser/qr.ts`). The rest of the API stays the same.

## Related

- https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec/pull/58

title: feat: register each install as a device before wallet sign-in
body:
## Why

Wallet sign-in with a trigger link (#303, #304) failed against a real VTA for any plugin that had never registered as a device. The VTA signs `auth/oob/identify` only for a caller whose own ACL entry has an active device binding. The plugin registered only inside `enrolUvPasskey`, at the first grant, which comes after `identify`. So `identify` was refused with `oobNotEnrolledDevice`, after the claim had already gone to the community.

**Requires OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1997 to be deployed for plugin sign-in to complete.** That PR has the `auth/oob` signing gate, UV-key enrolment and the `oobDeviceDisabled` code this PR reads.

## Multi-device model

The model needs no change. Every install is already a device of its own:

- onboarding mints a holder DID per install;
- the VTA keys the ACL entry, and the device binding on it, by that DID.

So two browser profiles, or a browser and a phone, are separate devices. Each has its own transport key, UV key, `consumerKind` and display name, and each can be listed, disabled or wiped without the others noticing. This PR makes the plugin act like one.

## What changed

- **Enrol early, once per holder per agent.**
  - New `ensureDeviceRegistered` (core) sends `device/heartbeat/0.2` first and falls back to `device/register/0.2` on `not_found`. A `conflict` from a racing register counts as success.
  - The offscreen document registers as `companion`/`browser`, under a name like "Chrome on macOS" (`device-name.ts`, from Client Hints or else the UA string):
    - after onboarding;
    - when an agent's inbox comes up, which is how existing installs enrol on upgrade, with no new onboarding;
    - at sign-in prepare, before anything is sent to the community.
  - A per-agent IndexedDB record (`pnm/device-enrolment/<vtaDid>` → the holder DID) keeps this to one heartbeat per holder.
- **Recover once, then explain.**
  - `identify` and `grant` register once and retry once on `oobNotEnrolledDevice`.
  - `oobDeviceDisabled`, `oobNoUvKey`, `oobUvInvalid` and a repeated `oobNotEnrolledDevice` show a clear message, and the claim is cancelled so the portal stops waiting.
  - Codes are read from `details.details.code` (R3.7).
- **The UV passkey stays lazy, and is tracked per agent and per holder.**
  - The window keeps the whole public enrolment.
  - The `uv-challenge` result names the credential the VTA holds for this holder.
  - When it is absent or different, the window enrols this browser's passkey (creating one only if it has none) and asks for a fresh grant. So a second agent or a re-onboarded holder works without a second passkey.
  - An `oobNoUvKey` refusal clears the record.
- `taskRefusalReason` moves into `vta/errors.ts`, so `device` and `vault` share it without a sideways import.

## Backwards compatibility

- **No new manifest permissions, no new dependencies.** The page-facing API (`window.vtaWallet.*`) is unchanged.
- **Stored state is additive.**
  - New keys: `pnm/device-enrolment/*`, `pnm/uv-passkey/enrolment` and `pnm/uv-passkey/enrolled/*`.
  - A missing key means "enrol now", never an error.
  - The legacy `pnm/uv-passkey/credentialId` is still written. A wallet that holds only that key reads as having no passkey, and creates one at its next approval: one extra passkey prompt, once.
- **Existing installs are not re-onboarded.** They register at the next unlock or sign-in.
- **Against a VTA without #1997** there is no `auth/oob` gate, so registering is harmless. `device/register/0.2` and `heartbeat/0.2` are sent exactly as the VTA already accepts them.
- `SignInVta.ensureDevice` and `enrolledUvCredential` are optional. The `uv-challenge` result gains an optional `uvCredentialId`.

## Tests

- `core/tests/device.ensure-registered.mjs`:
  - heartbeat-only when registered;
  - register on `not_found`;
  - `conflict` counts as success;
  - other refusals are rethrown;
  - `vaultOobRefusal` reads the code, never the message.
- `extension/tests/sign-in-flows.test.mts`:
  - the device enrols before identities are read and before anything reaches the community;
  - `uvCredentialId` is passed through;
  - VTA refusals map to messages and the claim is cancelled.
- `extension/tests/sign-in-view.render.test.mts`:
  - a first approval creates, enrols, then asserts over a fresh grant;
  - a passkey the VTA holds is asserted directly;
  - a stored passkey is enrolled at an agent that lacks it, without a second passkey.
- `extension/tests/device-name.test.mts`.
- Every `run` step of `ci.yml` passes locally on Node 26.

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2). There are no new network clients; everything goes through the existing `VtaSession`.
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3)
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect (R2.1). The enrolment and passkey records are written only after the VTA accepted. If the process dies first, the next heartbeat finds the binding.
- [x] Every retry is bounded; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4). There is one retry, only after a definitive `oobNotEnrolledDevice`, which the VTA returns before it signs or records anything.
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5). Enrolment from `startInbound` is fire-and-forget and cannot fail the inbox.
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): untouched.
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*): no wire change. The `uv-challenge` bridge result gains an optional member.
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*): an absent record means "register again", never "assume registered".
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*): "registered" is logged only on a successful `device/register`.
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1)
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged: none.

title: feat: register each install as a device before wallet sign-in (#305)
body:
feat: register each install as a device before wallet sign-in (#305)

The VTA signs an auth/oob/identify only for a caller whose own ACL entry
carries an active device binding. The plugin registered itself only from
enrolUvPasskey, at the first grant, so a plugin that had never registered
failed identify with oobNotEnrolledDevice, after the claim had already gone
to the community.

Every install is already a device of its own: onboarding mints a holder DID
per install, and the VTA keys the ACL entry and its binding by that DID. So
the fix is to enrol early, once per holder per agent:

- ensureDeviceRegistered (core) sends a heartbeat first and registers on
  not_found. A conflict from a racing register counts as success.
- The offscreen document enrols as companion/browser with a real name
  ("Chrome on macOS") after onboarding, when an agent's inbox comes up (the
  upgrade path for existing installs, with no new onboarding) and at sign-in
  prepare, before anything is sent to the community.
- identify and grant register once and retry once on oobNotEnrolledDevice.
  oobDeviceDisabled, oobNoUvKey and oobUvInvalid get clear messages, and the
  claim is cancelled.
- The UV passkey stays lazy, but is now tracked per agent and per holder:
  the window keeps the whole public enrolment, the uv-challenge result names
  the credential the VTA holds, and a second agent or a re-onboarded holder
  is enrolled with the same passkey. A legacy credential-id-only record
  reads as no passkey and creates one at the next approval.

No new permissions or dependencies, and the page-facing API is unchanged.
The stored state is additive: a missing record means "enrol", never an
error. Needs OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1997 deployed for
sign-in to complete.

title: fix(vtc): the member portal names a wallet sign-in as one
body:
The member portal's membership card showed **Signed in with: Your VTA (SIOPv2)** for every session that wasn't a passkey, including a wallet sign-in with a trigger link (#1998).

A wallet sign-in session carries `amr: ["did", "oob", "uv"]` (`vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/oob_tasks.rs`). The card now reads:

| `amr` contains | Label |
|---|---|
| `passkey` | Passkey |
| `oob` | Your wallet |
| otherwise (`did`, the SIOPv2 path) | Your VTA (SIOPv2) |

**Backwards compatibility:** the change is display-only. Passkey and SIOPv2 sessions show the same labels as before, and nothing on the server changed.

**Testing:** `npm run lint` (wire check and `tsc`) passes, and vitest passes, including a new test for each of the three `amr` cases.

title: feat(rooms): files in data rooms, and VTC room storage administration (#739)
body:
feat(rooms): files in data rooms, and VTC room storage administration (#739)

* spec(rooms): shared file and blob types

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(rooms): files in data rooms — blob upload and download, file keys, limits and usage, and VTC storage configs

Adds rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,chunk,commit,abort} and rooms/blobs/{get,chunk}, rooms/records/put 0.2 (blobs on a record), rooms/info, rooms/usage and rooms/keys/file-key; and, VTC-only under the new vtc.rooms.admin capability, vtc/rooms/{get,limits/set,usage}, vtc/rooms/storage/{assign,migrate}, vtc/storage/configs/{list,get,create,update,retire,probe} and vtc/storage/credentials/set. Shared types in rooms/_shared/0.1/blobs.schema.json and vtc/_shared/0.1/room-storage.schema.json.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* chore(bindings): regenerate Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart for the rooms file specs

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec(rooms): implementation feedback — permissionDenied, alreadyCommitted, slot lifetimes, records get/list 0.2 and FileManifest byte rules

From implementing #739 in room-host, vti-rooms and the VTA:
- rooms/blobs/upload/chunk drops the unreachable alreadyStored (digests are committed at begin, so different bytes fail as chunkMismatch).
- LimitScope drops object; LimitExceeded names the scope the refusing limit was set at.
- upload/begin: alreadyCommitted for a blob the room already holds; retryable tooManyUploads; slots live at least 15 minutes after the last chunk and extend to at least 24 hours; maxDocumentBytes.request 327680 with the arithmetic.
- records/put 0.2: re-referencing an orphaned blob is charged again and may be refused with limitExceeded; Security states that CommittedRecord does not yet commit to blobs.
- New rooms/records/get/0.2 and rooms/records/list/0.2 echo blobs (RecordMetadataV2), with a section on mirrors of rooms that hold files; the leaf preimage removes blobs.
- New specs in this PR state authorization refusals as the standard permissionDenied instead of declaring notAuthorized; file-key answers notFound for a room the oracle holds no group for, and unknownEpoch gains heldEpoch.
- FileManifest pins byte encodings (decoded fileId, UTF-8 roomId, u64be), u64 epochs, the Padmé formula with zero padding checked, chunk-count consistency, and that a streaming reader treats nothing as received until the digest verifies. BlobRef is defined over JSON, not any binding's type.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* chore(bindings): regenerate Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart for the rooms implementation feedback

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* spec: declare the not-found codes the framework does not define

The framework's standard vocabulary has no notFound. rooms/keys/file-key gains rooms/keys/file-key:noGroup; external/accounts/create answers external:notFound for an unknown context.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(rooms): files in data rooms, and VTC room storage administration
body:
Adds Trust Tasks for files in data rooms, and for the hosting community's administration of room storage. Design: [`data-rooms-files.md`](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/blob/main/docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md) in verifiable-trust-infrastructure.

## Room tasks (authorized by the room's own chain, never host ACLs)
- `rooms/blobs/upload/{begin,chunk,commit,abort}/0.1`: chunked, resumable upload of a file's ciphertext. The manifest is committed before any byte moves, and every limit is checked and reserved at `begin`.
- `rooms/blobs/{get,chunk}/0.1`: download of a file's ciphertext.
- `rooms/records/put/0.2`: a record can name a committed blob (`blobs`). This is a new version rather than an edit, because a 0.1 host would accept a record pointing at a blob it never checked.
- `rooms/info/0.1`: the room's limits and usage, plus the caller's own.
- `rooms/usage/0.1`: per-member usage, for the room's owner. Not offered on `private` rooms.
- `rooms/keys/file-key/0.1`: the member's VTA releases the key for one file. The spec explains why this releases a key when `rooms/keys/open` deliberately does not.

## VTC-only tasks, under a new `vtc.rooms.admin` capability
- `vtc/rooms/{get,limits/set,usage}/0.1`
- `vtc/rooms/storage/{assign,migrate}/0.1`
- `vtc/storage/configs/{list,get,create,update,retire,probe}/0.1`
- `vtc/storage/credentials/set/0.1`: the discouraged fallback for a sealed credential. It is write-only; only a fingerprint comes back.

Storage changes park in the administrator action list.

## Shared types
- `rooms/_shared/0.1/blobs.schema.json`:
  - `BlobRef`, `BlobManifest`, `TransferId`;
  - the limits and usage types: `ScopeLimits`, `RoomLimits`, `Usage`, `LimitExceeded`;
  - `FileManifest`, the sealed body's `file` member, which carries the KDF and STREAM construction.
- `vtc/_shared/0.1/room-storage.schema.json`

Bindings for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart are regenerated. `npm run validate` and `npm run check-bindings` pass, and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features` passes.

title: ci(release): keep the Release PR's versions valid automatically
body:
The Release PR (#1996) fails the release-line check: release-plz proposes `vti-common` 0.40.1, `vta-service` 0.56.1, `pnm-cli` 0.36.1 and `cnm-cli` 0.30.1, all inside Eucalyptus's lines. release-plz rewrites the PR on every merge to main, so a hand fix doesn't last.

After each rewrite, the Release PR job now runs `scripts/fix-release-bump-sizes.py` on the PR branch and pushes the result (no-op when the guards already pass), using `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` so CI re-runs. `branch rules` already permits version edits on `release-plz-*` heads; the `chore(release)` commit is skipped by the changelog.

actionlint clean; pins check passes. First real run: the next merge to main after this one.

## Backport
none
author: stormer78

title: ci(release): keep the Release PR's versions valid automatically (#2008)
body:
ci(release): keep the Release PR's versions valid automatically (#2008)

release-plz proposes patch bumps without knowing which compatibility lines
the release branches own (releases/*.toml), so the Release PR kept failing
the release-line guard, and since release-plz rewrites it on every merge to
main, a fix applied by hand was overwritten by the next merge.

The Release PR job now runs scripts/fix-release-bump-sizes.py on the PR's
branch after each rewrite and pushes the result (a no-op when every guard
already passes). Pushed with RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN so CI re-runs on the PR.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(vtc): member portal, with wallet sign-in by trigger link
body:
## Summary

This merges the VTC member portal branch into `main`. The branch has 10 commits: 63 files, about 10.5k lines added. It merges cleanly with current `main`.

- **Member portal at `/members`:** a home page that explains the community, and sign-in cards with DIDs shown abbreviated.
- **Sign in as another identity:** members can sign in as any identity their wallet holds.
- **Wallet sign-in with a trigger link (`auth/oob/*`, #1998):** the default sign-in. SIOPv2, issued by the member's VTA, stays as the legacy path behind "Using an older wallet?".
- **Custom consoles:** the admin console and the member portal can both be served from a directory, so an owner can customise them.
- **Fixes:**
  - setup shuts down the VTA client it lists hosting servers with;
  - the member session request's tokens are redacted in `Debug`.

## Breaking change

`af9beb14` retires `admin_ui.mode = "external"` and `admin_ui.external_origin`. A config that sets either one now fails to load, with an error that names the `mode = "directory"` replacement.

The mode was documented but never implemented. `/admin/*` always served the built-in console, whatever the setting said, so a deployment using it was already getting the stock console. Operators with either key must remove it before upgrading.

## Backwards compatibility otherwise

- **SIOPv2 member sign-in:** routes, cookies and session format are unchanged.
- **`POST /v1/trust-tasks`:** the new handlers match only `auth/oob/*`. Every existing task type is dispatched as before.
- **New config setting:** `sign_in_link_host` is optional and defaults to `link.trustoverip.org`.
- **Audit and sessions:** `AuditEvent` is `#[non_exhaustive]` and tagged, so old records still read. Sessions are unchanged; sign-in requests live under their own key prefix.

## Depends on

- **The VTA side (#1997, merged to `main`):** the `auth/oob/grant` attestation slug, the UV-consent gate, multi-device enrolment, and the `vtc-host` template that publishes `TrustTaskHTTPS` (`<url>/v1`) and `SignInPortal` (`<url>/members/`).
  - Wallet sign-in only completes against a member VTA that has #1997.
  - Existing VTC DIDs need a VTA-side `dids edit`, then `cnm did-log install`, to publish those two services.

## Related

- Spec: trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#58
- Trust Tasks: trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#738
- rp-sdk: OpenVTC/rp-sdk-js#7
- Browser plugin: OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin#303 (merged), #305
- DID hosting: affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#253

title: feat(vtc): member portal, with wallet sign-in by trigger link (#2007)
body:
feat(vtc): member portal, with wallet sign-in by trigger link (#2007)

* feat(vtc): a member portal at /members, and a home page that explains the community

Members could not sign in anywhere: VTC sign-in admitted administrators only,
and every session it minted read as an admin session. This adds a member
portal as a separate application from the console, with the separation
enforced by the daemon rather than by what each page shows.

Member portal (`crate::member_portal`, `routes::member_portal`):
- Only an active member signs in — a live ACL entry that is not expired,
  suspended or an `application` entry, plus a member record that has not been
  removed — checked at challenge (VTI-SES-006/007 via the shared handler), at
  authentication, on every refresh and on every request (VTI-SES-020..022).
- Sign-in by the browser wallet (SIOPv2 at `<origin>/v1/member/wallet`) or a
  portal passkey only. A passkey is added from the portal after a wallet
  sign-in; adding or removing one requires a wallet-proven session (`amr`
  contains `did`). Audited as the new `MemberPasskeyChanged` event.
- Tokens carry audience `VTC-member` (`JwtKeys::for_audience`), so console
  extractors refuse them and the portal refuses console tokens.
- Sessions and passkeys live in their own keyspaces (`member_sessions`,
  `member_passkeys`, excluded from backup), so a member who is also an
  administrator cannot redeem a portal refresh token or passkey at the console.
- Cookies `vtc_member_session` / `vtc_member_refresh` are `Path=/v1/member`;
  `vtc_member_csrf` is the portal's own double-submit value, and the CSRF gate
  picks the cookie pair by path.
- The portal is its own Vite bundle (`vite.members.config.ts`), baked by
  build.rs into `$OUT_DIR/member-ui-dist` and served at `/members/`; it loads
  no console code. In subdomain mode it is served on the API host.
- The sign-in page carries manual install steps for the VTA Wallet extension
  (OpenVTC/vta-browser-plugin).

Default landing page: rebuilt around a visitor who does not know what a VTC
is — "Get started" at openvtc.net, member sign-in, capability cards (git
across GitHub, Forgejo/Codeberg and Gitea, verifiable data rooms, access
management, credentials, recognition), a quieter operator-console link, and
the existing status panel. Fixes hidden status rows rendering empty.

The step-up passkey route test now compares an unrouted response with the
website fallback byte for byte; its old "no 'credentials' in the body" check
tripped on the new landing page copy.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc): redact the member session request's tokens in Debug

`MemberSessionRequest` derived `Debug` over the access and refresh tokens it
carries, so any log line or panic formatting it would print them. Written by
hand now, reporting both as <redacted>, as the console's `SiopAuthPayload`
does. Caught by vta-sdk's secret_debug_census.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc): setup shuts down the VTA client it lists hosting servers with

`vtc setup`'s DID-hosting picker connects the ephemeral setup key to the VTA
to list did-hosting servers, and returned — on success and on every `?` out
of a prompt — without calling `shutdown()`. Over DIDComm that drops a live,
auto-reconnecting session: it keeps the mediator's one socket for the setup
key and fights the provision round-trip's own session, and in a debug build
vta-sdk's leak guard panics ("DIDComm session ... dropped without
shutdown()") right after the WebVH path prompt.

The prompts now run in their own function against the client, which is shut
down however they end.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc): members sign in with SIOPv2 issued by their VTA, not the wallet's own key

The member portal's sign-in called the wallet extension's self-issued
`login()`, which presents the extension's holder did:key unless a persona
is bound to the site. A community admits members by their VTA identity, so
that button presented a DID no community admitted.

The portal now runs the VTA-proxied SIOPv2 flow: `walletProfile` resolves
(or binds, on first use) the VTA persona this community knows the member
as, the portal takes a challenge for that DID from
/v1/member/wallet/auth/challenge, `proxyLogin` has the VTA mint the
id_token with the challenge as nonce (the key never leaves the VTA), and
the token is posted to /v1/member/wallet/auth/. The self-issued button is
gone. A refusal names the DID the VTA presented. The daemon is unchanged:
it already accepted these shapes.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): serve the admin console from a directory so an owner can customise it

`admin_ui.mode = "directory"` with `admin_ui.dir` serves the console from
disk instead of the binary, with the same shell/asset/history-mode contract,
read per request so an edit shows on the next load. Every path goes through
the website's path-safety chain (no hidden files, no escaping the directory,
no executables).

`vtc admin-ui export <dir>` writes the baked console out as the starting
point; it refuses a non-empty directory.

The daemon refuses to start when the directory has no index.html or when it
or index.html is world-writable — the console signs with administrators'
console keys, so whoever writes it acts as them — and never falls back to
the baked console. `dir` beside another mode, directory mode without `dir`,
and an unknown mode are refused at config load. `admin_ui` remains host
configuration only.

The boot `AdminUiServed` audit row and `/admin/build-info.json` now describe
the console actually served.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): serve the member portal from a directory too

`admin_ui.members_dir` serves `/members/*` from disk instead of the binary,
independently of the console's `mode`, with the same serving rules, the same
path-safety chain and the same fail-closed start-up check (index.html present,
neither it nor the directory world-writable) — the portal's scripts run in
members' sessions. `vtc admin-ui export --members <dir>` writes the baked
portal out as the starting point.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc)!: retire admin_ui mode "external"

`admin_ui.mode = "external"` and `external_origin` were documented — skip the
embedded console and allowlist an operator origin in CORS — but never
implemented: `/admin/*` served the baked console whatever the mode said. Nor
could the stock console run from another origin: it reads the `csrf` cookie
from `document.cookie`, calls the API by relative URL, and passkeys are
verified against the VTC's own origin.

Customisation now goes through `mode = "directory"`, so the mode is retired
rather than built. A config declaring `mode = "external"` or
`external_origin` fails to load with an error naming the directory-mode
replacement, instead of silently serving the stock console.

BREAKING CHANGE: `admin_ui.mode = "external"` and `admin_ui.external_origin`
are refused at config load. Remove them, or move to `mode = "directory"`.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc): wider sign-in cards, and DIDs shown abbreviated rather than overflowing

The console's sign-in card was 26rem, so the community DID wrapped
character by character with its copy button stranded beneath, and the
pick-an-identity list put label and full DID on one line inside a
fixed-height button, spilling both outside the card.

The card is now 36rem. The community DID uses `DidText` (SCID and
subdomains abbreviated, the whole DID on hover, copy and QR beside it).
Each identity choice is a block: its vault label, then its abbreviated
DID, full DID on hover; the DID is always shown because two personas can
share a label. The member portal's sign-in column widens to 42rem to
match.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): members can sign in as another identity their wallet holds

"Sign in with your VTA" uses the persona the wallet has bound to this
community. A member whose wallet holds more than one VTA identity here,
and whose bound one is not the identity the community admitted, had no
way to choose another.

"Sign in as a different identity…" lists the wallet's did-self-issued
entries pinned to this community's DID (`vaultList`, behind an explicit
click because the wallet asks consent to disclose them), shows each by
label and abbreviated DID (full on hover), and runs the same VTA-issued
SIOPv2 round-trip as the chosen one. A refused sign-in shows the
presented DID abbreviated and offers the choice from the alert. Entries
without a principal DID are not offered.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): wallet sign-in with a trigger link (auth/oob/*); SIOPv2 kept as legacy (#1998)

* feat(vtc): wallet sign-in by trigger link — auth/oob/* handlers

The VTC side of the key-grant sign-in (design-docs/vtc-qr-login-design.md
§7, §12; sign-in-trigger-link contract C1–C9). The browser's
non-extractable K_b opens a request; a wallet claims it with a throwaway
K_a, proves membership and the on-screen number, and returns a grant signed
by the member's DID naming K_b; only K_b redeems it into a member session.

- auth/oob/{request,claim,prove,respond,redeem,cancel}/0.1 on the signed
  document spine (trust_tasks::oob_tasks), with local wire types marked
  "TODO: replace with generated trust-tasks types", matched to the
  dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf feat/auth-oob schemas and error codes.
- Request store in member_sessions (oob_req:*), swept with the sessions;
  two clocks (120 s claim, 120 s decision); every state change a
  compare-and-set under one process lock; a failed step from the lock holder
  declines the request.
- Check order of §7: ACL string check before any DID resolution (T15);
  identify verified for authentication and grant for assertionMethod (C5);
  claim parentThreadId must equal payload.requestId (VTI-LNK-054); carried
  documents checked for recipient, freshness and id replay.
- Step 1 and step 2 responses signed with the VTC's assertionMethod key
  (LocalSigner::sign_attested_response); contextDigest is the z-multibase
  sha2-256 multihash of the JCS signed step 2 response.
- redeem is a 25 s long poll (one per request, per-address cap) that creates
  the member session with K_b as session key, amr [did, oob, uv], ending at
  the grant's notAfter, through member_portal::cookies. Cancelled answers
  declined with details.state "cancelled" (C9).
- request accepted only from the portal's Origin over HTTPS (T19); five
  open requests per address; auth/oob responses are no-store; every step
  audited as MemberWalletSignIn (vti-common, non_exhaustive enum).
- GeoIP: no dependency or database here, so location is "unknown" behind
  oob::locate; browser/OS from the User-Agent family only.
- GET /v1/member/sign-in/config (DID, link host, flow); link host is
  admin_ui.sign_in_link_host, default link.trustoverip.org, refused on the
  portal's own domain (VTI-LNK-084).
- vtc status reports the SignInPortal (C4, VTI-LNK-102) and TrustTaskHTTPS
  (C9) services; the member page is served no-store, no-referrer, with
  frame-ancestors 'none'.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(vtc): member portal "Sign in with your wallet"; SIOPv2 deprecated

The portal's starter for the trigger-link sign-in (base design §13,
contract C1, C2, C7, C9):

- "Sign in with your wallet" is the first option: a WebCrypto Ed25519 K_b
  (non-extractable), a signed auth/oob/request, and the trigger link
  https://<link host>/t#_from=…&_id=…&_exp=…&_type=/vti/flow/sign-in/0.1
  drawn as a level-M QR (qrcode, already a dependency; 4-module quiet zone,
  dark on light) wrapped in <a href> to the same text (VTI-LNK-086).
- Long-polls redeem; shows the number once claimed, "Continue as …?" before
  the session is used ("Not me" signs out), and declined, cancelled and
  expired states. The code hides on visibilitychange without cancelling and
  the poll continues (C9). K_b is forgotten at sign-out.
- The VTA extension's SIOPv2 sign-in is kept behind "Using an older
  wallet?" and marked deprecated in code and docs (C7).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc): TrustTaskHTTPS is the Trust-Task base, as binding 0.2 §6 makes it

`vtc status` asked for a TrustTaskHTTPS service at the full
/v1/trust-tasks URL. Every consumer in the workspace, the browser plugin
and DID hosting treat a TrustTaskHTTPS serviceEndpoint as the base and POST
to <base>/trust-tasks, and the vtc-host template now publishes {URL}/v1. A
document at the full URL would send them to /v1/trust-tasks/trust-tasks.

The check now wants <public_url>/v1 and refuses the full request URL. The
handler stays at POST /v1/trust-tasks, and the portal posts there directly.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-sdk): name the VTC sign-in did:keys in the secret Debug census

The member portal's auth/oob types hold K_a and K_b as Ed25519 did:keys,
the public halves the VTC checks proofs against. The census flags them by
name; list them in NOT_SECRET as the VTA-side types already are.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(auth/oob): add the auth/oob out-of-band sign-in Trust Task family
body:
## What it adds

The `auth/oob/*` family: out-of-band sign-in, where a starter (the browser) asks a service to open a request and an approver (the wallet) decides it on another device. There are eight Trust Tasks, each at `https://trusttasks.org/spec/auth/oob/<task>/0.1`:

`request`, `claim`, `prove`, `identify`, `respond`, `grant`, `redeem`, `cancel`

- **Shared schema** `specs/auth/oob/_shared/0.1/oob.schema.json`. It defines `RequestId`, `OobKey`, `MatchNumber`, `Mode`, `Purpose`, `Origin`, `Service`, `Requester` and `SameNetwork` once for the whole family. Beside it:
  - `CONVENTIONS.md` holds the family rules: purposes, disclosure at each step, windows and errors.
  - `TRIGGER-LINK.md` describes the QR code / trigger link the starter shows.
- **Wire details** follow the cross-repo sign-in contract (C9):
  - `claimDeadline`, `decisionDeadline` and `notAfter` are integer epoch seconds.
  - `contextDigest` is a `DigestMultibase`.
  - `decision` is `approve` or `decline`.
  - `sameNetwork` is `true`, `false` or `"unknown"`.
  - `matchNumber` and `enteredNumber` match `^[0-9]{2}$`.
  - The claim's `parentThreadId` must equal `payload.requestId`.
  - `cancel` returns `{status: "cancelled"}`, and `respond` returns `{status: "approved" | "declined"}`.
  - `redeem` returns `{subject, displayName, notAfter, amr}`, never tokens.
- **Endpoint discovery:** `TRIGGER-LINK.md` and `auth/oob/claim` say the `TrustTaskHTTPS` `serviceEndpoint` is the Trust-Task base, and they point to HTTPS binding 0.2 §6 for how to build the request URL (`<base>/trust-tasks`).
- **Generated bindings:**
  - Rust: `trust_tasks_rs::specs::auth::oob::<task>::v0_1`, under the existing `auth` feature. Includes conformance tests.
  - TypeScript: `AuthOob<Task>_v0_1` and `OobShared_v0_1`.
  - Go and Dart: packages and libraries under `specs/auth/oob/...`.

## Backwards compatibility

Everything in this PR is additive. What I checked:

- **Diff against `main`:** every file is new except five generated index files. Those five only gain lines; no line is removed.
  - `trust-tasks-rs/src/schema_index.rs`: new match arms.
  - `trust-tasks-rs/src/specs/auth/mod.rs`: `pub mod oob;`.
  - `trust-tasks-rs/tests/conformance/main.rs`: new test modules.
  - `trust-tasks-ts/src/index.ts`: new namespace exports.
  - `trust-tasks-ts/src/_shared/components.ts`: new hoisted types.
- **Existing specs:** no existing spec, schema, `$id`, Type URI or generated binding changes in content, name or path.
- **Tooling:** no generator or tooling changes. The diff does not touch `scripts/`, `trust-tasks-codegen`, any `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `pubspec.yaml` or `go.mod`. I re-ran all four generators (`cargo run -p trust-tasks-codegen` with `cargo fmt`, and `build-ts-bindings`, `build-go-bindings`, `build-dart-bindings`) and there was no drift.
- **Rust features:** default features are unchanged (`default = ["all-specs"]`). The new modules sit behind the existing `auth` feature, so no new feature is introduced.
- **Packages:** the npm, Go and Dart package exports only gain entries. The new TS shared type names do not collide with existing exports, and `tsc` passes.
- **Registries:** the registry and indexes only gain entries.
- **Versions:** no version is bumped, as RELEASING.md asks. The Release PR sizes the bump from the conventional commits (`feat` gives a minor bump).

## Testing

I ran the same steps the CI workflows run:

- **Registry:** `TT_STRICT_SECURITY_PRIVACY=1 npm run build` passes: 698 specs validated and 1343 examples checked against the envelope schema. `npm run test:infra`, `npm run test-ceremonies` and `npm run check-dart-packages` pass.
- **Bindings conformance:** `npm run check-bindings` reports that all 698 specs agree across TS, Rust, Go and Dart, and that the 1549 declared error codes match Rust `ERROR_CODES`.
- **Generation drift:** Rust codegen with fmt, and the TS, Go and Dart generators, leave the tree clean.
- **Rust:**
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes.
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` passes with default features and with `--all-features`.
  - `cargo test --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --features validate --all-targets` pass, with 0 failures.
  - `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --all-features` passes.
- **TypeScript:**
  - `trust-tasks-ts`: `tsc --noEmit` passes, `npm test` passes 79/79, and `npm run smoke` passes.
  - `trust-tasks-ts-proof`, `-tsp` and `-capability-client`: build, test typecheck and tests all pass.
- **Go:** `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt -l` and `go test -race ./...` pass for the core module, `tsp` and `proof`.
- **Dart:**
  - `trust-tasks-dart`: `dart analyze --fatal-infos` is clean, `dart format --set-exit-if-changed` at the pubspec floor is clean, and `dart test` passes 74/74.
  - The proof, https, didcomm, capability-client and tsp packages: analyze is clean and the tests pass.

## Related

- VTI spec: https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec/pull/58
- Implementations in other repos will link back to this PR.

title: perf: raise TEE keys/sign throughput (vsock storage, fewer round trips, multi-core REST)
body:
## Summary

Load tests of the VTA in a Nitro Enclave found that `keys/sign` throughput is capped by serial sections, not by hardware. This PR removes them in seven independent commits, so each can be kept or dropped on its own. Together they take a c6g.xlarge appliance (1-vCPU enclave) from about 80 to about 195 keys/sign per second, and let bigger enclaves use their CPUs: a c6g.4xlarge with a 2-vCPU enclave reaches about 345, and with a 4-vCPU enclave about 380 to 400.

Only one commit depends on another: the one-write framing changes code added by the storage pool. The rest apply on their own.

## Commits

| # | Commit | What | Risk for review |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `fix(vti-common): pool the enclave's vsock storage connections` | All enclave storage went through one connection behind one mutex. Now a pool of up to 8. Also fixes a stale-response bug: a cancelled request could leave its response for the next caller. | Low; enclave builds only |
| 2 | `fix(vta-enclave): log to stderr only while vsock logging is down` | Every log line was also written synchronously to the enclave console, which nobody can read in production. | Low; enclave builds only. CI does not build the `vsock-log` feature, so this is checked by hand only |
| 3 | `perf(vti-common): send each vsock storage request in one write` | Length and payload went out as two packets. Depends on 1. | Low |
| 4 | `perf(vta-service): read the caller's ACL entry once per keys/sign` | Both sign gates read the same ACL row. Both gates still run, in the same order. | Low; authorization code, so worth a careful look |
| 5 | `perf(vta-service): reuse the context record for the keys/sign custody check` | The context row was read for the policy and again for the custody base path. Adds `effective_context_policy_and_record` (vta-support) and `derive_record_key_in_context` (key custody). | Medium; adds a second entry point to key custody. It falls back to reading the context when the record does not match |
| 6 | `perf(vta-service): serve REST on one worker per CPU` | REST ran on a current-thread runtime, so the VTA used at most one CPU. Now multi-threaded with more than one CPU; unchanged with one. | High; affects every deployment. Handlers now run in parallel, not only interleaved at awaits, so existing non-atomic read-modify-writes become likelier to race |
| 7 | `perf(vta-enclave): serve REST on vsock directly, without the inbound socat` | socat forked per inbound connection, and new connections timed out under load. The VTA now binds vsock itself when the entrypoint sets `VTA_REST_VSOCK_PORT`. | High; changes the enclave entrypoint (part of the image measurement) and the boot path: the parent's connections are refused until the VTA binds |

Commits 4 and 5 take a sign from 10 storage operations to 8.

## Results

`keys/sign/0.1` over REST through a load balancer, EdDSA over 32 bytes, from 50 agents in 5 contexts, open-loop stepped rates of 4 minutes each. "Healthy" means no errors and p95 under 150 ms. Approximate saturation in keys/sign per second:

| Build | c6g.xlarge, 1-vCPU enclave | c6g.4xlarge, 2-vCPU enclave | c6g.4xlarge, 4-vCPU enclave |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` before this PR | about 79 (healthy at 70) | not measured | not measured |
| + 1 | about 97 (healthy at 85) | not measured | not measured |
| + 1, 2 | about 165 (healthy at 160) | about 235 to 245 (see note) | not measured |
| + 1 to 5 | about 195 (healthy at 160, p95 63 ms) | about 287 (p95 30 ms at 235, 4 errors) | not measured |
| + 1 to 7 (this PR) | about 195 (healthy at 160, p95 59 ms) | about 345 (p95 114 ms at 320, 13 errors) | about 380 to 400 (p95 41 ms at 320, 7 errors; 309 ms at 400) |

Below saturation the latency gain is larger than the ceiling gain: on c6g.4xlarge with a 2-vCPU enclave at 235/s, p95 was 600 ms with commits 1 and 2, 30 ms with 1 to 5, and 12 ms with all seven.

The "+ 1 to 5" and "+ 1 to 7" rows are this branch exactly, built and run as they are. Note: the c6g.4xlarge figures for "+ 1, 2" and the 600 ms baseline come from builds with extra timing and counter logging, which is not part of this PR. While investigating, each change was also measured one at a time; those runs found commit 6 worth nothing on a 1-vCPU enclave (it keeps one thread there) and commit 7 worth no throughput but removing connect-timeout errors (7 → 0 at 320/s on a 4-vCPU enclave).

## How the bottlenecks were found

- Storage round trips were serial (commit 1), and console logging serialised every request on the stderr lock (commit 2).
- With those fixed, a 2-vCPU enclave sat half idle at its ceiling. The parent answered each storage request in about 33 µs, yet the round trip measured inside the enclave grew from 0.4 ms to about 4 ms under load. The time was the reply waiting for the single REST thread to poll it (commit 6). More storage connections (32 instead of 8) did not help, which ruled out the pool.
- Each sign made 10 storage round trips, 4 of them repeats or reads of data that almost never changes (commits 4 and 5 remove 2; the audit-key cache below would remove the other 2).
- Inbound socat cost little CPU (about 0.2 core) but caused connection timeouts while forking (commit 7).

## Not in this PR (follow-ups)

- **Audit key cache.** Every audited operation reads the active audit key from storage twice (the marker, then the key). Caching it in `AuditKeyStore` saves both, but a cache per store instance misses a rotation through another instance (the VTC builds several on one keyspace), and it breaks `vti_apv_022_a_waiver_that_cannot_be_audited_is_refused`, which simulates an audit outage by deleting the active marker. Needs a design that keeps VTI-APV-022 (a cache per keyspace that fails closed, or a different fault injection agreed for the test).

It is worth doing. It takes a sign from 8 storage operations to 6, and measured against this PR without it:

| Shape | This PR (no cache) | This PR's changes + audit-key cache |
|---|---|---|
| c6g.xlarge, 1-vCPU enclave | about 195 (healthy at 160) | about 220 (p95 193 ms at 220, 0 errors) |
| c6g.4xlarge, 2-vCPU enclave, commits 1 to 5 only | about 287 (p95 30 ms at 235, 4 errors) | about 300 (p95 15 ms at 235, 0 errors) |
| c6g.4xlarge, 4-vCPU enclave | about 380 to 400 (p95 309 ms at 400, 169 errors) | about 475 to 480 (p95 44 to 49 ms at 400, 22 to 43 errors) |

The cache runs used builds with the extra timing and counter logging, which cost some throughput (with a 2-vCPU enclave, all seven commits reached about 345 without that logging against about 310 with it and with the cache), so the cache figures are more likely low than high.

- **Audit chain lock.** Each audited operation holds the chain lock across one storage insert. With a 4-vCPU enclave, releasing the lock before the insert made 400/s fully healthy and cut p95 at 480/s from 374 to 111 ms. That prototype is not crash-safe (a failed insert leaves a gap in the chain), so it needs a design, not this PR.
- **Parent proxy inbound cap.** `MAX_CONCURRENT_CONNECTIONS = 256` in `deploy/nitro/enclave-proxy/src/channels.rs`. With commit 7, the remaining errors past about 400/s are this cap rejecting load-balancer connections.
- **Replies in one write.** The parent proxy still writes each storage reply as two packets.
- **Overload has no back-pressure.** Past saturation, health checks fail and the appliance restarts instead of shedding load.
- **Restart with a large audit log.** The first audited write after a restart reloads the chain head by scanning the whole audit keyspace over vsock. This will be reported separately.
- **CI does not build `vsock-log`.**

## Checks

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`, workspace doctests, and the vtc-service audit tests
- The enclave feature set (`rest,didcomm,vsock-store,vsock-log,tenant-overlay`) checked and linted on Linux
- Pre-existing on `main`, not from this PR: clippy errors in `vta-persona` (`store.rs`), `vtc-service` (`acl/resource_grant.rs`, `git_ns/projection.rs`) and `vta-service` (`routes/mod.rs:656`) with Rust 1.95; `vti_08_context_create_fits_half_a_default_worker_stack` fails on macOS
- Each change ran on real appliances (c6g.xlarge, c6g.4xlarge) as above

title: perf(audit): cache the active audit key per keyspace, failing closed
body:
**Stacked on #2003** (`perf/vsock-atomic-opcodes` @ 1623c372, itself on #1999). Retarget to `main` once those merge.

## What and why

Every audited operation read the active audit key from storage twice — the `audit_key:active` marker, then the key it names. #1951 (Carlos Rincon) measured removing both at roughly +13–25% `keys/sign` throughput in a Nitro Enclave. This caches it without missing a rotation through another instance, without weakening VTI-APV-022, and without the cancelled-write gap.

## Design

**Per-keyspace write tracking in the store** (`vti-common/src/store/generation.rs`), shared by every handle for a keyspace name:
- **Begin** (before the request leaves): bump the generation, count the write in flight.
- **End** (completed, failed or dropped): bump again, uncount.
- **Unknown only when the frame may have reached the parent.** The pool reports it: `round_trip_within` (under the pool's 10 s per-round-trip deadline) sets the caller's `ever_sent` flag at the same moment as its own per-attempt `sent`, once the whole frame has been written (`request_tracked`, `request_once_tracked`) — so it also survives the caller's future being dropped, where no error can say so. A write that ends with no reply **after** that — transport failure, a deadline that expired after sending, or its future dropped — marks the keyspace *unknown*. A write that ends **before** it (connect error, pool closed, write error, a deadline that expired before the frame was fully written, cancelled before sending) cannot have been applied — the proxy acts only on a whole frame — so it is a known outcome and marks nothing.
- **The unknown mark clears** when a write that *began after it* completes, **or after `UNKNOWN_SETTLE` = 30 s**: longer than any plausible late apply of an abandoned frame (the parent applies a frame as soon as it reads it; the frame is already in its buffer when the enclave gives up, and the pool drops that connection; a parent stalled past 30 s would be failing every storage call). Without it, one timed-out write on `audit_key` — written once in weeks — would switch the cache off until the next rotation.
- **Readers** take a ticket before reading: none while a write is in flight or unknown; a fresh read is cached only if its ticket is still current afterwards.

**Vsock — both pool paths tracked:** `send` → `request_tracked` (plain insert/delete, every single-op fallback, the restore's plain insert) and `send_atomic` → `request_once_tracked` (`OP_TAKE`, `OP_INSERT_IF_ABSENT`, `OP_SWAP_IF_ABSENT`, `OP_MOVE_IF_EQUAL`, the restore's insert-if-absent). In `send`, anything that is not a known read-only opcode is a write.

**Local:** each write's guard runs inside the blocking closure that performs it, so its outcome is always known (a panic excepted → unknown).

**`AuditKeyStore::active` / `try_active`** serve the cached key only under a current ticket and while younger than **`MAX_CACHE_AGE` = 30 s** (belt and braces: bounds anything unforeseen to 30 s of hashing under the previous key, which stays retained and verifiable). The value is per instance; only the tracking is per keyspace.

## Gaps closed
- **Late-applied abandoned write:** a rotation's marker write held by the parent, its writer times out, the parent then applies it → the next read sees the new key. Verified the test fails without the unknown mark.
- **One failed write disabling the cache for weeks:** a pre-send failure (including a pre-send deadline) marks nothing; an after-send unknown settles after 30 s. Verified the pre-send tests fail if every unreplied write is treated as unknown.

## VTI-APV-022
`vti_apv_022_a_waiver_that_cannot_be_audited_is_refused` deletes the marker through `state.audit_key_ks` and passes **unchanged**.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p vti-common --features vsock-store,encryption --lib`: **735 passed**.
- Vsock, both proxy generations, through a different handle than the cache's: one test per write path (insert, insert_raw, remove, insert_if_absent, insert_raw_if_absent, take_raw, swap, move_if_unchanged); an absent take retires the cache iff it sent `OP_TAKE`; the restore after an undecryptable take is two tracked writes (generation +4); late-applied rotation never served stale; in-flight write suppresses caching; a write that never left (plain and atomic path) does not disable caching; an after-send unknown disables it until it settles; **a deadline expiring after the frame was sent disables caching, and one expiring before it does not (both pool paths)**.
- Local: rotation via another instance seen; deleted marker fails closed; a hit reads nothing and any write ends it; failed read not remembered; max age forces a re-read; local in-flight write suppresses caching. `store::generation::tests`: the state machine, including pre-send failure and settle.
- `nextest -p vti-common -p vta-audit`: 700 passed. APV-022 test: passed. (Earlier on this branch: `vta-service` audit 31 passed; `vtc-service` audit / APV-022 / single-admin / syncer / tail 150 passed.)
- `cargo clippy -p vti-common --all-targets -D warnings`: default, `--all-features`, `vsock-store,encryption`. `cargo fmt --check`.

## Backport
none

title: perf(audit): cache the active audit key per keyspace, failing closed (#2004)
body:
perf(audit): cache the active audit key per keyspace, failing closed (#2004)

Every audited operation read the active audit key from storage twice: the
`audit_key:active` marker, then the key it names. #1951 measured removing
both reads at roughly +13-25% keys/sign throughput in a Nitro Enclave.

Per-keyspace write tracking in the store (store/generation.rs), shared by
every handle for a keyspace name:

- A write begins before its request leaves (generation bumped, counted in
  flight) and ends when it completes or is dropped (bumped again).
- A write that ends without a reply after its frame had completely left
  the enclave - transport failure, or its future dropped - marks the
  keyspace unknown: the parent may still apply it. A write that ends before
  its frame left (no connection, pool closed, write error) cannot have been
  applied, so it marks nothing. The pool reports which via a `sent` flag set
  in round_trip once the whole frame is written (request_tracked /
  request_once_tracked).
- The unknown mark clears when a write that began after it completes, or
  after UNKNOWN_SETTLE (30 s) - longer than any plausible late apply of an
  abandoned frame; without it one timed-out write would switch the
  audit_key cache off until the next rotation.
- Readers take a ticket before reading: none while a write is in flight or
  unknown, and a fresh read is cached only if its ticket is still current.
- Vsock: both pool paths are tracked - `send` (request_tracked: plain ops,
  fallbacks, the restore's plain insert) and `send_atomic`
  (request_once_tracked: OP_TAKE, OP_INSERT_IF_ABSENT, OP_SWAP_IF_ABSENT,
  OP_MOVE_IF_EQUAL, the restore). Anything not a known read-only opcode is a
  write.
- Local: each write's guard runs inside the blocking closure that writes, so
  its outcome is always known (a panic excepted).

AuditKeyStore::active / try_active serve the cached key only under a
current ticket and while it is younger than MAX_CACHE_AGE (30 s). A rotation
through another instance, a marker deleted through any handle, and a
rotation the vsock parent applies after its writer gave up all reach the
next read. Read errors are never cached. The value is per instance; sharing
it by keyspace name would hand a decrypted key to a bare handle.

VTI-APV-022: `vti_apv_022_a_waiver_that_cannot_be_audited_is_refused`
deletes the marker through `state.audit_key_ks` and passes unchanged.

Credit: Carlos Rincon measured this in #1951.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
