title: fix(vti-common): pooled enclave storage with atomic multi-step operations (#1999)
body:
fix(vti-common): pooled enclave storage with atomic multi-step operations (#1999)

* fix(vti-common): pool the enclave's vsock storage connections

Inside a Nitro enclave every storage operation went through one vsock
connection behind one mutex held for the whole round trip, so all storage
I/O in the VTA ran strictly one operation at a time. Throughput of anything
that touches storage was capped by the round-trip time, whatever the
enclave's vCPU count: a keys/sign costs about ten round trips, and load
tests saw the same ceiling (about 85 signs/s) with one and with two enclave
vCPUs, with neither the enclave nor the parent CPU saturated.

VsockStore now keeps a bounded pool of connections (up to 8). A request
owns a connection for one complete round trip and returns it only after a
full response; the parent's storage proxy already serves each connection in
its own task, so independent operations now run in parallel. Each
operation is still a single request, and the multi-step operations (swap,
take_raw, move_if_unchanged) are no less atomic than before: the old lock
was released between their steps too.

This also fixes a latent correctness bug. The old code kept the shared
connection after a cancelled request: if a request future was dropped
after writing its request but before reading the response (a request
timeout, a client disconnect), the next caller read the previous caller's
response. A pooled connection that fails or is cancelled mid-round-trip is
dropped instead of reused.

The pool is transport-agnostic and compiled under `test` as well as
`vsock-store`, so its tests run on every platform, not only Linux.

Signed-off-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>
(cherry picked from commit e24a09c841913f6d0981668860012b13002739df)
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vti-common): send each vsock storage request in one write

A storage request was written as two writes, the 4-byte length and then the
payload. On an unbuffered vsock stream each write is its own packet across
the enclave boundary, so every request cost two. The frame is now built in
one buffer and written once.

Measured alone on c6g.4xlarge with a 2-vCPU enclave, in builds with extra
timing logging: saturation about 245 -> 255 keys/sign per second, p95 at
235/s 600 -> 66 ms.
Replies from the parent are still written in two parts; changing that is a
change to the parent's proxy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>
(cherry picked from commit bace8cec27a01fa905aaaa463ccffc9699b1d98a)
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vti-common): make the enclave store's multi-step operations atomic

The parent's storage proxy serves single operations, so the vsock store
ran take_raw, insert_if_absent, swap and move_if_unchanged as sequences of
round trips with nothing excluding a second caller. Two presenters of one
refresh token could both read it before either deleted it and both rotate,
defeating reuse detection (RFC 9700 §4.14.2). The gap was documented as
"single-replica TEE deployments are unaffected in practice", which held
only while one mutex-guarded connection and a single REST thread kept the
steps from overlapping; a connection pool and a multi-thread REST runtime
remove both.

Per-key striped locks (store::key_locks), shared by every handle a
VsockStore hands out, are held across each multi-step operation; two-key
operations take both in stripe order, so crossed swaps cannot deadlock.
This is the local store's guarantee (two multi-step operations on one key
never interleave), per key rather than per keyspace because a vsock round
trip is long. It does not depend on the parent: the enclave is the only
writer to its store.

Tests run each operation 32-wide on a multi-thread runtime against a fake
parent that serves the wire protocol with a delay per request, and assert
exactly one winner; a control test shows the same harness catching the old
unlocked read-then-delete. CI runs them in the Enclave job (they are
behind vsock-store, which no other job compiles).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* perf(vti-common): coalesce only small storage frames

One write per frame keeps a small request to one vsock packet, but copying
a frame near the 16 MB limit just to prepend its length doubles peak memory
for a saving that does not exist: a frame that size spans many packets
anyway. Coalesce up to 64 KiB; above that, write the header and the payload
separately.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vti-common): bound every enclave storage round trip

A parent that accepts a frame and never answers held that request's pool
permit, and for a multi-step operation its key lock, with no end: eight
such requests and every storage operation in the enclave blocks. Each
round trip now has a 10 s deadline (the parent answers in tens of
microseconds); on expiry the request fails and the connection is dropped,
never reused, since its next bytes could be the late answer.

This is also what keeps key_locks within the intent of R1.3 (no lock
across an await): the locks are held across awaits by design, and every
such await is now bounded.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>
Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
Co-authored-by: Carlos Rincon <carlos.r@affinidi.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: feat: sender-bound, purpose-checked Trust Tasks and signed DIDComm sign-in
body:
## Summary

Three consumer changes have merged, and the wallet has to match them:

- **affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#213** removes the bare DIDComm `auth/authenticate` route. It also requires a sender-bound proof and checks the proof purpose.
- **OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1739** has the VTA and VTC act on a DIDComm or TSP Trust Task only when the proof's issuer is the transport sender.
- **OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1740** has the VTA sign its operational documents under `authentication`.

This PR rebuilds #279 on current `main` and **supersedes #279**. About 25 PRs landed after #279 was written, so its four commits served as the guide and were re-implemented against today's code, not cherry-picked.

## What this ports from #279

1. **DIDComm sign-in (#279 commit 1).**
   - `loginViaDidcomm` now runs `loginViaTrustTask` over a `DidcommVtaTransport` addressed to the RP: `auth/challenge/0.1`, then a signed `auth/authenticate/0.2`.
   - Each document is issued by the signing DID, addressed to the RP, and carries `issuedAt` and a fresh `id`.
   - The reply must come from the RP. Three checks enforce this: the bridge's `from` filter, the channel's thread and sender checks, and the reply's proof verified against the RP's DID.
2. **Outbound purpose and binding members (#279 commit 2).**
   - **Purpose:** `signOutboundTask` passes main's existing `proofPurposeForDocumentType` to the signer. Operational documents get `authentication`, and the `ATTESTATION_SLUGS` types get `assertionMethod`; that list includes `auth/oob/grant`.
   - **Binding members:** before signing, `signOutboundTask` names the signer as `issuer` when none is set and fills a missing `id` or `issuedAt`. It refuses a document with no `recipient` (`e.client.identity`).
   - **Callers checked:** every caller on main already sets a recipient, including the auth/oob sign-in from #303 and the step-up and consent paths, which sign outside the channels. Only two test fixtures composed a document without one.
3. **Sender binding (#279 commit 3).**
   - `signOutboundTask` refuses a signer that is not the channel's sender DID. `DidcommVtaTransport` and `TspChannel` pass theirs. REST passes none, because the consumer binds the issuer to the bearer.
   - The same-browser approver authcrypts its `task-consent/decision` as itself, and the worker's session only carries the forward. `buildTaskConsentDecision` gains an optional `sender` and refuses one that is not the signer.
   - `doDidcommLogin` refuses a per-site persona up front, because the persona's keys stay at the agent. Persona sign-in stays on REST. The persona document-signer plumbing in `buildVtaSession`, which is now unused, is removed.
4. **Inbound purpose (#279 commit 4).**
   - `verifyTrustTaskProof` with `expectedProofPurpose` also requires the verification method to be listed under that relationship in the signer's DID document (`listsMethodUnder`).
   - These now require `authentication`: replies (`verifyTrustTaskReply`), `task-consent/request` and `task-consent/decision#response`. `task-consent/request` and `#response` used to require `assertionMethod`.
   - An unsigned success `#response` is dropped. Error documents may stay unsigned.

## Adapted

- **One purpose policy.** The purpose comes from main's `trust-tasks/purpose.ts`, not from #279's separate `outboundProofPurpose` table. `task-consent/decision` names its purpose explicitly through the same function.
- **Mediator replies.** `verifyTrustTaskReply` and `DidcommVtaTransport` take an optional reply purpose, and the Mediator Lens passes `"any"`. A mediator signs its `messaging/*` replies for a purpose of its own choosing, and it is none of the consumers above. #279 required `authentication` there too, which a mediator is under no obligation to meet. Every other channel still requires `authentication`, and a test pins that the lens is the only opt-out.
- **`signTrustTask`'s default stays `assertionMethod`.** #279 changed it, but it is exported API. Channels now pass the purpose explicitly, and test fixtures that stand in for the VTA sign their replies under `authentication`, as the VTA now does.
- **`rpHttpsSender`** no longer needs its own authentication-only signer, because the channel rule now gives the same answer.
- **`loginDidcomm`'s page result** is built in one small module (`didcomm-login.ts`) and pinned by a test.

## Dropped, because main already has it

- The per-type purpose rule (`trust-tasks/purpose.ts`).
- The page-facing `signTrustTask` changes: the `asDid` refusal (#289, #290) and the type-chosen purpose for the holder.
- The step-up rework (#280, #291), which also covered #279's step-up mediator-DID removal and the `assertionMethod`-signed approve-request refusal.
- The session-key `auth/authenticate/0.2` login (#284) and the approver consent vouching (#293).
- `vaultTaskSigner`'s purpose refusal. The VTA's `vault/sign-trust-task` now picks the purpose from the document type (VTI-KEY-106), so REST persona sign-in keeps working.
- #279's removal of the step-up VTA mediator page parameter and setting. It would have changed the page-facing API.

## Backwards compatibility

- **Page-facing API unchanged.**
  - `window.vtaWallet` and its methods (`login`, `loginDidcomm`, `proxyLogin`, `signTrustTask` and the rest) keep their signatures, parameters, result shapes and bridge messages.
  - `loginDidcomm` still resolves with exactly `{ accessToken, refreshToken, sessionId, holderDid, timings }`. A new extension test pins that shape. The existing provider legacy-login test still pins the bridge message.
- **Exported `core` API.**
  - `TaskSigner.sign`'s new options argument is optional, and the new `signOutboundTask`, `verifyTrustTaskReply`, `buildTaskConsentDecision` and `DidcommVtaTransport` arguments are all optional.
  - `loginViaDidcomm` keeps every existing option. `signing` and `scope` are new and optional.
  - `DidcommLoginResult` is kept and gains `expiresIn` and `scope`. On the challenge flow, `accessExpiresAt` is computed from `expiresIn`. `refreshExpiresAt` is `0` because `auth/authenticate` does not report it; the old flow also returned `0` when the RP said nothing.
- **Deprecated adapter.** `loginViaDidcomm` called without `signing` still sends the bare `auth/authenticate`. With no signing key there is nothing to sign, so this is the only thing those options can mean. RPs running webvh #213 or later refuse it, as they would refuse that caller today. The old tests for that path are kept unchanged.
  - This repo's CLAUDE.md asks for no compatibility arms. The adapter is kept because this change had to stay backwards compatible, and the comment beside it explains why.
- **No `!` in any commit title.** No unavoidable break remains.
- **No manifest permission changes, no stored-state migration, no new dependencies.**
- **Wire behaviour changes only where the consumer PRs require it:**
  - outbound purpose and binding members (webvh #213, VTI #1739, VTI #1740);
  - sender equals signer, including the persona refusal on DIDComm and the approver sending as itself (VTI #1739, webvh #213);
  - inbound `authentication` with the key-relationship check (VTI #1740, webvh #213).

## Testing

- **Ported and adapted from #279:**
  - `rp-login.didcomm-challenge.mjs`: real channel and in-memory RP. It covers order, issuer, recipient, `issuedAt`, unique ids, `authentication` proofs, the `from` filter, impostor senders and signers, unsigned replies, refusals, a persona signer, and the result shape.
  - `vta.outbound-signing.mjs`: purpose by type, binding members, sender binding, the relationship check, and reply purpose.
  - `inbound.task-consent.mjs`: the decision's issuer, purpose, `issuedAt` and id; the relay sending as the approver; a mismatched sender refused; an `assertionMethod` consent request refused.
  - `inbound.task-consent-outcome.mjs` and `inbound.consent-schema.mjs`: an unsigned or `assertionMethod` success is dropped.
- **New extension tests:**
  - `didcomm-login.test.mts`: the page-level result shape and the persona refusal.
  - `consent-relay-sender.test.mts`: the relay sends as the approver.
  - `mediator-lens.test.mts`: the lens is the only reply-purpose opt-out.
- **Local results.** Every `run` step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` passes locally from a clean build on Node 26: `npm ci`, lint, build, tests for every workspace, the bundle and surface guards, and the Web Store packaging checks. Core: 862/862. Extension: 947/947.

## Supersedes

This supersedes #279, which will be closed in its favour.

title: feat: sender-bound, purpose-checked Trust Tasks and signed DIDComm sign-in (#304)
body:
feat: sender-bound, purpose-checked Trust Tasks and signed DIDComm sign-in (#304)

* feat(core): sign each outbound Trust Task for the purpose its type requires

The VTA, the VTC and the did-hosting RP now check the proof purpose on what
they receive (VTI #1740, affinidi-webvh-service #213): an operational document
must be an authentication proof, and an attestation an assertionMethod one.
Channels signed everything for assertionMethod.

- signOutboundTask passes proofPurposeForDocumentType(envelope.type), the
  wallet's existing per-type rule, to the signer.
- TaskSigner.sign gains an optional TaskSignOptions argument; existing
  one-argument signers still type-check.
- localTaskSigner signs for the purpose it is given, or the type's purpose
  when called without one.
- The RP HTTPS sender no longer needs its own authentication-only signer.
- task-consent/decision names its purpose explicitly (assertionMethod).
- signTrustTask's default is unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(core): bind every outbound Trust Task to its signer and audience

VTI #1739 has the VTA and VTC act on a DIDComm or TSP document only when it
names its issuer, the proven signer, and they key their replay window on
(issuer, id). signOutboundTask now, before the proof is taken:

- names the signer as issuer when the document has none;
- fills a missing id or issuedAt;
- refuses a document with no recipient (e.client.identity), since a signed
  document with no audience is replayable anywhere.

Every document this package builds already carries a recipient, including
the auth/oob sign-in, step-up and task-consent paths, which sign outside the
channels. Only two test fixtures composed one without it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(rp-login): sign in over DIDComm with auth/challenge and a signed auth/authenticate

affinidi-webvh-service #213 removes the bare DIDComm auth/authenticate route,
which issued a session to the authcrypt sender and read nothing from the
body. loginViaDidcomm now runs loginViaTrustTask over a DidcommVtaTransport
addressed to the RP, so there is one login implementation for every
transport.

- Each document is issued by the signing DID, addressed to the RP, and
  carries issuedAt and a fresh id. Both are signed for authentication.
- The reply is accepted only from the RP: the bridge's from filter, the
  channel's thread and sender checks, and the reply's proof verified against
  the RP's DID.
- The new inputs are optional: signing (who signs in) and scope.
- DidcommLoginResult keeps every member and gains expiresIn and scope.
- A caller that passes no signing still gets the bare message, deprecated.
  It has nothing to sign with, so that is the only thing those options can
  mean.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix: send each DIDComm and TSP document as its signer

The VTA, the VTC and the did-hosting RP act on a DIDComm or TSP document
only when its proven signer is the transport sender (VTI #1739,
affinidi-webvh-service #213). Two paths signed as one DID and sent as
another.

- signOutboundTask takes the channel's sender DID and refuses a signer that
  is not it. DidcommVtaTransport and TspChannel pass theirs; REST passes
  none, because the consumer binds the issuer to the bearer.
- The same-browser approver relay authcrypts the task-consent/decision as
  the approver, and the worker's session only carries the forward.
  buildTaskConsentDecision gains an optional sender and refuses one that is
  not the signer.
- A per-site persona cannot be sent as, because its keys, keyAgreement
  included, live at the VTA. doDidcommLogin refuses a persona up front, and
  persona sign-in stays on REST. The unused persona document-signer plumbing
  in buildVtaSession is removed.
- loginDidcomm's page-level result is built in one place
  (didcomm-login.ts) and pinned by a test to the members it has always
  carried.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix: verify what the executors push and reply under authentication

affinidi-webvh-service #213 and VTI #1740 sign every non-error reply, every
task-consent/request and every step-up approve-request with the executor's
operational key, under authentication, and check that a key is listed under
the relationship its proof names. The wallet read these as assertionMethod.

- verifyTrustTaskProof with expectedProofPurpose also requires the
  verification method to be listed under that relationship in the signer's
  DID document (listsMethodUnder).
- verifyTrustTaskReply, parseTaskConsentRequest and parseTaskConsentOutcome
  require authentication. The step-up approve-request already did, and now
  gets the relationship check too.
- An unsigned task-consent/decision#response is dropped. Error documents may
  still be unsigned.
- verifyTrustTaskReply and DidcommVtaTransport take an optional reply
  purpose. The Mediator Lens passes "any": a mediator signs its messaging/*
  replies for a purpose of its own, and is none of the consumers above.
- Test fixtures that stand in for the VTA sign their replies for
  authentication, as the VTA now does.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(demo): describe the DIDComm sign-in as a signed challenge

The demo still said the RP authenticated the authcrypt sender of a bare
MSG_AUTHENTICATE. It is now auth/challenge then a signed auth/authenticate,
and the RP checks the proof.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat: wallet sign-in with a trigger link (VTI 7a, auth/oob)
body:
## Summary

Wallet sign-in with a trigger link (VTI spec chapter 7a, sign-in trigger-link contract C1 to C9). The plugin now acts as reader and approver for `auth/oob/*`:

- **Trigger-link reader** (`@openvtc/pnm-core/links`). It parses and validates links in the VTI-LNK-020 order, with the VTI-LNK-021 outcomes and messages.
- **Click interception.** A trusted click on a sign-in code (`https://link.trustoverip.org/t#_from=…&_id=…&_exp=…&_type=/vti/flow/sign-in/0.1`) opens the wallet's sign-in window instead of navigating. The page's origin is recorded at the click, held to the browser-attested `sender.origin`, and checked against the community's `SignInPortal` service (VTI-LNK-056, 105). The page is told nothing about the result.
- **Approver flow** (`core/src/vtc/oob-sign-in.ts`, `extension/src/sign-in-flows.ts`). The wallet order follows C3: check membership, verify the community's DID document, confirm, then claim with a throwaway `K_a`. After that come the two-digit number, identify, review and respond (grant or decline). Closing the window cancels a held claim.
- **VTA signing** (`core/src/vault/sign-oob.ts`). `identify` is signed for `authentication`. `grant` is an attestation (`auth/oob/grant` is added to `ATTESTATION_SLUGS`) and carries the `org.openvtc.uv-consent` decision (C9).
- **User-verification passkey.** It is an ES256 (P-256) WebAuthn credential, separate from the unlock passkey, because `vti-webauthn` verifies P-256 only. It is created and enrolled with the VTA (`org.openvtc.uv-key`) on the first approval. The WebAuthn challenge is the UTF-8 bytes of the grant digest D.
- **Trust-task transport.** Sign-in documents are POSTed to `<TrustTaskHTTPS base>/trust-tasks` (HTTPS binding 0.2 §6). The URL is composed with the existing `trustTaskUrl`, the same way the VTA calls compose theirs.
- **Content script build.** The content script is now built on its own (IIFE, no code splitting) so it can import the parser. A new CI step asserts that `content.js` contains no `import` or `export`.

## Backwards compatibility

I checked each point against `origin/main` and fixed what broke.

**1. Legacy SIOPv2 API: unchanged.** `window.vtaWallet.login`, `loginDidcomm` and `proxyLogin` keep their signatures, bridge messages, results and errors. They are marked `@deprecated` in JSDoc and print one console warning per method per page. Nothing pinned them before, so a new test (`provider-legacy-login.test.mts`) now covers:
- arity;
- the posted `{source, id, method, params}` message, with params passed through untouched;
- the result and the error message passed through verbatim;
- the content script's routing to the same runtime types;
- the one-time notice.

**2. Page-facing API: additive only.**
- No member of `window.vtaWallet` was added, removed or changed.
- No page message shape or `vtawallet:*` event changed.
- One new runtime message type exists, `vta-wallet/trigger-link`. It travels from the content script to the worker and never reaches the page, and it is in `PAGE_FACING_RUNTIME_TYPES` so its origin is browser-attested.

**3. Manifest: no change.** There are no new permissions, host permissions or content-script matches. The provider is still registered at runtime only for granted origins. On a site that is not granted, a sign-in code navigates to the link host as before.

**4. Click interception: found a break and fixed it.** The spec's reader accepts a trigger link on any host, and it calls a link with reserved names in the query `invalid`. So the handler would have prevented navigation on ordinary links such as `https://shop.example/item?_id=5` or `https://docs.example/page#_from=toc`.
- **Host and shape gate.** The handler now acts only on an `isTrusted`, unmodified primary click on an `https` link on the configured link host (default `link.trustoverip.org`), at path `/t`, with the fields in the fragment. The background applies the same gate again.
- **No wallet connected.** While no VTA is connected, no click is taken. A browser with the plugin but no wallet behaves exactly like one without it: the click lands on the link host's no-wallet page (C2). If the wallet is disconnected after the page loaded, the worker finishes the navigation it prevented.
- **Tests.** New tests cover look-alike links, non-link clicks, the no-wallet case, a configured host, and a `send` that throws after an extension reload. In every case the page is not prevented or broken.
- **Locked wallet.** A locked wallet still takes the click. The sign-in window shows any error, and the page is unaffected.

**5. Stored state: no migration.** Wallet, settings and connection storage shapes are unchanged. The only new persisted item is the UV passkey's credential id, under its own IndexedDB key. It is absent until the first approval and written only after the VTA accepts the enrolment. Existing users do not re-enrol anything for legacy login or any existing feature. Sign-in flow records live in `chrome.storage.session` only.

**6. Shared `core` exports: additive.**
- Added the `./links` subpath and root re-exports of `links`, `vault/sign-oob` and `vtc/oob-sign-in`.
- Added `auth/oob/grant` to `ATTESTATION_SLUGS`, which affects only that type.
- No existing export changed or was removed. The PWA and the demos build and test unchanged.

## Testing

I ran every step of the CI workflow locally on Node 26 from a clean build, and all passed:
- `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test`: 1915 tests, 0 failures (core 836, extension 940, tsp-js 124, demo-rp 6, reviewer-demo 9);
- every bundle assertion, including the new content-script one;
- packaging and the Web Store zip checks;
- the action-pinning check.

CI also runs Node 24.

The `auth/oob` payload schema tests run when the `dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf` `feat/auth-oob` schemas are checked out. They skip in CI.

Plugin sign-in against a real VTA needs the plugin's VTA-minted holder to be an enrolled device, because the VTA signs `identify` only for enrolled devices. A decision on how to handle this is pending.

title: feat: wallet sign-in with a trigger link (VTI 7a, auth/oob) (#303)
body:
feat: wallet sign-in with a trigger link (VTI 7a, auth/oob) (#303)

* feat(core): trigger-link reader (VTI spec 7a)

Add @openvtc/pnm-core/links: a pure parser and validator for trigger links,
from text to a parsed link or a reason and outcome, in the evaluation order
of VTI-LNK-020. Covers fragment-only fields with the query ignored, WHATWG
form decoding split at the first '=', unknown names ignored and reserved
names refused when repeated, _from classification with agent names (/@)
refused as unsupported-vid, the _id base64url rules, _exp grammar and the
60 s allowance, the _type path form resolved against https and the
lowercased host, the host rules, the 1,536-code-point limit, and the
VTI-LNK-021 outcome/message table.

The module imports nothing, so it sits at layer 0 beside util. Tests cover
every row of the chapter's Examples table plus each rule's edges.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(core): state the proof purposes the VTA signs sign-trust-task for

The response comment claimed every vault/sign-trust-task proof is
assertionMethod. The VTA chooses the purpose from the document type
(VTI-KEY-106): the auth/oob/grant is an attestation, signed for
assertionMethod; auth/oob/identify is signed for authentication.

Mirror the VTA's ATTESTATION_SLUGS change (contract C5) by adding
auth/oob/grant to the wallet's copy, and pin both purposes in the test.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(core): approver side of wallet sign-in (auth/oob/*)

vtc/oob-sign-in.ts is the protocol for the member's wallet: select the
SignInPortal and TrustTaskHTTPS services from the community's verified DID
document (matched on type, first usable in document order, host rules),
resolve that document afresh, compare the activation origin with the
portal origin (VTI-LNK-105), build claim (K_a issuer, parentThreadId =
requestId), identify, prove, grant, respond and cancel, and refuse any
reply not signed by the community for assertionMethod with a key its
document lists there, not threaded to the request, or whose step 1 / step 2
does not match what the wallet knows.

vault/sign-oob.ts isolates everything that depends on the VTA's
not-yet-final signing shapes (TODO(vta-oob-signing)): identify goes through
vault/sign-trust-task as today; grant carries a WebAuthn consent decision
over the grant digest (contract C6).

Payload types are local, marked TODO: replace with generated trust-tasks
types.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(core): deadlines and notAfter in epoch seconds (sign-in contract C9)

decisionDeadline is read as integer epoch seconds, with RFC 3339 also
accepted as C9 allows; the grant's notAfter is integer epoch seconds.
contextDigest already matched C9 (base58btc sha2-256 multihash over the
JCS-canonical signed step 2 response).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(extension): sign in with a trigger link (click, approver flow)

Click handling (VTI-LNK-056, contract C2): the content script catches a
person's plain primary click (event.isTrusted) on an anchor whose href is a
trigger link, records location.origin at the click, prevents navigation and
hands the link to the worker fire-and-forget. A link that is not a trigger
link (pass-on) navigates normally. Nothing is posted back to the page. The
worker requires the body origin to equal the browser-attested sender
origin, re-parses the link, keeps it and the origin in storage.session
under a flow id, and opens the sign-in window via openConsentWindow.

content.js is now its own vite build (IIFE, codeSplitting: false) so it
can import the core parser without risking a shared chunk; CI asserts it
stays one classic script.

The sign-in flow (contract C3) runs in the offscreen document
(sign-in-flows.ts): parse, known-community check against the VTA vault's
didSelfIssued entries targeting the VTC (listed whole, matched locally),
resolve and verify the VTC document, wrong-origin against SignInPortal,
then the confirm screen with the name from the wallet's record. Only after
Continue is K_a generated and auth/oob/claim sent; then prove (typed number,
identify signed via vault/sign-trust-task), the step 2 review (location,
browser, sameNetwork), and respond with the grant the VTA signs after a
passkey assertion over the grant digest (C6). Decline signs a decline grant
without UV; closing the window cancels a held claim. The window
(sign-in-view.tsx) names only its flow id.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(extension): deprecate window.vtaWallet login, loginDidcomm and proxyLogin

Sign-in contract C7: wallet sign-in with a trigger link is the default; the
SIOPv2-era page methods stay working as legacy. Mark them @deprecated on the
provider interface and their parameter types, warn once per page in the
console when one is called, and document the new flow and the deprecation
in the README, including that the click needs the portal origin granted.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(core): VTA signing shapes and C9 wire details for wallet sign-in

- The TrustTaskHTTPS serviceEndpoint is the full POST URL, used exactly as
  published; nothing is appended (C9).
- Deadlines are integer epoch seconds only; sameNetwork is true, false or
  "unknown"; prove and respond carry parentThreadId (C9).
- vault/sign-oob.ts now speaks the VTA's shapes (feat/oob-sign-in-vta): a
  grant's vault/sign-trust-task/0.2 payload carries
  ext["org.openvtc.uv-consent"].decision, a task-consent/decision/0.2 to
  the VTA, issued and signed (assertionMethod) by the device transport key,
  with challenge = payloadDigest = D and webauthn evidence. The WebAuthn
  challenge is the UTF-8 bytes of D.
- UV passkey enrolment: device/heartbeat/0.2 with
  ext["org.openvtc.uv-key"] (kind webauthn, P-256 zDn Multikey), plus
  P-256 SPKI and Multikey helpers.
- Tests pin each shape and validate every auth/oob payload against the
  feat/auth-oob schemas when that checkout is present.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(extension): ES256 UV passkey, enrolment and the VTA's grant shapes

The sign-in window approves with a dedicated ES256 (P-256) passkey, because
vti-webauthn verifies P-256 only; the holder's PRF passkey stays as it is.
The first approval on a browser creates it, enrols it with the VTA over the
device's own session (device/heartbeat ext org.openvtc.uv-key) and only
then remembers it. The assertion is over the UTF-8 bytes of the grant
digest and travels as task-consent/decision/0.2 webauthn evidence, signed
in the offscreen document by the holder's transport key.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(core): enrol the UV passkey on an unregistered device via device/register

device/heartbeat/0.2 needs an existing device binding, and the wallet has
never sent device/register. Enrolment now tries the heartbeat first and, on
the VTA's stable not_found reject reason, registers the device with
device/register/0.2 (companion/browser) carrying the same
ext["org.openvtc.uv-key"]. Any other refusal is surfaced, not papered over.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(core): POST sign-in tasks to <TrustTaskHTTPS base>/trust-tasks

A TrustTaskHTTPS serviceEndpoint is a Trust-Task base, and documents are
POSTed to <base>/trust-tasks (HTTPS binding 0.2 section 6). The sign-in
code used the published endpoint as the full POST URL. It now composes the
URL with trustTaskUrl from vta/endpoint.ts, the same way the VTA calls do,
dropping a trailing slash on the base. Fixtures publish the base (.../v1)
rather than .../v1/trust-tasks.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(extension): keep every page's links and the legacy sign-in unchanged

- Take a click only for an https link on the configured link host
  (default link.trustoverip.org), at path /t, with the fields in the
  fragment. The spec's reader accepts a trigger link on any host and calls a
  query-form link 'invalid', so the click handler prevented navigation on
  ordinary links such as https://shop.example/item?_id=5. The background
  holds the same gate again.
- Take no click while the wallet has no active VTA connection, so a browser
  with the plugin but no wallet behaves as one without it. If the wallet is
  disconnected after the page loaded, the background finishes the
  navigation the content script prevented.
- Pin window.vtaWallet.login, loginDidcomm and proxyLogin: arity, bridge
  message, result and error passed through unchanged, routing to the same
  runtime types, and a console notice once per method.
- Fix the JSDoc @deprecated notes' line breaks, and drop a stray blank
  line in webauthn-prf-unlock.ts.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

body:
Bumps [@openvtc/trust-tasks](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/tree/HEAD/trust-tasks-ts) from 0.23.0 to 0.23.1.
Changelog

Sourced from @​openvtc/trust-tasks's changelog.

0.23.1 — 2026-10-03

Added

  • vtc: Cooling-off actions, a reduction-pending notice and an offline-write record type (#719)

OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1920 found in the vtc/admin/actions family.

vtc/admin/actions/_shared/0.2 adds the cooling-off action. A removal of an administrator with no third party to consent is parked for a cooling-off period and lands by itself unless its requester cancels. 0.1 could only say that by omitting threshold and expiresAt against its own prose and carrying the landing time in ext. 0.2 adds category coolingOff, landsAt (when it lands), cancellableBy (requester), closedReason landedAfterCoolingOff, and callerRole subject, so the administrator being removed can see the action. list, show, cancel and acknowledge 0.2 re-point at _shared 0.2; their request payloads and error codes are unchanged.

vtc/members/authority-reduction-pending-notice/0.1 tells the subject that a reduction is cooling off, before it lands. The subject cannot block it, because a veto held by the subject would protect a compromised subject. One-way, proof REQUIRED.

vtc/operator/offline-write/0.1 is a record type, never sent. An acknowledge action for an operator's offline write (vtc admin emergency-bootstrap and its siblings) names it as typeUri and carries the record as payload. Before, there was no Type URI to name, because those commands are not Trust Tasks. sideEffects none. It follows the registry's existing never-sent-on-its-own documents (auth/step-up/approver/attest, auth/signing-key/authorize).

Updates `wrangler` from 4.147.0 to 4.148.0
Release notes

Sourced from wrangler's releases.

wrangler@4.148.0

Minor Changes

  • #16051 b4e1299 Thanks @​devteamaegis! - Add --source-namespace and --source-repo-name to wrangler queues subscription create for the artifacts.repo source

    The Event Subscriptions API requires source.namespace and source.repo_name for artifacts.repo subscriptions, but Wrangler had no way to pass them, so --source artifacts.repo always failed with a validation error. Both flags are now required for this source, and wrangler queues subscription get shows the subscription's resource as <namespace>/<repo-name>.

  • #15998 b75421f Thanks @​dario-piotrowicz! - Add assets.base_path support to Workers Assets

    Serve an asset directory from a public URL prefix without changing its on-disk layout:

    {
  "assets": {
    "directory": "./public",
    "base_path": "/docs"
  }
}

    Wrangler, preview, Miniflare, and generated build configuration preserve the explicitly selected value, while the Asset Worker normalizes it and strips the prefix only for asset lookup. Requests passed to a user Worker, request-facing headers, and redirects retain the public path. Relative pathname inputs are interpreted as root-relative prefixes, URL-shaped values are rejected, and omitting the option preserves existing root-path behavior.

    Authored _headers and _redirects rules continue to match full public paths. In particular, both the source and destination of an authored 200 asset rewrite must include the configured public prefix; Asset Worker-generated redirects are prefixed automatically.

  • #16005 4d308f6 Thanks @​oOPa! - Add a --experimental-mode instant option to wrangler kv namespace create

    This lets entitled accounts create Workers KV Instant namespaces while the feature is in private beta.

  • #16030 aa2f9b7 Thanks @​edmundhung! - Add email-protected Quick Tunnels to wrangler dev

    Pass one or more --tunnel-allowed-mail flags to require email authentication when exposing a local development server through a Quick Tunnel. Each value can be an exact email address or a domain pattern.

  • #15283 2dde890 Thanks @​shubhxho! - Support deleting secrets with wrangler versions secret bulk

    Set a secret's value to null in JSON input to remove it from the new Worker version. Bulk output now distinguishes between created and deleted secrets, so retrying wrangler secret bulk with wrangler versions secret bulk preserves requested deletions. Deploy the new version with wrangler versions deploy to apply the changes to production traffic.

Patch Changes

  • #15534 2b1a0ca Thanks @​vahidshaik1901! - Improve guidance for conflicting Wrangler configuration files

    When user and generated deploy configurations are found under different base paths, Wrangler now identifies the expected deploy configuration location, suggests how to resolve the conflict, and links to the relevant documentation.

title: docs(rooms): files in VTC data rooms, and the VTA as key authority for cloud accounts
body:
Two design notes, no code. They are for review before any of it is specified in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf or built.

## `docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md`: files in VTC data rooms

- **Records and blobs.** A room record can carry files. Each file is encrypted end to end with a per-file key derived from the room's MLS storage key, using HKDF and then STREAM chunking. The host stores only ciphertext. The member's VTA releases the per-file key through `rooms/keys/file-key/0.1`, and the browser extension does the crypto, so the page never holds a key.
- **Pluggable blob store.** A `BlobStore` trait has four backends: local directory, S3, GCS and Walrus. Uploads and downloads go over `rooms/blobs/*` Trust Tasks, reusing the chunked, resumable `backup_transfer`.
- **Storage configs.** Any number of configs can exist, and each room is assigned to one. Each config has a per-room prefix, and a room can be assigned or migrated to another config.
- **Limits** apply at three scopes: the room, a member within a room, and a single object. Each scope limits file count, file size and total bytes, and each config has a capacity. Uploads reserve their space first, and policy can tighten the limits. Overrides use a new `vtc.rooms.admin` capability.
- **Usage reporting:** counters, 400 days of daily usage, egress, alerts and CSV export.
- **Credentials are unrecoverable by administrators.** The VTC holds no cloud secret. Credentials of at most 15 minutes come from the VTA (see the next note). Ambient identity is also supported, and a `sealed` fallback is documented but discouraged.
- **UX** is covered for the console, the member portal and the extension, along with a parties table, the specs needed, prerequisites, phases P0–P12, and open questions.

## `docs/05-design-notes/vta-external-accounts.md`: the VTA as key authority for cloud and third-party accounts

- **Driver models:** one `ExternalAuthDriver` per model:
  - `aws-roles-anywhere`, with the VTA as the CA;
  - `gcp-wif-pinned`, with an uploaded JWKS;
  - `azure-cert`;
  - `oauth2-private-key-jwt`;
  - `s3-static-presign`;
  - `sui-signer`, for Walrus;
  - `static-secret`, which is never released.
- **No inbound surface on the VTA, by requirement.** Each model pins the VTA's public material in the provider's account. Nothing calls back into the VTA, and the only egress is to token endpoints. Plain OIDC-discovery federation is excluded for that reason: the host serving the JWKS would become a trust root.
- **Issuing and signing.** `external/credentials/issue/0.1` has the VTA perform the exchange and downscope the result. Responses are sealed through a new `SealedPayloadV1::ExternalCredential` variant. `external/sign/0.1` signs only protocol-defined bytes, following the `keys/sign-sshsig` precedent, so it is never a general oracle.
- **Management** goes through `external/accounts/*` Trust Tasks, so the VTC console can drive it. It uses two capabilities, `external-accounts-manage` and `external-auth-use`. Changes need DTTE consent from approvers signing with their own DIDs, while suspend and revoke take one person.
- **Also covered:** generated setup and probe, key handling (derived P-256, wrapped RSA, `rcgen` CA, rotation), backup, audit, phases E0–E6 and open questions.

## Unverified, and flagged in the notes
- Whether GCP Workload Identity accepts ES256.
- Whether Roles Anywhere accepts a session policy on each request.
- The exact Sui secp256r1 digest.
- Whether `object_store` passes `cargo-deny`.

## Decision wanted
Open question Q2 in the data-rooms note: must a VTC that hosts rooms with files keep a runtime link to its VTA? The proposal is yes.

title: docs(rooms): files in VTC data rooms, and the VTA as key authority for cloud accounts (#1993)
body:
docs(rooms): files in VTC data rooms, and the VTA as key authority for cloud accounts (#1993)

* docs(rooms): files in a pluggable blob store, and working with a room from a VTC

A design note, docs/05-design-notes/data-rooms-files.md. Nothing is built.

A file is a record plus a blob. The record stays sealed exactly as today and
gains a cleartext `blobs` reference. The blob is the file's ciphertext:
- chunked with the STREAM construction, so truncation, reordering and splicing
  fail to authenticate;
- under a per-file key derived from the epoch storage key with HKDF, bound to
  the room, the file and the epoch.

The member's VTA keeps the group and releases one file's key through a new
`rooms/keys/file-key` task, so file bytes never pass through the VTA and the
storage key never reaches a browser.

The host moves blobs as chunked Trust Tasks over vti_common::backup_transfer,
so any binding carries them and no REST exception is added. A pluggable
BlobStore has three backends: a local directory and S3-compatible storage
(both via object_store), and Walrus. The note states what Walrus changes:
- blobs are public;
- deletion is cryptographic only;
- storage lapses unless extended.

Per-room limits are set by the hosting VTC: the rooms policy returns them at
creation, and an administrator can override one room. Members see limits and
usage before uploading. A new vtc.rooms.admin capability gates the overrides.

The VTC experience is split as the console and portal already are:
- the console administers hosting (storage, limits, activity), never content;
- the member portal is where people browse, search, preview, upload and
  curate, and where a room's owner creates and runs it, all through the
  wallet extension and the member's VTA.

Also lists the spec changes that land in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf first, the two
owner-side prerequisites (owner MLS tasks, `pnm rooms owner`), and an
eleven-phase plan.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(rooms): storage configs rooms are assigned to, limits at three scopes, usage reporting, unrecoverable credentials

Revises the files design note following review.

Storage configs (§7). A VTC defines as many named configs as it wants, each
one backend with its own account and credentials. Every room is assigned to
one config, and one config serves any number of rooms. Each blob records the
config it was written to, so reassigning a room never strands its files, and a
migration task moves them. The rooms policy picks a room's config at creation,
optionally from a list the creator may choose from.

Credentials (§7.4). The VTC can use them; no administrator can recover them:
- First choice is holding no secret: ambient cloud identity for S3, and for
  Walrus a P-256 key in the community's VTA used through the signing oracle
  (Sui accepts secp256r1). The digest compatibility is to be verified before
  the Walrus phase.
- Otherwise a write-only credential, sealed in the browser with sealed_transfer
  and encrypted at rest under a key derived from the VTC's secret. No surface
  returns it; it is shown only by fingerprint.
- Credentials are excluded from backup, because a VTC backup carries the VTC's
  key bundle.
- Storage changes park for a second administrator.
- The note says plainly that this protects against administrators, not against
  whoever operates the machine.

Limits (§6). The room, each member in the room, and each object, measured as
file count, file size and total size, plus a storage config's capacity:
- usage is charged to the member at the root of the presented chain, so
  agents spend their member's quota;
- uploads reserve against every scope at begin;
- refusals name the limit that was hit;
- private rooms get no per-member limits, because the host cannot tell members
  apart.

Usage reporting (§6.3): live counters per room, member and config, a daily
history kept 400 days with egress, threshold alerts on the console's live
channel, and CSV export. Members see their own and the room's usage, and room
owners see theirs per member.

The console gains Storage and Usage pages, and the phase plan grows to P0–P12.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(rooms): GCS, and federation so a VTC off AWS or GCP still stores no cloud key

A VTC need not run on the cloud it stores to, so ambient identity is not
enough. Adds a `federated` auth mode for S3 and GCS: the VTC acts as a minimal
OIDC issuer.
- AWS: an IAM OIDC provider and AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity.
- GCP: Workload Identity Federation, the STS exchange and optional
  service-account impersonation.
- Each config gets its own `sub`, so a role trusted for one bucket cannot be
  used for another.
- Tokens last five minutes and cloud credentials at most an hour.
- Discovery and the JWKS are declared REST exceptions beside
  /.well-known/did.jsonl.
- The console generates the cloud-side setup verbatim, and a
  mint → exchange → canary probe runs before the config parks for a second
  administrator.

The token-signing key lives in the community's VTA, behind a new
protocol-defined `keys/sign-oidc-token` task, so the VTC host never holds it.
A local federation key is the fallback where the VTC has no runtime VTA link.

Corrects the Walrus signer. The VTA's general oracle signs caller bytes only
under its opaque-signing domain prefix, so its output cannot be a Sui
signature. Walrus needs its own task, `keys/sign-sui-transaction`, built like
`keys/sign-sshsig`: it accepts only Walrus storage calls and has its own
capability.

Also adds Google Cloud Storage as a native backend through object_store.
GCS's S3-interop mode would need static HMAC keys. Plans a P4b phase, and
opens the question of whether a VTC hosting rooms must keep a runtime VTA
link.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(vta): the VTA as key authority for cloud and third-party accounts; rooms storage uses it

A new design note, docs/05-design-notes/vta-external-accounts.md. It
generalises what vault/proxy-login and keys/sign-sshsig already do: use a key
or secret inside the VTA, build what is signed, and return only something
short-lived.

An external account is an authority the VTA holds, with drivers per auth model.
The models are ranked by what has to be trusted. Pinned models come first,
because research showed a hosted OIDC issuer makes whoever can edit its JWKS
able to assume every federated role:
- AWS IAM Roles Anywhere, with the VTA as the CA and the trust anchor uploaded
  to AWS;
- GCP Workload Identity with an uploaded JWKS;
- presigned URLs for S3-compatible stores that cannot federate, so the access
  key never leaves the VTA;
- a Sui signer limited to allow-listed Walrus calls;
- OIDC discovery and Azure only where nothing pinned exists. Azure documents
  RS256 only, so the VTA also needs wrapped RSA keys.

How an account is used:
- the VTA performs the exchange itself, so downscoping (AWS session policies,
  GCS Credential Access Boundaries) is the VTA's enforcement and not the
  consumer's promise;
- issued credentials travel only inside sealed_transfer;
- management is a family of Trust Tasks, so the VTC console can drive it;
- changes are consented at the VTA by approvers signing with their own DIDs,
  so a compromised VTC can propose but never approve. Suspend and revoke stay
  fast and single-handed.

data-rooms-files.md now keeps no long-lived credential on the VTC:
- storage configs name a VTA account;
- blobs live under a per-room hashed prefix, and every credential is scoped to
  one room's prefix for at most 15 minutes;
- Walrus goes through an upload relay with VTA-signed transactions, never a
  publisher holding a hot wallet;
- ambient identity stays allowed, with the same self-downscoping;
- the VTC-held sealed credential stays as a discouraged fallback that says what
  it does not protect against.

Two corrections to the earlier draft:
- File keys no longer reach the web page. The wallet extension encrypts and
  decrypts in its own context and streams plaintext over a port. A file key
  never expires, and on Walrus the ciphertext is public forever, so a key
  leaked from a page would have been a permanent disclosure.
- The VTC-as-OIDC-issuer section is gone, superseded by the pinned models.

Also states that the file manifest sits inside the author's in-body signature,
so a decrypted file is attributable to the member who added exactly those
bytes.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(vta): external accounts need no public VTA endpoint; only oidc-discovery would

Adds a network-exposure section. Inbound, every task travels the VTA's
existing transports. The pinned models put verification material in the
provider's account, and the provider never calls back; a Roles Anywhere CRL
is pushed, not fetched. Only oidc-discovery needs a public JWKS, so a hidden
VTA uses the pinned model for the same cloud instead.

Outbound, brokered models need egress to the provider's token endpoints only,
named in each account's settings so an egress proxy can allow-list exactly
those. Presign and the Sui signer need no egress at all.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(vta): external accounts require no inbound surface on the VTA; drop OIDC discovery

A VTA using external accounts accepts no inbound connection from the internet:
no fixed IP, no public URL, no REST route. This is now stated as a requirement
in §3.1.

Every remaining model puts its verification material in the provider's account
(a CA certificate, an uploaded JWKS, a certificate, a registered key), and no
provider ever calls back. Tasks arrive over TSP or DIDComm on connections the
VTA dialled out. Brokered models need outbound HTTPS to their token endpoints
only.

OIDC discovery federation is removed rather than discouraged. It works only by
the provider fetching a public JWKS, which needs an inbound endpoint and makes
whoever hosts that file a trust root. Each cloud has a pinned alternative:
Roles Anywhere for AWS, an uploaded JWKS for GCP, and certificate credentials
for Azure. azure-cert moves out of "later", with its generated setup.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

title: chore(release): use the VTI-<Name> tag convention, adopt shipped releases
body:
Aspen to Eucalyptus were tagged `VTI-<Name>-RC-<n>` / `VTI-<Name>` / `VTI-<Name>-R<n>`. The release tooling from #1989 used its own scheme; this switches it to yours, so Eucalyptus's next patch is `VTI-Eucalyptus-R1`.

- `RELEASE` holds the branch's current tag; prep steps RC → RC, RC → GA, GA → R1 → R2.
- `publish.yml` checks the tag (not a GitHub Release) to decide "already tagged".
- `cut-release.py --released-as <tag>` adopts a release that already went GA, refusing a source commit whose workspace crates or root manifests differ from the tag (dry-run: `origin/main` carries VTI-Eucalyptus unchanged; `7d0c77e7` is refused, naming the files).
- `RELEASES.md` records the history; Dogwood gets no branch (reason in the doc).

After merge: `python3 scripts/cut-release.py eucalyptus --released-as VTI-Eucalyptus --from origin/main`.

## Backport
none
author: stormer78

title: chore(release): use the VTI-<Name> tag convention, adopt shipped releases (#1994)
body:
chore(release): use the VTI-<Name> tag convention, adopt shipped releases (#1994)

Releases Aspen to Eucalyptus were tagged VTI-<Name>-RC-<n>, VTI-<Name> and
VTI-<Name>-R<n> (VTI-Dogwood-R1). The release tooling invented its own
(eucalyptus.rc1, eucalyptus.0); it now follows the existing one, so the
history reads as one sequence: VTI-Eucalyptus is followed by
VTI-Eucalyptus-R1.

- RELEASE holds the branch's current tag; prepare-release-branch.py steps
  RC-<n> -> RC-<n+1>, RC-<n> -> GA, GA -> R1 -> R2.
- publish.yml decides "already tagged" from the tag, not a GitHub Release:
  the older tags mostly have none.
- cut-release.py --released-as <tag> gives a branch to a release that
  already went GA as a tag, refusing a source commit whose workspace crates
  or root manifests differ from it. That is how release/eucalyptus is made:
  nothing but CI and release tooling has changed on main since its GA.
- RELEASES.md records Aspen to Eucalyptus. Dogwood gets no branch: it would
  need the tooling ported onto its code to support it until Fig's GA.

A full set of compiled caches is ~13 GB with every Rust job in it, and each lockfile change (every Release PR) starts a new set while the old one ages out, so two sets must fit. MSRV and the enclave proxy now run on a PR only when their own inputs change, so their compiled trees would hold space for runs that seldom restore them. They keep registry-only caches (`compiled: "false"`, mapped to rust-cache's `cache-targets`) and keep mold.

## Backport

title: ci: cache compiled dependencies, link with mold, run less per PR
body:
## What and why

The last green main run took **77 min** end to end. Test (workspace) spent **19 of 22 min compiling**; every job compiled every third-party crate from scratch (nothing compiled was cached), and tier 2 waited for all of tier 1, so Test (VTC) (~36 min) and Mobile (~39–55 min) ran back to back.

| Change | Effect |
|---|---|
| Cache compiled third-party crates (`.github/actions/rust-cache` → Swatinem/rust-cache) | Each job stops recompiling ~400 crates at opt-level 2 |
| mold as linker (`-Clinker-features=-lld -Clink-arg=-fuse-ld=mold`, x86_64 Linux only) | Faster links of the large test binaries |
| Drop `Check` | `clippy --all-targets` already compiles all of it |
| Tier 2 needs Clippy only | Removes the longest test job from the critical path |
| vetting-pcs → its own job | ~17 min no longer serial inside Test (VTC) |
| Clippy gated `--any`, enclave proxy gated `--paths` | A docs-only PR compiles nothing |

**Why the cache is safe where #1133's wasn't:** rust-cache deletes every workspace member's artifacts before saving, and all 32 local crates are workspace members, so only content-addressed crates.io/git builds are restored. Keyed per job (no #891 cross-feature restores). Saved from `main` only — today 46 cache entries / 11.2 GB, mostly per-PR copies.

## Expect on this PR
This PR's own run restores **no** compiled cache (none is saved until it runs on main), so it shows the restructure and mold, not the cache. The first PR after merge shows the cache.

## Tested locally
- `ci-affects.sh --any` / `--paths` on scratch commits: docs-only → false/false; Rust change → true/false; enclave-proxy change → proxy true.
- actionlint clean; action pins check; `ci-feature-combo-pkgs.sh --list`.

## Needs a maintainer
- **Raise the Actions cache limit above 10 GB** if the plan allows (Settings → Actions → General → Cache). Compiled-dependency caches for ~14 jobs will exceed 10 GB, and eviction would make them miss.

## Backport
none

title: ci(release): named release branches, a green nightly, backports and branch rules
body:
## What and why

Named releases (Dogwood, Eucalyptus, Fig, …) cut every 4–6 weeks and patched on their own branches, with crate patches published from those branches. N and N-1 are supported; LTS is a maintainer decision per release. `RELEASES.md` is the policy and schedule; the README links it; `CLAUDE.md` tells agents where a PR goes.

**Branches**
- `main` — all development; the next release while it is being built. Crates keep publishing from it via release-plz.
- `nightly` — `nightly.yml` fast-forwards it daily to the newest main commit on which **every** CI job passed (read per job, not from the rollup). Cuts come from here, never from main's tip.
- `release/<name>` — cut by `scripts/cut-release.py`; takes backports only.

**Release branches publish their own crate patches**
- A cut records `releases/<name>.toml`: each crate's version line now belongs to that branch. `check-release-line-ownership.py` keeps main's Release PR out of it, so the branch always has a patch number to take. A crate unchanged since an earlier cut would share a line; the cut refuses, and `--claim` opens the PR on main that gives it a new one.
- release-plz's Release PR can't run on a release branch: it derives versions from the *newest* crate on crates.io (`Crate::new(name, None)` in its source), which is main's line. `prepare-release-branch.py` (run by the *Prepare a named release* workflow) does it: next patch per changed crate, `cargo semver-checks --release-type patch` (a breaking change is refused), changelog from `cliff.toml`. Its publish step checks the exact `name@version`, so `publish.yml` publishes from `release/**` unchanged, then tags `<name>.<n>` with a bill of materials, never "latest".

**Enforcement**
- `backport.yml` cherry-picks a merged PR labelled `backport release/<name>`; a conflict opens as a draft.
- `branch-rules.yml` (new, seconds, no build): a PR into `release/**` is a bot backport, a prep PR, or labelled `release-direct`; only the release tooling edits `version =`, `RELEASE` or `releases/`. Main had no check that a feature PR leaves versions alone; this is it.
- PR template asks the backport question.

No container or enclave images are published; operators build from the tag and generate their own PCR0.

## Tested locally
- Ownership guard: fails a proposed version in an owned line, passes on the owning branch.
- Cut: `--dry-run` against main (23 published crates, all on crates.io); shared-line detection against a scratch ref; `--claim` cascade on a scratch worktree (`vti-webauthn` 0.2.2→0.3.0, `vta-service` follows).
- Prep: compatible change → patch + changelog + `RELEASE` move; removed re-export → refused, tree untouched.
- Branch rules: 10 simulated PRs (version edits, backports to the right/wrong branch, `release-direct`).

**Not yet run on GitHub:** `nightly.yml`, `backport.yml`, `release-branch.yml`, the tag step in `publish.yml`. Dogwood's cut is their first real run.

## After merge (repository settings, a maintainer)
- Rulesets: `release/**` (require PR, CI + `branch rules`, no force-push/delete; bypass for the `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` identity); `nightly` (only that identity updates it); `main` (require PR + `branch rules`).
- `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN`: contents, pull-requests, actions:read.
- Run *Nightly* once by hand to create the branch.

## Backport
none

- claimDeadline, decisionDeadline and notAfter are integer epoch seconds,
  emitted and required; RFC 3339 is refused
- contextDigest compares z/u multibase multihashes only; hex is refused

  auth/oob/<task>:* per task, framework malformedRequest, which a claim

title: Refresh wiki for September–October 2026 ecosystem cycle
body:
The ecosystem tagged VTI-Eucalyptus on 2026-10-07, its fifth and by far largest coordinated release (eighteen repos, 203 breaking changes), and the same day the project was presented to kernel developers at the Linux Plumbers Conference. The wiki last reflected the 2026-09-18 state and no longer matched what the stack ships: every operation is now a signed, proof-bound Trust Task, the REST management surfaces are gone, DTG Credentials v1 is the only credential shape, vetting is live, and a second independent client (the Keyring phone wallet) has joined.

New pages:

- content/concepts/trust-tasks.md: the universal wire format, its ToIP registry and bindings, and how Eucalyptus made it the only door.
- content/concepts/kernel-web-of-trust.md: the PGP web-of-trust pain points, Linux ID, and what shipped for the maintainer pilot.
- content/concepts/community-git-namespaces.md: a VTC governing a GitHub/Forgejo namespace; rights model, vgi-bridge, VTA-held commit signing.
- content/entities/keyring-wallet.md, keyring-bifold.md: Harvard BKC's iOS/Android wallet and its Bifold fork as new Secondary sources.

Rewritten or substantially revised:

- coordinated-releases.md around the Eucalyptus release and its integrator-visible breaking changes.
- peer-identity-vetting.md for Vetting V0 and hidden vetting; the Vetting Statement is corrected to a `vetted/1` Statement Credential, not an `IdentityVetting` endorsement as last cycle's page said.
- Eighteen credential concept pages for DTG Credentials v1: the v1 JSON-LD context, registry predicates (`endorses/1`, `witnessed/1`), `issuerScope`, `taskDigestMultibase`, categories dropped, community roles as Authority Credentials.
- Entity activity logs for the VTI, OpenVTC, VGI (0.4.12 to 0.18.2), mediator, did-hosting, TDK, didwebvh-rs, the Farm repos, browser wallet and vti-setup.
- index.md, overview.md and log.md for the new cycle.

Also normalizes British spellings to American across content, including older log entries, per the wiki's spelling convention.

title: docs(assurance): assess shared RAHP testing baseline candidates
body:
## What changed

Progresses #17 with a bounded fit assessment before any transfer. Adds `docs/baseline-assessment/README.md`, `inventory.json` and `execution.json`: eight candidate groups, 46 SHA-256-identified source assets at immutable upstream/downstream revisions, upstream overlap, interfaces/dependencies/consumers, proposed dispositions, retained execution evidence and a smallest-next-contribution proposal.

The recommendation is to adapt a real-source replay to the existing upstream review contract. Maintainers should choose TRQP adaptation or the requested VRC 0.3 example. Downstream pressure-test vocabularies are not equivalent to the upstream review contract. Consolidation, ownership, independent review and merge rights remain explicit decisions. Pending CI #14 is distinguished from accepted main. No code transfer, schema/corpus change, workflow change or enforcement change is included.

## Artefact IDs affected

Assessment-local C1–C8. No canonical RAHP record IDs changed.

## Provenance — what triggered this change?

Issue #17 and the maintainer proposal on #9. Upstream source: ab191485b48bca805ea2cc962c2ea9476a65db66. Downstream source: af58247e83d0aff4d47650d929bfc6280d9e41d3. Prepared with AI assistance; recommendations are not task-force decisions or independent review.

## Validation output

```text
Upstream: 12 tests passed; corpus 0 errors / 32 warnings; minimal review and temporary build exit 0.
Downstream: 3 standalone TRQP tests, 4 engine-contract tests and 6 freshness tests passed; retained replay matched.
Inventory: 46 source digests verified; eight candidate groups and eight successful executions; local document links verified.
```

The initial environment lacked jsonschema. Review tests failed and corpus schema checks were skipped; requirements were installed and all recorded checks rerun. Full outputs, dependency versions and limitations are retained in execution.json. No complete downstream suite, unfamiliar-adopter trial, live authorization/revocation, independent review or deployed Pages verification is claimed.

## Decisions and residual gaps

Keep #17 open: candidate acceptance, first target, vocabulary/validator architecture, maintenance ownership and GAP-5.1 independent review remain pending. This assessment supplies its inventory/mapping/disposition/proposal deliverables without implementing unsettled decisions.

The contributor reviewed PR #18 and explicitly authorized DCO sign-off using the existing author identity. The amended head `fec5ed096354518486ec73cf4b4bc92d11bdad94` preserves the original file tree and has a passing DCO check. Independent review and maintainer acceptance remain required. No automatic merge is enabled.

## Checklist

- [x] `python3 tools/validate.py` exits 0 with dependencies present
- [x] Assessment provenance, source pins and execution evidence recorded
- [x] No generated `build/` file edited
- [x] Existing tests retained and passed
- [x] Actual contributor DCO certification
- [ ] Independent review and maintainer acceptance
